肺.eEn: The organ associated with Metal. Formed from 肉, with 巿 indicating the pronunciation.

脾.eEn: The organ associated with Earth. Formed from 肉, with 卑 indicating the pronunciation.

肝.eEn: The organ associated with Wood. Formed from 肉, with 干 indicating the pronunciation.

膽.eEn: The receptacle connected to the liver. Formed from 肉, with 詹 indicating the pronunciation.

祇.e: 地祇，提出萬物者也。从示氏聲。
祇.eEn: An earth deity, which brings forth all things. Formed from 示, with 氏 indicating the pronunciation.

葵.eEn: A vegetable. Formed from 艸, with 癸 indicating the pronunciation.

胃.eEn: The receptacle for grain. Formed from 肉; 纻 is a pictograph.

脬.eEn: The urinary bladder. Formed from 肉, with 孚 indicating the pronunciation.

腸.eEn: The large and small intestines. Formed from 肉, with 昜 indicating the pronunciation.

膏.eEn: Fat. Formed from 肉, with 高 indicating the pronunciation.

肪.eEn: Fat. Formed from 肉, with 方 indicating the pronunciation.

钋.eEn: The chest. Formed from 肉, with 𤸰 indicating the pronunciation.

肊.eEn: The breastbone. Formed from 肉, with 乙 indicating the pronunciation.

背.eEn: The backbone. Formed from 肉, with 北 indicating the pronunciation.

脅.eEn: The two sides of the torso. Formed from 肉, with 劦 indicating the pronunciation.

膀.eEn: The side of the torso. Formed from 肉, with 㫄 indicating the pronunciation.

脟.e: 脅肉也。从肉寽聲。一曰脟，腸閒𦘺也。一曰膫也。
脟.eEn: Flesh on the ribs. Formed from 肉, with 寽 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation says that 脟 is fat between the intestines. Another says it is 膫, intestinal fat.

肋.eEn: The bones of the side of the torso: the ribs. Formed from 肉, with 力 indicating the pronunciation.

胂.eEn: The flesh on either side of the backbone. Formed from 肉, with 申 indicating the pronunciation.

脢.e: 背肉也。从肉𣫭聲。《易》曰：“咸其脢。”
脢.eEn: Flesh on the back. Formed from 肉, with 𣫭 indicating the pronunciation. The Changes says: “Feeling in the flesh of his back.”

胳.eEn: The area beneath the armpit. Formed from 肉, with 各 indicating the pronunciation.

胠.eEn: The area beneath the armpit. Formed from 肉, with 去 indicating the pronunciation.

臂.eEn: The part above the hand: the arm. Formed from 肉, with 辟 indicating the pronunciation.

臑.e: 臂羊矢也。从肉需聲。讀若襦。
臑.eEn: The part of the arm called the “sheep's dropping.” Formed from 肉, with 需 indicating the pronunciation. Read like 襦.

肘.e: 臂節也。从肉从寸。寸，手寸口也。
肘.eEn: The joint of the arm: the elbow. Formed from 肉 and 寸. 寸 is the pulse site at the wrist.

蓼.eEn: A pungent vegetable, called 薔虞. Formed from 艸, with 翏 indicating the pronunciation.

腹.eEn: Thick. Formed from 肉, with 复 indicating the pronunciation.

腴.eEn: Fat beneath the belly. Formed from 肉, with 臾 indicating the pronunciation.

脽.eEn: The buttocks. Formed from 肉, with 隹 indicating the pronunciation.

胯.eEn: The thigh. Formed from 肉, with 夸 indicating the pronunciation.

股.eEn: The thigh. Formed from 肉, with 殳 indicating the pronunciation.

腳.eEn: The lower leg. Formed from 肉, with 卻 indicating the pronunciation.

脛.eEn: The lower leg. Formed from 肉, with 坙 indicating the pronunciation.

胻.eEn: The end of the lower leg. Formed from 肉, with 行 indicating the pronunciation.

腓.eEn: The calf of the lower leg. Formed from 肉, with 非 indicating the pronunciation.

腨.eEn: The calf muscle. Formed from 肉, with 耑 indicating the pronunciation.

胑.eEn: The body's four limbs. Formed from 肉, with 只 indicating the pronunciation.

胲.eEn: Hair on the big toe. Formed from 肉, with 亥 indicating the pronunciation.

肖.e: 骨肉相似也。从肉小聲。不似其先，故曰“不肖”也。
肖.eEn: Resemblance between blood relatives. Formed from 肉, with 小 indicating the pronunciation. Someone who does not resemble their forebears is therefore called 不肖, “unlike one's forebears; unworthy.”

胤.e: 子孫相承續也。从肉；从八，象其長也；从幺，象重累也。
胤.eEn: Descendants succeeding one another in an unbroken line. Formed from 肉; also from 八, depicting their growth, and 幺, depicting successive accumulation.

胄.eEn: Descendants. Formed from 肉, with 由 indicating the pronunciation.

膻.e: 肉膻也。从肉亶聲。《詩》曰：“膻裼暴虎。”
膻.eEn: The rank smell of meat. Formed from 肉, with 亶 indicating the pronunciation. The Odes says: “With his upper body bared, he fights a tiger barehanded.”

臞.eEn: Having little flesh; lean. Formed from 肉, with 瞿 indicating the pronunciation.

脫.eEn: To lose flesh and become lean. Formed from 肉, with 兌 indicating the pronunciation.

脙.e: 齊人謂臞脙也。从肉求聲。讀若休止。
脙.eEn: People of Qi call leanness 脙. Formed from 肉, with 求 indicating the pronunciation. Read like 休 in 休止, “to stop.”

膌.eEn: Thin. Formed from 肉, with 𦟝 indicating the pronunciation.

胗.eEn: A sore on the lips. Formed from 肉, with 㐱 indicating the pronunciation.

腄.eEn: A scar or callus. Formed from 肉, with 垂 indicating the pronunciation.

胝.eEn: A callus. Formed from 肉, with 氐 indicating the pronunciation.

薇.eEn: A vegetable resembling bean leaves. Formed from 艸, with 微 indicating the pronunciation.

肬.eEn: An outgrowth of flesh; a wart. Formed from 肉, with 尤 indicating the pronunciation.

肒.eEn: A sore caused by scratching. Formed from 肉, with 丸 indicating the pronunciation.

腫.eEn: An abscess. Formed from 肉, with 重 indicating the pronunciation.

胅.e: 骨差也。从肉失聲。讀與跌同。
胅.eEn: A bone out of alignment. Formed from 肉, with 失 indicating the pronunciation. Pronounced the same as 跌.

脪.eEn: Flesh protruding outward from a wound. Formed from 肉, with 希 indicating the pronunciation.

臘.e: 冬至後三戌，臘祭百神。从肉巤聲。
臘.eEn: On the third xu day after the winter solstice, the la sacrifice is offered to the hundred spirits. Formed from 肉, with 巤 indicating the pronunciation.

膢.e: 楚俗以二月祭飲食也。从肉婁聲。一曰祈穀食新曰離膢。
膢.eEn: A Chu custom of making offerings of food and drink in the second month. Formed from 肉, with 婁 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation says that praying for grain and eating the new harvest is called 離膢.

朓.eEn: A sacrifice. Formed from 肉, with 兆 indicating the pronunciation.

胙.eEn: Sacrificial meat conveying blessings. Formed from 肉, with 乍 indicating the pronunciation.

蓶.eEn: A vegetable. Formed from 艸, with 唯 indicating the pronunciation.

隋.eEn: To split meat apart. Formed from 肉 and an abbreviated form of 隓.

膳.eEn: To prepare food. Formed from 肉, with 善 indicating the pronunciation.

腬.eEn: Fine, good meat. Formed from 肉, with 柔 indicating the pronunciation.

肴.eEn: To eat. Formed from 肉, with 爻 indicating the pronunciation.

腆.e: 設膳腆腆多也。从肉典聲。
腆.eEn: To set out food in abundance; 腆腆 means plentiful. Formed from 肉, with 典 indicating the pronunciation.

腯.e: 牛羊曰𦘺，豕曰腯。从肉盾聲。
腯.eEn: Fatness in cattle and sheep is called 𦘺; in pigs it is called 腯. Formed from 肉, with 盾 indicating the pronunciation.

胡.eEn: The hanging flesh beneath an ox's chin. Formed from 肉, with 古 indicating the pronunciation.

胘.eEn: An ox's “hundred-leaved” stomach. Formed from 肉, with an abbreviated form of 弦 indicating the pronunciation.

膍.e: 牛百葉也。从肉𣬉聲。一曰鳥膍胵。
膍.eEn: An ox's “hundred-leaved” stomach. Formed from 肉, with 𣬉 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation says it is a bird's gizzard.

菦.e: 菜，類蒿。从艸近聲。《周禮》有“菦菹”。
菦.eEn: A vegetable resembling mugwort. Formed from 艸, with 近 indicating the pronunciation. The Rites of Zhou mentions “pickled 菦.”

胵.e: 鳥胃也。从肉至聲。一曰胵，五藏緫名也。
胵.eEn: A bird's stomach. Formed from 肉, with 至 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation says that 胵 is a collective name for the five internal organs.

膘.e: 牛脅後髀前合革肉也。从肉𤐫聲。讀若繇。
膘.eEn: The flesh adjoining the hide behind an ox's ribs and in front of its thigh. Formed from 肉, with 𤐫 indicating the pronunciation. Read like 繇.

膫.e: 牛腸脂也。从肉尞聲。《詩》曰：“取其血膫。”
膫.eEn: Fat from an ox's intestines. Formed from 肉, with 尞 indicating the pronunciation. The Odes says: “Take its blood and intestinal fat.”

脯.eEn: Dried meat. Formed from 肉, with 甫 indicating the pronunciation.

脩.eEn: Dried meat. Formed from 肉, with 攸 indicating the pronunciation.

膎.eEn: Dried meat. Formed from 肉, with 奚 indicating the pronunciation.

脼.eEn: Dried meat. Formed from 肉, with 兩 indicating the pronunciation.

膊.e: 薄脯，膊之屋上。从肉尃聲。
膊.eEn: Thin slices of dried meat, spread out on a roof. Formed from 肉, with 尃 indicating the pronunciation.

脘.e: 胃府也。从肉完聲。讀若患。舊云脯。
脘.eEn: The stomach receptacle. Formed from 肉, with 完 indicating the pronunciation. Read like 患. An older explanation says “dried meat.”

朐.eEn: A strip of dried meat. Formed from 肉, with 句 indicating the pronunciation.

膴.e: 無骨腊也。楊雄說：鳥腊也。从肉無聲。《周禮》有膴判。讀若謨。
膴.eEn: Boneless dried meat. Yang Xiong explains it as dried bird meat. Formed from 肉, with 無 indicating the pronunciation. The Rites of Zhou mentions 膴判, “pieces of 膴.” Read like 謨.

胥.eEn: Crab paste. Formed from 肉, with 疋 indicating the pronunciation.

腒.e: 北方謂鳥腊曰腒。从肉居聲。傳曰：堯如腊，舜如腒。
腒.eEn: In the north, dried bird meat is called 腒. Formed from 肉, with 居 indicating the pronunciation. A transmitted account says: “Yao was like dried meat; Shun was like dried bird meat.”

肍.e: 孰肉醬也。从肉九聲。讀若舊。
肍.eEn: A paste made from cooked meat. Formed from 肉, with 九 indicating the pronunciation. Read like 舊.

腝.eEn: Meat paste containing bones. Formed from 肉, with 耎 indicating the pronunciation.

脠.eEn: A paste made from raw meat. Formed from 肉, with 延 indicating the pronunciation.

胹.eEn: Cooked until soft. Formed from 肉, with 而 indicating the pronunciation.

莧.eEn: The vegetable amaranth. Formed from 艸, with 見 indicating the pronunciation.

胜.e: 犬膏臭也。从肉生聲。一曰不孰也。
胜.eEn: The smell of dog fat. Formed from 肉, with 生 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation says “uncooked.”

臊.eEn: The smell of pig fat. Formed from 肉, with 喿 indicating the pronunciation.

膮.eEn: Pork broth. Formed from 肉, with 堯 indicating the pronunciation.

腥.e: 星見食豕，令肉中生小息肉也。从肉从星，星亦聲。
腥.eEn: Feeding pigs when the stars appear causes small fleshy growths to develop in their meat. Formed from 肉 and 星, with 星 also indicating the pronunciation.

脂.e: 戴角者脂，無角者膏。从肉旨聲。
脂.eEn: Fat from horned animals is called 脂; fat from animals without horns is called 膏. Formed from 肉, with 旨 indicating the pronunciation.

膩.eEn: Fat on the upper part. Formed from 肉, with 貳 indicating the pronunciation.

膜.eEn: The membranes between the flesh. Formed from 肉, with 莫 indicating the pronunciation.

祕.eEn: Divine. Formed from 示, with 必 indicating the pronunciation.

芋.e: 大葉實根，駭人，故謂之芌也。从艸亏聲。
芋.eEn: It has large leaves and a substantial root that startles people; hence it is called 芌. Formed from 艸, with 亏 indicating the pronunciation.

膹.eEn: Meat broth. Formed from 肉, with 賁 indicating the pronunciation.

臇.eEn: Meat broth. Formed from 肉, with 雋 indicating the pronunciation. Read like 纂.

胾.eEn: A large piece of meat. Formed from 肉, with 𢦔 indicating the pronunciation.

膾.eEn: Finely sliced meat. Formed from 肉, with 會 indicating the pronunciation.

腌.eEn: Meat steeped in liquid. Formed from 肉, with 奄 indicating the pronunciation.

脃.e: 小耎易斷也。从肉，从絕省。
脃.eEn: Slight, soft, and easily broken. Formed from 肉 and an abbreviated form of 絕.

膬.eEn: Soft and easily broken apart. Formed from 肉, with 毳 indicating the pronunciation.

莒.eEn: What the people of Qi call 芌, taro. Formed from 艸, with 呂 indicating the pronunciation.

膞.eEn: To cut meat. Formed from 肉, with 專 indicating the pronunciation.

腏.e: 挑取骨閒肉也。从肉叕聲。讀若《詩》曰“啜其泣矣”。
腏.eEn: To pick out meat from between bones. Formed from 肉, with 叕 indicating the pronunciation. Pronounced like 啜 in the quotation from the Book of Odes: “She sobs and weeps.”

肰.eEn: Dog meat. Formed from 犬 and 肉. Pronounced like 然.

膠.e: 昵也。作之以皮。从肉翏聲。
膠.eEn: To adhere closely. It is made from hides. Formed from 肉, with 翏 indicating the pronunciation.

蘧.eEn: The plant 蘧麥. Formed from 艸, with 遽 indicating the pronunciation.

肙.e: 小蟲也。从肉囗聲。一曰空也。
肙.eEn: A small crawling creature. Formed from 肉, with 囗 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation is “empty.”

腐.eEn: Rotten. Formed from 肉, with 府 indicating the pronunciation.

肎.e: 骨閒肉肎肎箸也。从肉，从冎省。一曰骨無肉也。
肎.eEn: Meat clinging to the spaces between bones. Formed from 肉 and an abbreviated form of 冎. Another explanation is “a bone without meat.”

肥.eEn: Having much flesh; fat. Formed from 肉 and 卪.

脧.e: 赤子陰也。从肉夋聲。或从血。
脧.eEn: An infant boy’s genitals. Formed from 肉, with 夋 indicating the pronunciation. An alternative form uses 血.

腔.e: 内空也。从肉从空，空亦聲。
腔.eEn: Hollow inside. Formed from 肉 and 空; 空 also indicates the pronunciation.

筋.e: 肉之力也。从力从肉从竹。竹，物之多筋者。凡筋之屬皆从筋。
筋.eEn: The strength of the flesh; sinews. Formed from 力, 肉, and 竹. Bamboo is a thing with many sinews. All characters in the 筋 class are formed with 筋.

菊.eEn: The large 菊: the plant 蘧麥. Formed from 艸, with 匊 indicating the pronunciation.

刀.e: 兵也。象形。凡刀之屬皆从刀。
刀.eEn: A weapon. A pictograph. All characters in the 刀 class are formed with 刀.

削.e: 鞞也。一曰析也。从刀肖聲。
削.eEn: A scabbard. Another explanation is “to split.” Formed from 刀, with 肖 indicating the pronunciation.

剴.e: 大鎌也。一曰摩也。从刀豈聲。
剴.eEn: A large sickle. Another explanation is “to rub.” Formed from 刀, with 豈 indicating the pronunciation.

剞.eEn: 剞𠜾: a curved knife. Formed from 刀, with 奇 indicating the pronunciation.

葷.eEn: Strong-smelling vegetables. Formed from 艸, with 軍 indicating the pronunciation.

利.e: 銛也。从刀。和然後利，从和省。《易》曰：“利者，義之和也。”
利.eEn: Sharp. Formed from 刀. Only after harmony is established is there benefit; it therefore also contains an abbreviated form of 和. The Book of Changes says: “Benefit is the harmony of righteousness.”

剡.eEn: Sharp and keen. Formed from 刀, with 炎 indicating the pronunciation.

初.e: 始也。从刀从衣。裁衣之始也。
初.eEn: The beginning. Formed from 刀 and 衣, representing the beginning of making a garment by cutting its cloth.

剪.eEn: To cut off evenly. Formed from 刀, with 歬 indicating the pronunciation.

則.e: 等畫物也。从刀从貝。貝，古之物貨也。
則.eEn: To grade and demarcate things. Formed from 刀 and 貝. Cowrie shells were used as currency in antiquity.

剛.eEn: Firm and decisive. Formed from 刀, with 岡 indicating the pronunciation.

剬.eEn: To cut evenly. Formed from 刀, with 耑 indicating the pronunciation.

劊.eEn: To sever. Formed from 刀, with 會 indicating the pronunciation.

切.eEn: To cut. Formed from 刀, with 七 indicating the pronunciation.

刌.eEn: To cut. Formed from 刀, with 寸 indicating the pronunciation.

蘘.e: 蘘荷也。一名葍蒩。从艸襄聲。
蘘.eEn: The plant 蘘荷, also called 葍蒩. Formed from 艸, with 襄 indicating the pronunciation.

刉.e: 劃傷也。从刀气聲。一曰斷也。又讀若㱯。一曰刀不利，於瓦石上刏之。
刉.eEn: To wound by slashing. Formed from 刀, with 气 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation is “to sever.” It is also pronounced like 㱯. A further explanation is to sharpen a blunt knife on tiles or stones.

劌.eEn: To wound with a sharp edge. Formed from 刀, with 歲 indicating the pronunciation.

刻.eEn: To engrave. Formed from 刀, with 亥 indicating the pronunciation.

副.e: 判也。从刀畐聲。《周禮》曰：“副辜祭。”
副.eEn: To split apart. Formed from 刀, with 畐 indicating the pronunciation. The Rites of Zhou says: “Split apart the sacrificial victim and offer it in sacrifice.”

剖.eEn: To split apart. Formed from 刀, with 咅 indicating the pronunciation.

辧.eEn: To divide. Formed from 刀, with 辡 indicating the pronunciation.

判.eEn: To divide. Formed from 刀, with 半 indicating the pronunciation.

剫.eEn: To split apart. Formed from 刀, with 度 indicating the pronunciation.

刳.eEn: To split apart. Formed from 刀, with 夸 indicating the pronunciation.

菁.eEn: The flowers of the Chinese chive. Formed from 艸, with 青 indicating the pronunciation.

列.eEn: To divide and separate. Formed from 刀, with 𡿪 indicating the pronunciation.

刊.eEn: To cut away. Formed from 刀, with 干 indicating the pronunciation.

剟.eEn: To cut away. Formed from 刀, with 叕 indicating the pronunciation.

刪.eEn: To cut away. Formed from 刀 and 冊. 冊 means a written document.

劈.eEn: To break apart. Formed from 刀, with 辟 indicating the pronunciation.

剝.e: 裂也。从刀从录。录，刻割也。录亦聲。
剝.eEn: To split or tear apart. Formed from 刀 and 录. 录 means to carve or cut. 录 also indicates the pronunciation.

割.eEn: To strip away. Formed from 刀, with 害 indicating the pronunciation.

剺.eEn: To strip away; to slash. Formed from 刀, with 𠩺 indicating the pronunciation.

劃.e: 錐刀曰劃。从刀从畫，畫亦聲。
劃.eEn: To work with an awl or knife is called 劃. Formed from 刀 and 畫; 畫 also indicates the pronunciation.

剈.e: 挑取也。从刀肙聲。一曰窐也。
剈.eEn: To pick out. Formed from 刀, with 肙 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation is “a hollow.”

蘆.e: 蘆菔也。一曰薺根。从艸盧聲。
蘆.eEn: 蘆菔, the radish. Another explanation is “the root of shepherd’s purse.” Formed from 艸, with 盧 indicating the pronunciation.

劀.e: 刮去惡創肉也。从刀矞聲。《周禮》曰：“劀殺之齊。”
劀.eEn: To scrape away diseased flesh from a sore. Formed from 刀, with 矞 indicating the pronunciation. The Rites of Zhou says: “Preparations for scraping away and destroying diseased tissue.”

劑.eEn: To make even. Formed from 刀 and 齊; 齊 also indicates the pronunciation.

刷.e: 刮也。从刀，㕞省聲。《禮》：“布刷巾。”
刷.eEn: To scrape. Formed from 刀, with an abbreviated form of 㕞 indicating the pronunciation. The Rites says: “A cloth wiping towel.”

刮.eEn: To scrape up and gather in the hand. Formed from 刀, with 𠯑 indicating the pronunciation.

剽.e: 砭刺也。从刀𤐫聲。一曰剽，劫人也。
剽.eEn: To pierce with a stone needle. Formed from 刀, with 𤐫 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation is that 剽 means to rob someone.

刲.e: 刺也。从刀圭聲。《易》曰：“士刲羊。”
刲.eEn: To stab. Formed from 刀, with 圭 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Changes says: “The man stabs a sheep.”

剉.eEn: To injure by breaking. Formed from 刀, with 坐 indicating the pronunciation.

劋.e: 絕也。从刀喿聲。《周書》曰：“天用劋絕其命。”
劋.eEn: To cut off completely. Formed from 刀, with 喿 indicating the pronunciation. The Documents of Zhou says: “Heaven thereby cut off their mandate completely.”

刖.eEn: To cut off. Formed from 刀, with 月 indicating the pronunciation.

刜.eEn: To strike. Formed from 刀, with 弗 indicating the pronunciation.

菔.e: 蘆菔。似蕪菁，實如小尗者。从艸服聲。
菔.eEn: 蘆菔, the radish. It resembles the turnip, and its seeds resemble small beans. Formed from 艸, with 服 indicating the pronunciation.

劖.e: 斷也。从刀毚聲。一曰剽也，釗也。
劖.eEn: To sever. Formed from 刀, with 毚 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation is “to pierce” or “to carve away.”

刓.e: 剸也。从刀元聲。一曰齊也。
刓.eEn: To cut. Formed from 刀, with 元 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation is “to make even.”

釗.e: 刓也。从刀从金。周康王名。
釗.eEn: To cut or carve away. Formed from 刀 and 金. The personal name of King Kang of Zhou.

制.e: 裁也。从刀从未。未，物成有滋味，可裁斷。一曰止也。
制.eEn: To cut to shape. Formed from 刀 and 未. 未 represents something that has matured and acquired flavor, and can be cut apart. Another explanation is “to stop.”

刵.eEn: To cut off an ear. Formed from 刀 and 耳.

刑.eEn: To cut the neck. Formed from 刀, with 幵 indicating the pronunciation.

苹.e: 蓱也。無根，浮水而生者。从艸平聲。
苹.eEn: Duckweed: a plant without roots that grows floating on water. Formed from 艸, with 平 indicating the pronunciation.

剄.eEn: To cut the neck. Formed from 刀, with 坙 indicating the pronunciation.

魝.e: 楚人謂治魚也。从刀从魚。讀若鍥。
魝.eEn: What the people of Chu call preparing fish. Formed from 刀 and 魚. Pronounced like 鍥.

券.e: 契也。从刀𢍏聲。券別之書，以刀判契其旁，故曰契券。
券.eEn: A tally or contract. Formed from 刀, with 𢍏 indicating the pronunciation. A document divided into matching portions has notches cut into its side with a knife; hence it is called 契券, a notched contract.

刺.e: 君殺大夫曰刺。刺，直傷也。从刀从朿，朿亦聲。
刺.eEn: When a ruler kills a high officer, it is called 刺. 刺 means to wound directly. Formed from 刀 and 朿; 朿 also indicates the pronunciation.

剔.eEn: To separate flesh from bones. Formed from 刀, with 易 indicating the pronunciation.

刎.eEn: To cut the neck. Formed from 刀, with 勿 indicating the pronunciation.

剜.eEn: To pare away. Formed from 刀, with 宛 indicating the pronunciation.

劇.eEn: Especially severe or extreme. Formed from 刀, though its role is not yet understood, with 豦 indicating the pronunciation.

刹.eEn: A pillar. Formed from 刀, though its role is not yet understood, with an abbreviated form of 殺 indicating the pronunciation.

齋.eEn: To observe ritual restraint and purification. Formed from 示, with an abbreviated form of 齊 indicating the pronunciation.

茞.eEn: A kind of plant. Formed from 艸, with 臣 indicating the pronunciation.

刃.e: 刀堅也。象刀有刃之形。凡刃之屬皆从刃。
刃.eEn: The hard part of a knife. It depicts the shape of a knife with an edge. All characters in the 刃 class are formed with 刃.

刅.eEn: To wound. Formed from 刃 and 一.

劒.eEn: A weapon worn on the person. Formed from 刃, with 僉 indicating the pronunciation.

栔.eEn: To carve. Formed from 㓞 and 木.

丯.e: 艸蔡也。象艸生之𢿱亂也。凡丯之屬皆从丯。讀若介。
丯.eEn: Tangled grass. It depicts grass growing in disorder. All characters in the 丯 class are formed with 丯. Pronounced like 介.

耒.e: 手耕曲木也。从木推丯。古者垂作耒㭒以振民也。凡耒之屬皆从耒。
耒.eEn: A curved wooden implement for plowing by hand. Formed from 木 pushing 丯. In antiquity, Chui made the 耒 and 㭒 plowing implements to aid the people. All characters in the 耒 class are formed with 耒.

耕.e: 犂也。从耒井聲。一曰古者井田。
耕.eEn: To plow. Formed from 耒, with 井 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation connects it with the well-field system of antiquity.

薲.eEn: Large duckweed. Formed from 艸, with 賓 indicating the pronunciation.

耦.e: 耒廣五寸爲伐，二伐爲耦。从耒禺聲。
耦.eEn: A plowing implement five inches wide constitutes one 伐; two 伐 constitute one 耦. Formed from 耒, with 禺 indicating the pronunciation.

耤.e: 帝耤千畝也。古者使民如借，故謂之耤。从耒昔聲。
耤.eEn: The emperor’s plowing of the thousand-mu field. In antiquity, employing the people was like borrowing their labor; hence it was called 耤. Formed from 耒, with 昔 indicating the pronunciation.

耡.e: 商人七十而耡。耡，耤稅也。从耒助聲。《周禮》曰：“以興耡利萌。”
耡.eEn: The people of Shang allotted seventy mu and practiced communal cultivation. 耡 is a tax paid through labor on borrowed fields. Formed from 耒, with 助 indicating the pronunciation. The Rites of Zhou says: “Thereby to promote communal cultivation and benefit the people.”

角.e: 獸角也。象形，角與刀、魚相似。凡角之屬皆从角。
角.eEn: An animal’s horn. A pictograph; the shape of a horn resembles those of a knife and a fish. All characters in the 角 class are formed with 角.

觻.e: 角也。从角樂聲。張掖有觻得縣。
觻.eEn: A horn. Formed from 角, with 樂 indicating the pronunciation. There is a county called 觻得 in Zhangye.

觠.eEn: A curved horn. Formed from 角, with 𢍏 indicating the pronunciation.

藍.eEn: A plant used to dye things blue. Formed from 艸, with 監 indicating the pronunciation.

觬.e: 角觬曲也。从角兒聲。西河有觬氏縣。
觬.eEn: A horn curved in shape. Formed from 角, with 兒 indicating the pronunciation. There is a county called 觬氏 in Xihe.

觢.e: 一角仰也。从角㓞聲。《易》曰：“其牛觢。”
觢.eEn: One horn pointing upward. Formed from 角, with 㓞 indicating the pronunciation. The Changes says: “Its ox has a horn pointing upward.”

觭.e: 角一俛一仰也。从角奇聲。
觭.eEn: One horn pointing downward and the other upward. Formed from 角, with 奇 indicating the pronunciation.

觓.e: 角皃。从角丩聲。《詩》曰：“兕觵其觓。”
觓.eEn: The appearance of horns. Formed from 角, with 丩 indicating the pronunciation. The Odes says: “The wild-ox horn cup has its curving horn.”

觸.eEn: To butt against. Formed from 角, with 蜀 indicating the pronunciation.

觲.e: 用角低仰便也。从羊、牛、角。《詩》曰：“觲觲角弓。”
觲.eEn: To move the horns downward and upward with ease. Formed from 羊, 牛, and 角. The Odes says: “The horn bow bends readily.”

藼.e: 令人忘憂艸也。从艸憲聲。《詩》曰：“安得藼艸？”
藼.eEn: A plant that makes people forget their sorrows. Formed from 艸, with 憲 indicating the pronunciation. The Odes says: “Where can I obtain the sorrow-forgetting plant?”

觷.eEn: To work horn. Formed from 角, with an abbreviated form of 學 indicating the pronunciation.

衡.e: 牛觸，橫大木其角。从角从大，行聲。《詩》曰：“設其楅衡。”
衡.eEn: When an ox butts, a large piece of wood is placed crosswise across its horns. Formed from 角 and 大, with 行 indicating the pronunciation. The Odes says: “Fit it with the horn-restraint and crossbar.”

觰.e: 觰拏，獸也。从角者聲。一曰下大者也。
觰.eEn: 觰拏, a beast. Formed from 角, with 者 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation: something large at the bottom.

觤.eEn: A sheep's horns being unequal. Formed from 角, with 危 indicating the pronunciation.

觟.e: 牝牂羊生角者也。从角圭聲。
觟.eEn: A female sheep that grows horns. Formed from 角, with 圭 indicating the pronunciation.

觡.eEn: A name for bony horns. Formed from 角, with 各 indicating the pronunciation.

觜.e: 鴟舊頭上角觜也。一曰觜觿也。从角此聲。
觜.eEn: The hornlike projections on the head of the 鴟舊 owl. Another explanation: 觜觿, a name for a constellation. Formed from 角, with 此 indicating the pronunciation.

解.e: 判也。从刀判牛角。一曰解𢊁，獸也。
解.eEn: To divide. Formed from 刀 dividing an ox's horn. Another explanation: 解𢊁, a beast.

觿.e: 佩角，銳耑可以解結。从角巂聲。《詩》曰：“童子佩觿。”
觿.eEn: A horn implement worn at the waist, with a pointed end that can undo knots. Formed from 角, with 巂 indicating the pronunciation. The Odes says: “The boy wears a knot-opener.”

觵.e: 兕牛角可以飲者也。从角黃聲。其狀觵觵，故謂之觵。
觵.eEn: A wild ox's horn that can be used for drinking. Formed from 角, with 黃 indicating the pronunciation. Its shape is broad and spreading, described as 觵觵; hence it is called 觵.

觶.e: 鄉飲酒角也。《禮》曰：“一人洗，舉觶。”觶受四升。从角單聲。
觶.eEn: A horn drinking vessel used at the communal drinking ceremony. The Rites says: “One person washes it and raises the 觶.” A 觶 holds four sheng. Formed from 角, with 單 indicating the pronunciation.

觛.eEn: A small 觶 drinking vessel. Formed from 角, with 旦 indicating the pronunciation.

觴.e: 觶實曰觴，虚曰觶。从角，𥏻省聲。
觴.eEn: A 觶 drinking vessel is called 觴 when full and 觶 when empty. Formed from 角, with an abbreviated form of 𥏻 indicating the pronunciation.

觚.e: 鄉飮酒之爵也。一曰觴受三升者謂之觚。从角瓜聲。
觚.eEn: A wine cup used at the communal drinking ceremony. Another explanation: a drinking vessel holding three sheng is called 觚. Formed from 角, with 瓜 indicating the pronunciation.

觼.eEn: A ring fitted with a tongue. Formed from 角, with 敻 indicating the pronunciation.

藭.eEn: The plant 𦵡藭. Formed from 艸, with 窮 indicating the pronunciation.

觳.e: 盛觵卮也。一曰射具。从角㱿聲。讀若斛。
觳.eEn: A vessel for holding horn cups and goblets. Another explanation: an archery implement. Formed from 角, with 㱿 indicating the pronunciation. Pronounced like 斛.

竹.e: 冬生艸也。象形。下垂者，箁箬也。凡竹之屬皆从竹。
竹.eEn: A plant that grows in winter. A pictograph; the hanging portions are the leaf buds and sheaths. All characters in the 竹 class are formed with 竹.

箭.eEn: An arrow. Formed from 竹, with 前 indicating the pronunciation.

箘.e: 箘簬也。从竹囷聲。一曰博棊也。
箘.eEn: The bamboo called 箘簬. Formed from 竹, with 囷 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation: a piece used in the game of bo.

簬.e: 箘簬也。从竹路聲。《夏書》曰：“惟箘簬楛。”
簬.eEn: The bamboo called 箘簬. Formed from 竹, with 路 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Xia says: “The 箘簬 bamboo and the 楛 shrub.”

筱.eEn: A kind of arrow bamboo; a small bamboo. Formed from 竹, with 攸 indicating the pronunciation.

簜.e: 大竹也。从竹湯聲。《夏書》曰：“瑤琨筱簜。”簜可爲幹，筱可爲矢。
簜.eEn: A large bamboo. Formed from 竹, with 湯 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Xia says: “Jade, fine jade, small bamboo, and large bamboo.” Large bamboo can be used for shafts, and small bamboo for arrows.

蘭.eEn: A fragrant plant. Formed from 艸, with 闌 indicating the pronunciation.

筍.eEn: A bamboo embryo: a bamboo shoot. Formed from 竹, with 旬 indicating the pronunciation.

箁.eEn: A bamboo leaf-sheath. Formed from 竹, with 咅 indicating the pronunciation.

箬.e: 楚謂竹皮曰箬。从竹若聲。
箬.eEn: In Chu, bamboo skin is called 箬. Formed from 竹, with 若 indicating the pronunciation.

節.eEn: A bamboo joint. Formed from 竹, with 即 indicating the pronunciation.

筡.e: 折竹笢也。从竹余聲。讀若絮。
筡.eEn: Bamboo skin split off from bamboo. Formed from 竹, with 余 indicating the pronunciation. Pronounced like 絮.

笢.eEn: Bamboo skin. Formed from 竹, with 民 indicating the pronunciation.

笨.eEn: The inner part of bamboo. Formed from 竹, with 本 indicating the pronunciation.

葌.eEn: A plant that grows on Mount Wulin. Formed from 艸, with 姦 indicating the pronunciation.

篸.eEn: Uneven or unequal. Formed from 竹, with 𠻝 indicating the pronunciation.

篆.eEn: Writing with drawn-out strokes. Formed from 竹, with 彖 indicating the pronunciation.

籒.e: 讀書也。从竹㩅聲。《春秋傳》曰“卜籒”云。
籒.eEn: To read a written text. Formed from 竹, with 㩅 indicating the pronunciation. The Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals has the expression “divining and reading.”

篇.e: 書也。一曰關西謂榜曰篇。从竹扁聲。
篇.eEn: A written text. Another explanation: west of the passes, a writing board is called 篇. Formed from 竹, with 扁 indicating the pronunciation.

籍.eEn: Registers and written records. Formed from 竹, with 𦔡 indicating the pronunciation.

篁.eEn: A bamboo field. Formed from 竹, with 皇 indicating the pronunciation.

籥.eEn: A bamboo writing tablet used by a young student. Formed from 竹, with 龠 indicating the pronunciation.

葰.e: 䕬屬。可以香口。从艸俊聲。
葰.eEn: A kind of ginger. It can be used to perfume the mouth. Formed from 艸, with 俊 indicating the pronunciation.

簡.eEn: A writing tablet. Formed from 竹, with 閒 indicating the pronunciation.

笐.eEn: Bamboo arranged in rows. Formed from 竹, with 亢 indicating the pronunciation.

篰.eEn: The object called 㒼爰. Formed from 竹, with 部 indicating the pronunciation.

等.e: 齊簡也。从竹从寺。寺，官曹之等平也。
等.eEn: To make bamboo slips even. Formed from 竹 and 寺. 寺 refers to the ordering and equalizing of ranks in government offices.

笵.e: 法也。从竹，竹，𥳑書也；氾聲。古法有竹刑。
笵.eEn: A rule or standard. Formed from 竹, representing written bamboo slips, with 氾 indicating the pronunciation. Ancient laws included penal statutes written on bamboo.

箋.eEn: Writing used to mark or identify something. Formed from 竹, with 戔 indicating the pronunciation.

符.e: 信也。漢制以竹，長六寸，分而相合。从竹付聲。
符.eEn: A token of authentication. Under the Han system, it is made of bamboo, six cun long, and divided into parts that fit together. Formed from 竹, with 付 indicating the pronunciation.

筮.e: 《易》卦用蓍也。从竹从𢍮。𢍮，古文巫字。
筮.eEn: To use milfoil stalks for the hexagrams of the Changes. Formed from 竹 and 𢍮. 𢍮 is the ancient-script form of 巫, “shaman.”

笄.eEn: A hairpin. Formed from 竹, with 幵 indicating the pronunciation.

芄.e: 芄蘭，莞也。从艸丸聲。《詩》曰：“芄蘭之枝。”
芄.eEn: 芄蘭, the plant called 莞. Formed from 艸, with 丸 indicating the pronunciation. The Odes says: “The branches of the 芄蘭 plant.”

籆.eEn: An implement for gathering silk thread. Formed from 竹, with 蒦 indicating the pronunciation.

筳.eEn: A tube used in winding silk thread. Formed from 竹, with 廷 indicating the pronunciation.

筦.eEn: A silk-winding tube, called 筟. Formed from 竹, with 完 indicating the pronunciation.

筟.e: 筳也。从竹孚聲。讀若《春秋》魯公子彄。
筟.eEn: A silk-winding tube, called 筳. Formed from 竹, with 孚 indicating the pronunciation. Pronounced like the name of Prince 彄 of Lu in the Spring and Autumn Annals.

笮.e: 迫也。在瓦之下，棼上。从竹乍聲。
笮.eEn: To press tightly. It lies beneath the roof tiles and above the roof timbers. Formed from 竹, with 乍 indicating the pronunciation.

簾.eEn: A hall curtain. Formed from 竹, with 廉 indicating the pronunciation.

簀.eEn: The slatted support of a bed. Formed from 竹, with 責 indicating the pronunciation.

笫.eEn: The slatted support of a bed. Formed from 竹, with 𠂔 indicating the pronunciation.

筵.e: 竹席也。从竹延聲。《周禮》曰：“度堂以筵。”筵一丈。
筵.eEn: A bamboo mat. Formed from 竹, with 延 indicating the pronunciation. The Rites of Zhou says: “Measure the hall by mats.” A 筵 is one zhang long.

禋.e: 潔祀也。一曰精意以享爲禋。从示垔聲。
禋.eEn: To offer sacrifice in purity. Another explanation: to make an offering with concentrated sincerity is called 禋. Formed from 示, with 垔 indicating the pronunciation.

虈.e: 楚謂之蘺，晉謂之虈，齊謂之茝。从艸嚻聲。
虈.eEn: In Chu it is called 蘺, in Jin 虈, and in Qi 茝. Formed from 艸, with 嚻 indicating the pronunciation.

簟.eEn: A bamboo mat. Formed from 竹, with 𪉷 indicating the pronunciation.

籧.e: 籧篨，粗竹席也。从竹遽聲。
籧.eEn: 籧篨, a coarse bamboo mat. Formed from 竹, with 遽 indicating the pronunciation.

篨.eEn: The coarse bamboo mat called 籧篨. Formed from 竹, with 除 indicating the pronunciation.

籭.e: 竹器也。可以取粗去細。从竹麗聲。
籭.eEn: A bamboo implement used to retain the coarse material and remove the fine. Formed from 竹, with 麗 indicating the pronunciation.

籓.e: 大箕也。从竹潘聲。一曰蔽也。
籓.eEn: A large winnowing basket. Formed from 竹, with 潘 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation: a screen.

籔.eEn: A basket used in preparing grain for cooking. Formed from 竹, with 數 indicating the pronunciation.

箅.e: 蔽也，所以蔽甑底。从竹𢌿聲。
箅.eEn: A covering: something used to cover the bottom of a steamer. Formed from 竹, with 𢌿 indicating the pronunciation.

蘺.eEn: 江蘺, the plant called 蘼蕪. Formed from 艸, with 離 indicating the pronunciation.

筥.eEn: A basket called 䈰. Formed from 竹, with 呂 indicating the pronunciation.

笥.e: 飯及衣之器也。从竹司聲。
笥.eEn: A container for cooked grain or clothing. Formed from 竹, with 司 indicating the pronunciation.

簞.e: 笥也。从竹單聲。漢津令：簞，小筐也。《傳》曰：“簞食壺漿。”
簞.eEn: A container called 笥. Formed from 竹, with 單 indicating the pronunciation. The Han Regulations for Fords states: “A 簞 is a small basket.” The Commentary says: “Food in baskets and drink in jars.”

簁.eEn: 簁箄, a bamboo implement. Formed from 竹, with 徙 indicating the pronunciation.

箄.eEn: The bamboo implement called 簁箄. Formed from 竹, with 卑 indicating the pronunciation.

篿.eEn: A round bamboo implement. Formed from 竹, with 專 indicating the pronunciation.

箸.eEn: An implement for lifting food when eating. Formed from 竹, with 者 indicating the pronunciation.

簍.eEn: A bamboo basket. Formed from 竹, with 婁 indicating the pronunciation.

筤.eEn: A basket. Formed from 竹, with 良 indicating the pronunciation.

籃.eEn: A large 篝 basket. Formed from 竹, with 監 indicating the pronunciation.

茝.eEn: The plant called 虈. Formed from 艸, with 𦣞 indicating the pronunciation.

篝.e: 笿也。可熏衣。从竹冓聲。宋楚謂竹篝牆以居也。
篝.eEn: A basket called 笿. It can be used to perfume clothing with smoke. Formed from 竹, with 冓 indicating the pronunciation. In Song and Chu, bamboo enclosures used as walls for a dwelling are called 篝.

笿.eEn: A basket for cups. Formed from 竹, with 各 indicating the pronunciation.

籢.eEn: A mirror case. Formed from 竹, with 斂 indicating the pronunciation.

籫.e: 竹器也。从竹贊聲。讀若纂。一曰叢。
籫.eEn: A bamboo implement. Formed from 竹, with 贊 indicating the pronunciation. Pronounced like 纂. Another explanation: a cluster.

籯.eEn: A basket called 笭. Formed from 竹, with 贏 indicating the pronunciation.

簋.e: 黍稷方器也。从竹从皿从皀。
簋.eEn: A square vessel for glutinous and non-glutinous millet. Formed from 竹, 皿, and 皀.

簠.e: 黍稷圜器也。从竹从皿，甫聲。
簠.eEn: A round vessel for glutinous and non-glutinous millet. Formed from 竹 and 皿, with 甫 indicating the pronunciation.

蘪.eEn: The plant called 蘪蕪. Formed from 艸, with 麋 indicating the pronunciation.

篅.e: 以判竹圜以盛穀也。从竹耑聲。
篅.eEn: A round container made from split bamboo for holding grain. Formed from 竹, with 耑 indicating the pronunciation.

簏.eEn: A tall bamboo chest. Formed from 竹, with 鹿 indicating the pronunciation.

筩.eEn: A cut section of bamboo. Formed from 竹, with 甬 indicating the pronunciation.

箯.eEn: A bamboo conveyance for carrying a person. Formed from 竹, with 便 indicating the pronunciation.

笯.eEn: A birdcage. Formed from 竹, with 奴 indicating the pronunciation.

竿.eEn: A bamboo pole. Formed from 竹, with 干 indicating the pronunciation.

籱.eEn: A device for trapping fish by covering them. Formed from 竹, with 靃 indicating the pronunciation.

箇.eEn: An individual piece of bamboo. Formed from 竹, with 固 indicating the pronunciation.

薰.eEn: A fragrant plant. Formed from 艸, with 熏 indicating the pronunciation.

筊.eEn: Bamboo rope. Formed from 竹, with 交 indicating the pronunciation.

筰.eEn: Bamboo rope, 筊. Formed from 竹, with 作 indicating the pronunciation.

箑.eEn: A fan. Formed from 竹, with 疌 indicating the pronunciation.

籠.e: 舉土器也。一曰笭也。从竹龍聲。
籠.eEn: A container for carrying earth. Another explanation says it means 笭, a basket. Formed from 竹, with 龍 indicating the pronunciation.

簝.e: 宗廟盛肉竹器也。从竹尞聲。《周禮》：“供盆簝以待事。”
簝.eEn: A bamboo vessel for holding meat in the ancestral temple. Formed from 竹, with 尞 indicating the pronunciation. The Rites of Zhou says: “Supply basins and 簝 vessels in readiness for the ceremonies.”

篼.eEn: A vessel for watering horses. Formed from 竹, with 兜 indicating the pronunciation.

籚.e: 積竹矛𢧢矜也。从竹盧聲。《春秋國語》曰：“朱儒扶籚。”
籚.eEn: A shaft made of assembled bamboo for a spear or halberd. Formed from 竹, with 盧 indicating the pronunciation. The Discourses of the States of the Spring and Autumn period says: “The dwarfs supported the 籚 shafts.”

箝.eEn: Pincers, 籋. Formed from 竹, with 拑 indicating the pronunciation.

籋.eEn: Pincers, 箝. Formed from 竹, with 爾 indicating the pronunciation.

簦.eEn: A rain hat or canopy. Formed from 竹, with 登 indicating the pronunciation.

笠.eEn: A 簦 without a handle. Formed from 竹, with 立 indicating the pronunciation.

箱.eEn: The receptacle or load compartment of a large carriage. Formed from 竹, with 相 indicating the pronunciation.

篚.eEn: A carriage basket. Formed from 竹, with 匪 indicating the pronunciation.

笭.e: 車笭也。从竹令聲。一曰笭，籯也。
笭.eEn: A carriage basket. Formed from 竹, with 令 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation says that 笭 means 籯, a basket.

策.eEn: A horsewhip. Formed from 竹, with 朿 indicating the pronunciation.

萹.eEn: The plant 萹茿. Formed from 艸, with 扁 indicating the pronunciation.

箠.eEn: To strike a horse. Formed from 竹, with 𡍮 indicating the pronunciation.

笍.e: 羊車騶箠也。箸箴其耑，長半分。从竹内聲。
笍.eEn: A driver's whip for a sheep-drawn carriage. A needle is attached to its tip, extending half a fen. Formed from 竹, with 内 indicating the pronunciation.

籣.e: 所以盛弩矢，人所負也。从竹闌聲。
籣.eEn: A container for crossbow bolts, carried on a person's back. Formed from 竹, with 闌 indicating the pronunciation.

箙.e: 弩矢箙也。从竹服聲。《周禮》：“仲秋獻矢箙。”
箙.eEn: A quiver for crossbow bolts. Formed from 竹, with 服 indicating the pronunciation. The Rites of Zhou says: “In the middle month of autumn, present arrows and quivers.”

笘.e: 折竹箠也。从竹占聲。潁川人名小兒所書寫爲笘。
笘.eEn: A whip made from a split piece of bamboo. Formed from 竹, with 占 indicating the pronunciation. People in Yingchuan call the tablets on which young children practise writing 笘.

笪.eEn: To whip. Formed from 竹, with 旦 indicating the pronunciation.

笞.eEn: To strike. Formed from 竹, with 台 indicating the pronunciation.

籤.e: 驗也。一曰銳也，貫也。从竹韱聲。
籤.eEn: To verify. Another explanation says: sharp; to pierce through. Formed from 竹, with 韱 indicating the pronunciation.

茿.eEn: The plant 萹茿. Formed from 艸, with an abbreviated form of 筑 indicating the pronunciation.

箴.eEn: A needle for stitching clothing. Formed from 竹, with 咸 indicating the pronunciation.

箾.e: 以竿擊人也。从竹削聲。虞舜樂曰箾韶。
箾.eEn: To strike someone with a pole. Formed from 竹, with 削 indicating the pronunciation. The music of Shun of Yu was called 箾韶.

竽.e: 管三十六簧也。从竹亏聲。
竽.eEn: A wind instrument with thirty-six reeds. Formed from 竹, with 亏 indicating the pronunciation.

笙.e: 十三簧。象鳳之身也。笙，正月之音。物生，故謂之笙。大者謂之巢，小者謂之和。从竹生聲。古者隨作笙。
笙.eEn: An instrument with thirteen reeds. It represents the body of a phoenix. The 笙 is the sound of the first month. Because things come into life, 生, it is called 笙. The large kind is called 巢, and the small kind 和. Formed from 竹, with 生 indicating the pronunciation. In antiquity, Sui invented the 笙.

簧.e: 笙中簧也。从竹黃聲。古者女媧作簧。
簧.eEn: The reed inside a 笙. Formed from 竹, with 黃 indicating the pronunciation. In antiquity, Nüwa invented the 簧.

簫.e: 參差管樂。象鳳之翼。从竹肅聲。
簫.eEn: A musical instrument with pipes of unequal lengths. It represents the wings of a phoenix. Formed from 竹, with 肅 indicating the pronunciation.

筒.eEn: A 簫 with a passage running through it. Formed from 竹, with 同 indicating the pronunciation.

籟.e: 三孔龠也。大者謂之笙，其中謂之籟，小者謂之箹。从竹賴聲。
籟.eEn: A three-holed 龠 pipe. The large kind is called 笙, the middle-sized kind 籟, and the small kind 箹. Formed from 竹, with 賴 indicating the pronunciation.

箹.eEn: A small 籟 pipe. Formed from 竹, with 約 indicating the pronunciation.

管.e: 如篪，六孔。十二月之音。物開地牙，故謂之管。从竹官聲。
管.eEn: An instrument like a 篪, with six holes. It is the sound of the twelfth month. Because things open the earth and sprout, it is called 管. Formed from 竹, with 官 indicating the pronunciation.

篎.eEn: A small 管 pipe is called 篎. Formed from 竹, with 眇 indicating the pronunciation.

笛.e: 七孔筩也。从竹由聲。羌笛三孔。
笛.eEn: A pipe with seven holes. Formed from 竹, with 由 indicating the pronunciation. The Qiang flute has three holes.

筑.e: 以竹曲五弦之樂也。从竹从𢀜。𢀜，持之也。竹亦聲。
筑.eEn: A five-stringed musical instrument played with a curved piece of bamboo. Formed from 竹 and 𢀜. The component 𢀜 signifies holding it. The component 竹 also indicates the pronunciation.

箏.e: 鼓弦竹身樂也。从竹爭聲。
箏.eEn: A musical instrument with a bamboo body whose strings are plucked. Formed from 竹, with 爭 indicating the pronunciation.

箛.eEn: A wind instrument called a “blowing whip.” Formed from 竹, with 孤 indicating the pronunciation.

篍.eEn: A pipe for blowing. Formed from 竹, with 秋 indicating the pronunciation.

籌.eEn: An arrow used in the game of throwing arrows into a pot. Formed from 竹, with 壽 indicating the pronunciation.

簺.e: 行棊相塞謂之簺。从竹从塞，塞亦聲。
簺.eEn: Moving game pieces so that they block one another is called 簺. Formed from 竹 and 塞, with 塞 also indicating the pronunciation.

簙.e: 局戲也。六箸十二棊也。从竹博聲。古者烏胄作簙。
簙.eEn: A board game using six throwing sticks and twelve playing pieces. Formed from 竹, with 博 indicating the pronunciation. In antiquity, Wuzhou invented 簙.

篳.e: 藩落也。从竹畢聲。《春秋傳》曰：“篳門圭窬。”
篳.eEn: A fence or enclosure. Formed from 竹, with 畢 indicating the pronunciation. The Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals says: “A brushwood gate and a small, pointed opening in the wall.”

篽.e: 禁苑也。从竹御聲。《春秋傳》曰：“澤之目篽。”
篽.eEn: A restricted park or preserve. Formed from 竹, with 御 indicating the pronunciation. The Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals says: “The designated preserve of the marsh.”

筭.e: 長六寸。計歷數者。从竹从弄。言常弄乃不誤也。
筭.eEn: Counting rods six cun long, used to calculate calendrical numbers. Formed from 竹 and 弄. This signifies that only by continually handling them does one avoid mistakes.

算.eEn: To count. Formed from 竹 and 具. Pronounced like 筭.

笑.eEn: Explanation missing in the source for this character.

簃.e: 閣邊小屋也。从竹移聲。《說文》通用誃。
簃.eEn: A small room beside an elevated chamber. Formed from 竹, with 移 indicating the pronunciation. In the Shuowen Jiezi, 誃 is used interchangeably with it.

筠.eEn: The outer skin of bamboo. Formed from 竹, with 均 indicating the pronunciation.

天.eEn: The summit. Supremely high, with nothing above it. Formed from 一 and 大.

祭.eEn: To make a sacrificial offering. Formed from 示 and a hand holding meat.

苺.eEn: The plant 馬苺. Formed from 艸, with 母 indicating the pronunciation.

笏.e: 公及士所搢也。从竹勿聲。案：籒文作𡇉，象形。義云佩也。古笏佩之。此字後人所加。
笏.eEn: A tablet tucked into the sash by dukes and officers. Formed from 竹, with 勿 indicating the pronunciation. Note: the large-seal form is 𡇉, a pictograph. Its meaning is said to be “to wear at one's side.” In antiquity, the 笏 was worn at the side. This character was added by a later hand.

篦.e: 導也。今俗謂之篦。从竹𣬉聲。
篦.eEn: A comb for arranging the hair. It is now commonly called 篦. Formed from 竹, with 𣬉 indicating the pronunciation.

篙.eEn: An implement for propelling a boat. Formed from 竹, with 高 indicating the pronunciation.

箕.e: 簸也。从竹；𠀠，象形；下其丌也。凡箕之屬皆从箕。
箕.eEn: To winnow. Formed from 竹; 𠀠 is a pictograph, with 丌 beneath it. All characters in the 箕 class are formed with 箕.

簸.eEn: To toss rice upward to remove the husks. Formed from 箕, with 皮 indicating the pronunciation.

丌.e: 下基也。薦物之丌。象形。凡丌之屬皆从丌。讀若箕同。
丌.eEn: A supporting base underneath; a stand on which objects are placed. A pictograph. All characters in the 丌 class are formed with 丌. Pronounced the same as 箕.

典.e: 五帝之書也。从冊在丌上，尊閣之也。莊都說，典，大冊也。
典.eEn: The writings of the Five Emperors. Formed from 冊 placed above 丌, indicating that they are respectfully set upon a stand. Zhuang Du says: “典 means a large written volume.”

顨.e: 巽也。从丌从𩔊 。此《易》顨卦“爲長女，爲風”者。
顨.eEn: The same as 巽. Formed from 丌 and 𩔊. This is the 顨 hexagram in the Book of Changes, described as “the eldest daughter” and “wind.”

畀.e: 相付與之。約在閣上也。从丌甶聲。
畀.eEn: To hand something over to another. A bound bundle is on a stand. Formed from 丌, with 甶 indicating the pronunciation.

茖.eEn: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 各 indicating the pronunciation.

巽.eEn: To provide or have ready. Formed from 丌, with 𠨎 indicating the pronunciation.

奠.e: 置祭也。从酋。酋，酒也。下其丌也。《禮》有奠祭者。
奠.eEn: To set out a sacrificial offering. Formed from 酋, which means wine, with 丌 beneath it. The Rites includes a sacrificial observance called 奠.

左.e: 手相左助也。从𠂇、工。凡左之屬皆从左。
左.eEn: For hands to assist one another. Formed from 𠂇 and 工. All characters in the 左 class are formed with 左.

差.e: 貳也。差不相值也。从左从𠂹。
差.eEn: To differ. 差 means that things do not match one another. Formed from 左 and 𠂹.

工.e: 巧飾也。象人有規榘也。與巫同意。凡工之屬皆从工。
工.eEn: Skilful embellishment. It depicts a person with a compass and square. It follows the same conception as 巫. All characters in the 工 class are formed with 工.

式.eEn: A rule or model. Formed from 工, with 弋 indicating the pronunciation.

巧.eEn: Skill. Formed from 工, with 丂 indicating the pronunciation.

巨.eEn: A carpenter's square. Formed from 工, depicting a hand holding it.

苷.eEn: Licorice. Formed from 艸 and 甘.

巫.e: 祝也。女能事無形，以舞降神者也。象人兩褎舞形。與工同意。古者巫咸初作巫。凡巫之屬皆从巫。
巫.eEn: A ritual invoker: a woman able to serve the unseen and bring down spirits through dance. It depicts a person dancing with two sleeves. It follows the same conception as 工. In antiquity, Wu Xian first instituted the role of 巫. All characters in the 巫 class are formed with 巫.

覡.e: 能齋肅事神明也。在男曰覡，在女曰巫。从巫从見。
覡.eEn: One able to serve the spirits with ritual purification and reverence. A man is called 覡; a woman is called 巫. Formed from 巫 and 見.

甘.e: 美也。从口含一。一，道也。凡甘之屬皆从甘。
甘.eEn: Pleasant-tasting. Formed from 口 containing 一. The component 一 signifies the Way. All characters in the 甘 class are formed with 甘.

甛.e: 美也。从甘从舌。舌，知甘者。
甛.eEn: Pleasant-tasting. Formed from 甘 and 舌. The tongue, 舌, is what recognizes sweetness.

猒.eEn: To be satiated. Formed from 甘 and 肰.

甚.e: 尤安樂也。从甘，从匹耦也。
甚.eEn: Especially contented and happy. Formed from 甘 and 匹, with 匹 signifying a pair.

曰.e: 詞也。从口乙聲。亦象口气出也。凡曰之屬皆从曰。
曰.eEn: To speak. Formed from 口, with 乙 indicating the pronunciation. It also depicts breath coming out of the mouth. All characters in the 曰 class are formed with 曰.

曷.eEn: What; why. Formed from 曰, with 匃 indicating the pronunciation.

芧.e: 艸也。从艸予聲。可以爲繩。
芧.eEn: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 予 indicating the pronunciation. It can be used to make rope.

曶.e: 出气詞也。从曰，象气出形。《春秋傳》曰：“鄭太子曶。”
曶.eEn: An utterance made by expelling breath. Formed from 曰, depicting breath coming out. The Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals says: “Hu, crown prince of Zheng.”

朁.e: 曾也。从曰兓聲。《詩》曰：“朁不畏明。”
朁.eEn: An adverb meaning “ever,” 曾. Formed from 曰, with 兓 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Odes says: “Could they really not fear the light?”

沓.e: 語多沓沓也。从水从曰。遼東有沓縣。
沓.eEn: Much speech, flowing on and on. Formed from 水 and 曰. There is a county named 沓 in Liaodong.

曹.e: 獄之兩曹也。在廷東。从㯥，治事者；从曰。
曹.eEn: The two opposing parties in a legal case. They are situated to the east of the court. Formed from 㯥, signifying those who conduct the proceedings, and 曰.

乃.e: 曳詞之難也。象气之出難。凡𠄎之屬皆从𠄎。
乃.eEn: The difficulty of drawing out an utterance. It depicts breath emerging with difficulty. All characters in the 𠄎 class are formed with 𠄎.

丂.e: 气欲舒出。纸上礙於一也。丂，古文以爲亏字，又以爲巧字。凡丂之屬皆从丂。
丂.eEn: Breath seeking to spread outward, its upward emergence obstructed by 一. In ancient script, 丂 was used for 亏 and also for 巧. All characters in the 丂 class are formed with 丂.

甹.e: 亟詞也。从丂从由。或曰甹，俠也。三輔謂輕財者爲甹。
甹.eEn: An urgent utterance. Formed from 丂 and 由. Another explanation says that 甹 means a chivalrous person. In the Three Metropolitan Districts, someone who places little value on wealth is called 甹.

寧.eEn: An expression of a wish. Formed from 丂, with 寍 indicating the pronunciation.

藎.eEn: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 盡 indicating the pronunciation.

可.e: 𦘫也。从口丂，丂亦聲。凡可之屬皆从可。
可.eEn: To assent, 𦘫. Formed from 口 and 丂, with 丂 also indicating the pronunciation. All characters in the 可 class are formed with 可.

奇.e: 異也。一曰不耦。从大从可。
奇.eEn: Unusual. Another explanation says: unpaired. Formed from 大 and 可.

哿.e: 可也。从可加聲。《詩》曰：“哿矣富人。”
哿.eEn: Acceptable or satisfactory. Formed from 可, with 加 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Odes says: “The wealthy are well enough off.”

哥.e: 聲也。从二可。古文以爲謌字。
哥.eEn: A vocal sound. Formed from two instances of 可. In ancient script, it was used for 謌, “to sing.”

叵.eEn: Not possible. Formed from a reversed 可.

兮.e: 語所稽也。从丂，八象气越亏也。凡兮之屬皆从兮。
兮.eEn: A point at which speech pauses. Formed from 丂; 八 depicts breath passing beyond 亏. All characters in the 兮 class are formed with 兮.

羲.eEn: Breath or vapor. Formed from 兮, with 義 indicating the pronunciation.

乎.e: 語之餘也。从兮，象聲上越揚之形也。
乎.eEn: A surplus sound at the end of an utterance. Formed from 兮, depicting the sound rising and spreading upward.

蒁.eEn: An herb. Formed from 艸, with 述 indicating the pronunciation.

号.e: 痛聲也。从口在丂上。凡号之屬皆从号。
号.eEn: A cry of pain. Formed from 口 placed above 丂. All characters in the 号 class are formed with 号.

號.eEn: To call out. Formed from 号 and 虎.

亏.e: 於也。象气之舒亏。从丂从一。一者，其气平之也。凡亏之屬皆从亏。(今變隸作于。)
亏.eEn: Equivalent to 於. It depicts breath spreading out. Formed from 丂 and 一; 一 represents the breath becoming level. All characters in the 亏 class are formed with 亏. In present clerical script, it has changed to 于.

虧.eEn: A diminution of breath. Formed from 亏, with 雐 indicating the pronunciation.

粵.e: 亏也。審愼之詞者。从亏从宷。《周書》曰：“粤三日丁亥。”
粵.eEn: Equivalent to 亏; a particle expressing careful consideration. Formed from 亏 and 宷. The Book of Zhou says: “On the third day, dinghai.”

平.e: 語平舒也。从亏从八。八，分也。爰禮說。
平.eEn: Speech that is level and unhurried. Formed from 亏 and 八. 八 means division. This is Yuan Li's explanation.

旨.e: 美也。从甘匕聲。凡旨之屬皆从旨。
旨.eEn: Delicious; fine. Formed from 甘, with 匕 indicating the pronunciation. All characters in the 旨 class are formed with 旨.

嘗.eEn: To taste with the mouth. Formed from 旨, with 尚 indicating the pronunciation.

喜.e: 樂也。从壴从口。凡喜之屬皆从喜。
喜.eEn: Joy. Formed from 壴 and 口. All characters in the 喜 class are formed with 喜.

荵.eEn: The herb 忍冬, honeysuckle. Formed from 艸, with 忍 indicating the pronunciation.

憙.eEn: To be pleased. Formed from 心 and 喜, with 喜 also indicating the pronunciation.

嚭.e: 大也。从喜否聲。《春秋傳》：“吳有太宰嚭。”
嚭.eEn: Great. Formed from 喜, with 否 indicating the pronunciation. The Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals says: “Wu had a Grand Steward named 嚭.”

壴.e: 陳樂立而上見也。从屮从豆。凡壴之屬皆从壴。
壴.eEn: Musical instruments set upright on display, with their upper parts visible. Formed from 屮 and 豆. All characters in the 壴 class are formed with 壴.

尌.e: 立也。从壴从寸，持之也。讀若駐。
尌.eEn: To set upright. Formed from 壴 and 寸, representing holding it in place. Pronounced like 駐.

彭.eEn: The sound of a drum. Formed from 壴, with 彡 indicating the pronunciation.

嘉.eEn: Fine; excellent. Formed from 壴, with 加 indicating the pronunciation.

鼛.e: 大鼓也。从鼓咎聲。《詩》曰：“鼛鼓不勝。”
鼛.eEn: A large drum. Formed from 鼓, with 咎 indicating the pronunciation. The Odes says: “The great drums cannot prevail.”

鼖.e: 大鼓謂之鼖。鼖八尺而兩面，以鼓軍事。从鼓，賁省聲。
鼖.eEn: A large drum is called 鼖. It measures eight chi and has two faces; it is used to drum signals in military affairs. Formed from 鼓, with an abbreviated form of 賁 indicating the pronunciation.

萇.e: 萇楚，跳弋。一名羊桃。从艸長聲。
萇.eEn: 萇楚, the plant called 跳弋; another name is 羊桃. Formed from 艸, with 長 indicating the pronunciation.

鼙.eEn: A cavalry drum. Formed from 鼓, with 卑 indicating the pronunciation.

鼘.e: 鼓聲也。从鼓𣶒聲。《詩》曰：“鼗鼓鼘鼘。”
鼘.eEn: The sound of drums. Formed from 鼓, with 𣶒 indicating the pronunciation. The Odes says: “The pellet drums resound.”

鼞.e: 鼔聲也。从鼓堂聲。《詩》曰：“擊鼓其鼞。”
鼞.eEn: The sound of a drum. Formed from 鼓, with 堂 indicating the pronunciation. The Odes says: “Strike the drum: how it booms!”

豈.e: 還師振旅樂也。一曰欲也，登也。从豆，微省聲。凡豈之屬皆从豈。
豈.eEn: Music performed when an army returns and its troops are marshaled. Another explanation is “to desire” or “to ascend.” Formed from 豆, with an abbreviated form of 微 indicating the pronunciation. All characters in the 豈 class are formed with 豈.

愷.eEn: At ease; peaceful. Formed from 心 and 豈, with 豈 also indicating the pronunciation.

薊.eEn: The plant 芺. Formed from 艸, with 魝 indicating the pronunciation.

豆.e: 古食肉器也。从口，象形。凡豆之屬皆从豆。
豆.eEn: An ancient vessel for eating meat. Formed from 口. A pictograph. All characters in the 豆 class are formed with 豆.

梪.eEn: A wooden 豆 vessel is called 梪. Formed from 木 and 豆.

豊.e: 行禮之器也。从豆，象形。凡豊之屬皆从豊。讀與禮同。
豊.eEn: A vessel used in performing rites. Formed from 豆. A pictograph. All characters in the 豊 class are formed with 豊. Pronounced the same as 禮.

豑.e: 爵之次弟也。从豊从弟。《虞書》曰：“平豑東作。”
豑.eEn: The ordering of ranks of nobility. Formed from 豊 and 弟. The Book of Yu says: “Regulate and order the work of spring.”

豐.e: 豆之豐滿者也。从豆，象形。一曰《鄉飲酒》有豐侯者。凡豐之屬皆从豐。
豐.eEn: A 豆 vessel filled to abundance. Formed from 豆. A pictograph. Another explanation refers to an object called 豐侯 in the District Drinking Ceremony. All characters in the 豐 class are formed with 豐.

豔.e: 好而長也。从豐。豐，大也。盇聲。《春秋傳》曰：“美而豔。”
豔.eEn: Beautiful and tall. Formed from 豐, which means “great,” with 盇 indicating the pronunciation. The Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals says: “Beautiful and tall.”

荲.eEn: An herb. Formed from 艸, with 里 indicating the pronunciation. Pronounced like 釐.

虍.e: 虎文也。象形。凡虍之屬皆从虍。
虍.eEn: A tiger's markings. A pictograph. All characters in the 虍 class are formed with 虍.

虞.e: 騶虞也。白虎黑文，尾長於身。仁獸，食自死之肉。从虍吳聲。《詩》曰：“于嗟乎，騶虞。”
虞.eEn: The beast 騶虞: a white tiger with black markings and a tail longer than its body. It is a benevolent beast that eats the flesh of animals that have died naturally. Formed from 虍, with 吳 indicating the pronunciation. The Odes says: “Ah, the 騶虞!”

虙.eEn: The appearance of a tiger. Formed from 虍, with 必 indicating the pronunciation.

虔.e: 虎行皃。从虍文聲。讀若矜。
虔.eEn: The manner in which a tiger walks. Formed from 虍, with 文 indicating the pronunciation. Pronounced like 矜.

虘.e: 虎不柔不信也。从虍且聲。讀若䣜縣。
虘.eEn: A tiger's being neither gentle nor trustworthy. Formed from 虍, with 且 indicating the pronunciation. Pronounced like 䣜 in the name of 䣜 County.

虖.eEn: To roar or howl. Formed from 虍, with 𠀒 indicating the pronunciation.

虐.e: 殘也。从虍，虎足反爪人也。
虐.eEn: Cruel; destructive. Formed from 虍, depicting a tiger's feet turned back to claw a person.

祀.eEn: To offer sacrifices without ceasing. Formed from 示, with 巳 indicating the pronunciation.

藋.e: 釐艸也。一曰拜商藋。从艸翟聲。
藋.eEn: The herb 釐. Another name is 拜商藋. Formed from 艸, with 翟 indicating the pronunciation.

虨.eEn: A tiger's markings; its stripes. Formed from 虍, with 彬 indicating the pronunciation.

虎.e: 山獸之君。从虍，虎足象人足。象形。凡虎之屬皆从虎。
虎.eEn: Lord of the mountain beasts. Formed from 虍; the tiger's feet resemble human feet. A pictograph. All characters in the 虎 class are formed with 虎.

虪.eEn: A black tiger. Formed from 虎, with 儵 indicating the pronunciation.

虦.e: 虎竊毛謂之虦苗。从虎戔聲。竊，淺也。
虦.eEn: A tiger with pale fur is called 虦苗. Formed from 虎, with 戔 indicating the pronunciation. 竊 here means “pale.”

彪.e: 虎文也。从虎，彡象其文也。
彪.eEn: A tiger's markings. Formed from 虎, with 彡 depicting its markings.

芨.e: 堇艸也。从艸及聲。讀若急。
芨.eEn: The herb 堇. Formed from 艸, with 及 indicating the pronunciation. Pronounced like 急.

虓.e: 虎鳴也。一曰師子。从虎九聲。
虓.eEn: A tiger's cry. Another explanation is “lion.” Formed from 虎, with 九 indicating the pronunciation.

虩.e: 《易》：“履虎尾虩虩。”恐懼。一曰蠅虎也。从虎𡭴聲。
虩.eEn: The Changes says: “Treading on a tiger's tail, trembling with fear.” It means fear and dread. Another explanation is “fly-tiger,” a fly-catching spider. Formed from 虎, with 𡭴 indicating the pronunciation.

虢.e: 虎所攫畫明文也。从虎寽聲。
虢.eEn: The distinct markings made by a tiger's clawing and scratching. Formed from 虎, with 寽 indicating the pronunciation.

虒.e: 委虒，虎之有角者也。从虎𠂆聲。
虒.eEn: 委虒, a tiger with horns. Formed from 虎, with 𠂆 indicating the pronunciation.

虤.e: 虎怒也。从二虎。凡虤之屬皆从虤。
虤.eEn: A tiger's anger. Formed from two instances of 虎. All characters in the 虤 class are formed with 虤.

葥.eEn: Mountain berry. Formed from 艸, with 歬 indicating the pronunciation.

贙.e: 分別也。从虤對爭貝。讀若迴。
贙.eEn: To distinguish or separate. Formed from 虤, depicting two opposing tigers contending over a 貝, a shell. Pronounced like 迴.

皿.e: 飯食之用器也。象形。與豆同意。凡皿之屬皆从皿。讀若猛。
皿.eEn: A vessel used for meals. A pictograph. It follows the same idea as 豆. All characters in the 皿 class are formed with 皿. Pronounced like 猛.

盂.eEn: A vessel for food. Formed from 皿, with 亏 indicating the pronunciation.

盌.eEn: A small 盂 bowl. Formed from 皿, with 夗 indicating the pronunciation.

盛.e: 黍稷在器中以祀者也。从皿成聲。
盛.eEn: Broomcorn millet and foxtail millet placed in a vessel for sacrifice. Formed from 皿, with 成 indicating the pronunciation.

齍.e: 黍稷在器以祀者。从皿齊聲。
齍.eEn: Broomcorn millet and foxtail millet placed in a vessel for sacrifice. Formed from 皿, with 齊 indicating the pronunciation.

盧.eEn: A vessel for food. Formed from 皿, with 𧇄 indicating the pronunciation.

盄.eEn: A vessel. Formed from 皿, with 弔 indicating the pronunciation.

盎.eEn: A basin. Formed from 皿, with 央 indicating the pronunciation.

盆.eEn: A basin, equivalent to 盎. Formed from 皿, with 分 indicating the pronunciation.

盨.e: 㯯盨，負戴器也。从皿須聲。
盨.eEn: 㯯盨, a vessel carried on the back or on the head. Formed from 皿, with 須 indicating the pronunciation.

醯.e: 酸也。作醯以𩱙以酒。从𩱙、酒並省，从皿。皿，器也。
醯.eEn: Sour liquid. 醯 is made using 𩱙 and wine. Formed from abbreviated forms of both 𩱙 and 酒, together with 皿. 皿 means a vessel.

盉.eEn: To blend flavors. Formed from 皿, with 禾 indicating the pronunciation.

益.e: 饒也。从水、皿。皿，益之意也。
益.eEn: Abundant. Formed from 水 and 皿. 皿 conveys the idea of increase.

蓩.eEn: The plant 卷耳. Formed from 艸, with 務 indicating the pronunciation.

盈.eEn: To fill a vessel. Formed from 皿 and 夃.

盡.eEn: A vessel being empty inside. Formed from 皿, with 㶳 indicating the pronunciation.

盅.e: 器虛也。从皿中聲。《老子》曰：“道盅而用之。”
盅.eEn: A vessel being empty. Formed from 皿, with 中 indicating the pronunciation. The Laozi says: “The Way is empty, yet one uses it.”

盦.eEn: To cover. Formed from 皿, with 酓 indicating the pronunciation.

盥.e: 澡手也。从𦥑水臨皿。《春秋傳》曰：“奉𠤷沃盥。”
盥.eEn: To wash the hands. Formed from 𦥑 and 水 positioned over 皿, depicting hands and water above a basin. The Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals says: “Holding the water vessel, he poured water for washing the hands.”

盪.eEn: To wash vessels. Formed from 皿, with 湯 indicating the pronunciation.

盋.e: 盋器。盂屬。从皿犮聲。或从金从本。
盋.eEn: A bowl-like vessel, a kind of 盂. Formed from 皿, with 犮 indicating the pronunciation. An alternative form is formed from 金 and 本.

去.e: 人相違也。从大凵聲。凡去之屬皆从去。
去.eEn: People parting from one another. Formed from 大, with 凵 indicating the pronunciation. All characters in the 去 class are formed with 去.

蓡.e: 人薓，藥艸，出上黨。从艸𣹰聲。
蓡.eEn: Ginseng, a medicinal herb produced in Shangdang. Formed from 艸, with 𣹰 indicating the pronunciation.

朅.eEn: To depart. Formed from 去, with 曷 indicating the pronunciation.

血.e: 祭所薦牲血也。从皿，一象血形。凡血之屬皆从血。
血.eEn: The blood of a sacrificial animal presented in sacrifice. Formed from 皿, with 一 depicting the blood. All characters in the 血 class are formed with 血.

衁.e: 血也。从血亡聲。《春秋傳》曰：“士刲羊，亦無𥁃也。”
衁.eEn: Blood. Formed from 血, with 亡 indicating the pronunciation. The Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals says: “The man cut the sheep, but there was no blood either.”

衃.eEn: Congealed blood. Formed from 血, with 不 indicating the pronunciation.

衄.eEn: Bleeding from the nose. Formed from 血, with 丑 indicating the pronunciation.

卹.e: 憂也。从血卩聲。一曰鮮少也。
卹.eEn: To be concerned or anxious. Formed from 血, with 卩 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation is “scant; few.”

衋.e: 傷痛也。从血、聿，皕聲。《周書》曰：“民冈不衋傷心。”
衋.eEn: Grief and pain. Formed from 血 and 聿, with 皕 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Zhou says: “None of the people fails to grieve and suffer in the heart.”

盇.eEn: To cover. Formed from 血 and 大.

衊.eEn: Foul blood. Formed from 血, with 蔑 indicating the pronunciation.

丶.e: 有所絕止，丶而識之也。凡丶之屬皆从丶。
丶.eEn: Where something is broken off or comes to a stop, a dot is made to mark it. All characters in the 丶 class are formed with 丶.

主.e: 鐙中火主也。从纹，象形。从丶，丶亦聲。
主.eEn: The main flame in a lamp. Formed from 纹. A pictograph. It is formed with 丶, which also indicates the pronunciation.

咅.e: 相與語，唾而不受也。从丶从否，否亦聲。
咅.eEn: When speaking with another, to spit and refuse to accept what is said. Formed from 丶 and 否, with 否 also indicating the pronunciation.

丹.e: 巴越之赤石也。象采丹井，一象丹形。凡丹之屬皆从丹。
丹.eEn: A red stone from Ba and Yue. It depicts a shaft from which cinnabar is mined, with 一 depicting the cinnabar. All characters in the 丹 class are formed with 丹.

雘.e: 善丹也。从丹蒦聲。《周書》曰：“惟其𢾅丹雘。”讀若隺。
雘.eEn: Fine cinnabar. Formed from 丹, with 蒦 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Zhou says: “Only then coat it with cinnabar and fine pigment.” Pronounced like 隺.

彤.e: 丹飾也。从丹从彡。彡，其畫也。
彤.eEn: Decoration in cinnabar red. Formed from 丹 and 彡. 彡 represents its painted designs.

青.e: 東方色也。木生火，从生、丹。丹青之信言象然。凡青之屬皆从青。
青.eEn: The color of the east. Wood generates fire, so it is formed from 生 and 丹. The constancy of cinnabar red and blue-green is expressed by this depiction. All characters in the 青 class are formed with 青.

靜.eEn: To examine carefully. Formed from 青, with 爭 indicating the pronunciation.

井.e: 八家一井，象構韓形。•，𦉥之象也。古者伯益初作井。凡井之屬皆从井。
井.eEn: One well for eight households. It depicts the structure of the well's enclosure. The dot depicts a water jar. In ancient times, Boyi first made wells. All characters in the 井 class are formed with 井.

阱.eEn: A pitfall. Formed from 𨸏 and 井, with 井 also indicating the pronunciation.

刱.e: 造法刱業也。从井刅聲。讀若創。
刱.eEn: To establish rules and found an undertaking. Formed from 井, with 刅 indicating the pronunciation. Pronounced like 創.

荍.eEn: The plant called pifu. Formed from 艸, with 收 indicating the pronunciation.

皀.e: 穀之馨香也。象嘉穀在裹中之形。匕，所以扱之。或說皀，一粒也。凡皀之屬皆从皀。又讀若香。
皀.eEn: The fragrant aroma of grain. It depicts fine grain inside a wrapping. 匕 is the implement used to scoop it out. Another explanation says that 皀 means a single grain. All characters in the 皀 class are formed with 皀. It is also read like 香.

卽.eEn: To approach food and eat. Formed from 皀, with 卪 indicating the pronunciation.

旣.e: 小食也。从皀旡聲。《論語》曰：“不使勝食旣。”
旣.eEn: To eat a little. Formed from 皀, with 旡 indicating the pronunciation. The Analects says: “He did not allow it to exceed the amount of grain food eaten.”

冟.e: 飯剛柔不調相著。从皀冂聲。讀若適。
冟.eEn: Cooked rice whose hard and soft portions are uneven and stick together. Formed from 皀, with 冂 indicating the pronunciation. Read like 適.

鬯.e: 以秬釀𩰪艸，芬芳攸服，以降神也。从凵，凵，器也；中象米；匕，所以扱之。《易》曰：“不喪匕鬯。”凡鬯之屬皆从鬯。
鬯.eEn: A fragrant liquor brewed from black millet with aromatic herbs, used in ritual service to bring down the spirits. Formed from 凵, which represents a vessel; the middle depicts rice; 匕 is the implement used to scoop it out. The Changes says: “He does not lose the ladle or the sacrificial liquor.” All characters in the 鬯 class are formed with 鬯.

爵.e: 禮器也。象爵之形，中有鬯酒，又持之也。所以飲。器象爵者，取其鳴節節足足也。
爵.eEn: A ritual vessel. It depicts the shape of a jue vessel, with aromatic sacrificial liquor inside and a hand holding it. It is used for drinking. The vessel resembles a sparrow, taking its name from the sparrow's call, “jie-jie, zu-zu.”

食.e: 一米也。从皀亼聲。或說亼皀也。凡食之屬皆从食。
食.eEn: A grain of rice. Formed from 皀, with 亼 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation says that it represents gathering grain. All characters in the 食 class are formed with 食.

飪.eEn: Thoroughly cooked. Formed from 食, with 壬 indicating the pronunciation.

飴.eEn: A syrup made by boiling down malted rice. Formed from 食, with 台 indicating the pronunciation.

餅.eEn: A cake made from flour. Formed from 食, with 并 indicating the pronunciation.

餈.eEn: A rice cake. Formed from 食, with 次 indicating the pronunciation.

饘.e: 糜也。从食亶聲。周謂之饘，宋謂之餬。
饘.eEn: Thick porridge. Formed from 食, with 亶 indicating the pronunciation. In Zhou it is called 饘; in Song it is called 餬.

祡.e: 燒祡燓燎以祭天神。从示此聲。《虞書》曰：“至于岱宗，祡。”
祡.eEn: To burn firewood in a blazing fire as a sacrifice to the heavenly spirits. Formed from 示, with 此 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Yu says: “He arrived at Mount Daizong and offered a burnt sacrifice.”

萭.eEn: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 禹 indicating the pronunciation.

餥.e: 𩝍也。从食非聲。陳楚之閒相謁食麥飯曰餥。
餥.eEn: Food. Formed from 食, with 非 indicating the pronunciation. In the region between Chen and Chu, visiting one another and eating cooked wheat is called 餥.

饎.e: 酒食也。从食喜聲。《詩》曰：“可以饙饎。”
饎.eEn: Wine and food. Formed from 食, with 喜 indicating the pronunciation. The Odes says: “With these one can steam grain and prepare wine and food.”

籑.eEn: To prepare food. Formed from 食, with 算 indicating the pronunciation.

養.eEn: To provide sustenance and support. Formed from 食, with 羊 indicating the pronunciation.

飯.eEn: To eat. Formed from 食, with 反 indicating the pronunciation.

飤.eEn: Provisions. Formed from 人 and 食.

饡.eEn: To pour broth over cooked rice. Formed from 食, with 贊 indicating the pronunciation.

荑.eEn: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 夷 indicating the pronunciation.

餔.e: 日加申時食也。从食甫聲。
餔.eEn: To eat when the sun reaches the shen period of the day. Formed from 食, with 甫 indicating the pronunciation.

餐.eEn: To swallow. Formed from 食, with 𣦼 indicating the pronunciation.

饁.e: 餉田也。从食盍聲。《詩》曰：“饁彼南畝。”
饁.eEn: To take food to people working in the fields. Formed from 食, with 盍 indicating the pronunciation. The Odes says: “Take food to those in the southern fields.”

饟.e: 周人謂餉曰饟。从食襄聲。
饟.eEn: The people of Zhou call the supplying of food 饟. Formed from 食, with 襄 indicating the pronunciation.

餉.eEn: To supply food. Formed from 食, with 向 indicating the pronunciation.

饋.eEn: To supply food. Formed from 食, with 貴 indicating the pronunciation.

饗.e: 鄉人飲酒也。从食从鄉，鄉亦聲。
饗.eEn: People of a township drinking wine together. Formed from 食 and 鄉, with 鄉 also indicating the pronunciation.

饛.e: 盛器滿皃。从食蒙聲。《詩》曰：“有饛簋飧。”
饛.eEn: The appearance of a serving vessel filled to the brim. Formed from 食, with 蒙 indicating the pronunciation. The Odes says: “The gui vessel is heaped with supper.”

飵.e: 楚人相謁食麥曰飵。从食乍聲。
飵.eEn: The people of Chu call visiting one another and eating wheat 飵. Formed from 食, with 乍 indicating the pronunciation.

餬.eEn: To depend on others for one's food. Formed from 食, with 胡 indicating the pronunciation.

飶.e: 食之香也。从食必聲。《詩》曰：“有飶其香。”
飶.eEn: The fragrance of food. Formed from 食, with 必 indicating the pronunciation. The Odes says: “How fragrant is its aroma!”

飽.eEn: Satiated. Formed from 食, with 包 indicating the pronunciation.

饒.eEn: To have enough to eat. Formed from 食, with 堯 indicating the pronunciation.

苦.eEn: The great bitter herb, called ling. Formed from 艸, with 古 indicating the pronunciation.

餘.eEn: Abundance. Formed from 食, with 余 indicating the pronunciation.

餀.e: 食臭也。从食艾聲。《爾雅》曰：“餀謂之喙。”
餀.eEn: The foul smell of food. Formed from 食, with 艾 indicating the pronunciation. The Erya says: “餀 is called 喙.”

餞.e: 送去也。从食戔聲。《詩》曰：“顯父餞之。”
餞.eEn: To send someone off on departure. Formed from 食, with 戔 indicating the pronunciation. The Odes says: “Xianfu gave him a farewell feast.”

餫.eEn: Supplying food in the countryside is called 餫. Formed from 食, with 軍 indicating the pronunciation.

館.e: 客舍也。从食官聲。《周禮》：五十里有市，市有館，館有積，以待朝聘之客。
館.eEn: A lodging for guests. Formed from 食, with 官 indicating the pronunciation. The Rites of Zhou states: “Every fifty li there is a market; the market has a guesthouse, and the guesthouse has stored provisions to receive guests coming for court audiences and diplomatic visits.”

饕.eEn: Greedy. Formed from 食, with 號 indicating the pronunciation.

飻.e: 貪也。从食，殄省聲。《春秋傳》曰：“謂之饕飻。”
飻.eEn: Greedy. Formed from 食, with an abbreviated form of 殄 indicating the pronunciation. The Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals says: “They called him Taotie.”

饖.eEn: Cooked rice spoiled by heat. Formed from 食, with 歲 indicating the pronunciation.

饐.eEn: Cooked rice spoiled by dampness. Formed from 食, with 壹 indicating the pronunciation.

餲.e: 飯餲也。从食曷聲。《論語》曰：“食饐而餲。”
餲.eEn: Cooked rice that has turned bad. Formed from 食, with 曷 indicating the pronunciation. The Analects says: “The food has spoiled and turned bad.”

菩.eEn: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 咅 indicating the pronunciation.

饑.eEn: When grain fails to ripen, it is called 饑. Formed from 食, with 幾 indicating the pronunciation.

饉.eEn: When vegetables fail to mature, it is called 饉. Formed from 食, with 堇 indicating the pronunciation.

餧.e: 飢也。从食委聲。一曰魚敗曰餧。
餧.eEn: Hungry. Formed from 食, with 委 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation says that spoiled fish is called 餧.

飢.eEn: Hungry. Formed from 食, with 几 indicating the pronunciation.

餓.eEn: Hungry. Formed from 食, with 我 indicating the pronunciation.

餽.e: 吳人謂祭曰餽。从食从鬼，鬼亦聲。
餽.eEn: The people of Wu call a sacrifice 餽. Formed from 食 and 鬼, with 鬼 also indicating the pronunciation.

餟.eEn: To pour a libation in sacrifice. Formed from 食, with 叕 indicating the pronunciation.

餕.eEn: What remains of a meal. Formed from 食, with 夋 indicating the pronunciation.

餻.eEn: A kind of grain cake. Formed from 食, with 羔 indicating the pronunciation.

亼.e: 三合也。从入、一，象三合之形。凡亼之屬皆从亼。讀若集。
亼.eEn: Three coming together. Formed from 入 and 一, depicting three coming together. All characters in the 亼 class are formed with 亼. Read like 集.

合.eEn: To close the mouth. Formed from 亼 and 口.

僉.e: 皆也。从亼从吅从从。《虞書》曰：“僉曰伯夷。”
僉.eEn: All. Formed from 亼, 吅, and 从. The Book of Yu says: “All said, ‘Boyi.’”

侖.eEn: To think. Formed from 亼 and 冊.

今.e: 是時也。从亼从绁。绁，古文及。
今.eEn: The present time. Formed from 亼 and 绁. 绁 is the ancient-script form of 及.

舍.e: 市居曰舍。从亼、屮，象屋也。口象築也。
舍.eEn: A dwelling in a marketplace is called 舍. Formed from 亼 and 屮, depicting a house. 口 depicts its earthen construction.

會.e: 合也。从亼，从曾省。曾，益也。凡會之屬皆从會。
會.eEn: To join together. Formed from 亼 and an abbreviated form of 曾. 曾 means to add. All characters in the 會 class are formed with 會.

茅.eEn: Thatching grass. Formed from 艸, with 矛 indicating the pronunciation.

朇.eEn: To add. Formed from 會, with 卑 indicating the pronunciation.

倉.e: 榖藏也。倉黃取而藏之，故謂之倉。从食省，口象倉形。凡倉之屬皆从倉。
倉.eEn: A storehouse for grain. Grain is gathered and stored in haste, hence the name 倉. Formed from an abbreviated form of 食; 口 depicts the shape of a granary. All characters in the 倉 class are formed with 倉.

牄.e: 鳥獸來食聲也。从倉爿聲。《虞書》曰：“鳥獸牄牄。”
牄.eEn: The sound of birds and beasts coming to feed. Formed from 倉, with 爿 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Yu says: “Birds and beasts come clamoring to feed.”

入.e: 内也。象从上俱下也。凡入之屬皆从入。
入.eEn: To enter. It depicts coming down together from above. All characters in the 入 class are formed with 入.

內.eEn: To enter. Formed from 口, representing entry from outside.

糴.eEn: To buy grain. Formed from 入 and 䊮.

仝.eEn: Complete. Formed from 入 and 工.

菅.eEn: Thatching grass. Formed from 艸, with 官 indicating the pronunciation.

缶.e: 瓦器。所以盛酒𤖅。秦人鼓之以節謌。象形。凡缶之屬皆从缶。
缶.eEn: An earthenware vessel used to hold wine and liquid refreshments. The people of Qin beat it to keep time with songs. A pictograph. All characters in the 缶 class are formed with 缶.

匋.e: 瓦器也。从缶，包省聲。古者昆吾作匋。案：《史篇》讀與缶同。
匋.eEn: An earthenware vessel. Formed from 缶, with an abbreviated form of 包 indicating the pronunciation. In antiquity, Kunwu made pottery. Note: In the Shi Primer, it is read the same as 缶.

罌.eEn: An earthenware jar. Formed from 缶, with 賏 indicating the pronunciation.

缾.eEn: A jar. Formed from 缶, with 幷 indicating the pronunciation.

罃.e: 備火，長頸缾也。从缶，熒省聲。
罃.eEn: A long-necked jar kept ready for fighting fires. Formed from 缶, with an abbreviated form of 熒 indicating the pronunciation.

蘄.e: 艸也。从艸纥聲。江夏有蘄春亭。
蘄.eEn: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 纥 indicating the pronunciation. Jiangxia has a place called Qichun Pavilion.

缸.eEn: An earthenware vessel. Formed from 缶, with 工 indicating the pronunciation.

缺.eEn: A vessel being broken. Formed from 缶, with an abbreviated form of 決 indicating the pronunciation.

罅.e: 裂也。从缶虖聲。缶燒善裂也。
罅.eEn: To split or crack. Formed from 缶, with 虖 indicating the pronunciation. Earthenware vessels are prone to cracking when fired.

罄.e: 器中空也。从缶殸聲。殸，古文磬字。《詩》云：“缾之罄矣。”
罄.eEn: The inside of a vessel being empty. Formed from 缶, with 殸 indicating the pronunciation. 殸 is the ancient-script form of 磬. The Odes says: “The jar is empty.”

罊.eEn: The contents of a vessel being exhausted. Formed from 缶, with 𣪠 indicating the pronunciation.

莞.e: 艸也。可以作席。从艸完聲。
莞.eEn: A plant that can be used to make mats. Formed from 艸, with 完 indicating the pronunciation.

缿.e: 受錢器也。从缶后聲。古以瓦，今以竹。
缿.eEn: A vessel for receiving coins. Formed from 缶, with 后 indicating the pronunciation. In antiquity it was made of earthenware; now it is made of bamboo.

罐.eEn: A vessel. Formed from 缶, with 雚 indicating the pronunciation.

矢.e: 弓弩矢也。从入，象鏑栝羽之形。古者夷牟初作矢。凡矢之屬皆从矢。
矢.eEn: An arrow for a bow or crossbow. Formed from 入, depicting the arrowhead, nock, and feathers. In antiquity, Yimou first made arrows. All characters in the 矢 class are formed with 矢.

矯.eEn: A clamp for bending and straightening arrow shafts. Formed from 矢, with 喬 indicating the pronunciation.

矰.eEn: An arrow used for shooting birds with an attached cord. Formed from 矢, with 曾 indicating the pronunciation.

矦.e: 春饗所䠶矦也。从人；从厂，象張布；矢在其下。天子䠶熊虎豹，服猛也；諸矦䠶熊豕虎；大夫射麋，麋，惑也；士射鹿豕，爲田除害也。其祝曰：“毋若不寕矦，不朝于王所，故伉而䠶汝也。”
矦.eEn: The target shot at during the spring ceremonial feast. Formed from 人 and 厂, which depicts cloth stretched out, with 矢 beneath it. The Son of Heaven shoots at representations of bears, tigers, and leopards, signifying the subduing of fierce creatures. The feudal lords shoot at bears, boars, and tigers. Great officers shoot at milu deer; milu signifies delusion. Officers shoot at deer and boars, signifying the removal of pests from the fields. The invocation says: “Do not be like a restless lord who does not attend the king's court; for that reason we raise our bows and shoot you.”

短.e: 有所長短，以矢爲正。从矢豆聲。
短.eEn: Things have length or shortness, with the arrow serving as the standard. Formed from 矢, with 豆 indicating the pronunciation.

矤.e: 況也，詞也。从矢，引省聲。从矢，取詞之所之如矢也。
矤.eEn: ‘How much more’; a grammatical expression. Formed from 矢, with an abbreviated form of 引 indicating the pronunciation. It uses 矢 because words travel toward their destination like an arrow.

禷.e: 以事類祭天神。从示類聲。
禷.eEn: To sacrifice to the heavenly spirits according to the kind of affair involved. Formed from 示, with 類 indicating the pronunciation.

藺.eEn: A kind of mat-making rush. Formed from 艸, with 閵 indicating the pronunciation.

知.eEn: An expression in speech. Formed from 口 and 矢.

矣.eEn: A particle marking the completion of an utterance. Formed from 矢, with 以 indicating the pronunciation.

矮.eEn: A short person. Formed from 矢, with 委 indicating the pronunciation.

高.e: 崇也。象臺觀高之形。从冂、口。與倉、舍同意。凡高之屬皆从高。
高.eEn: Lofty. It depicts the height of a raised terrace or lookout tower. Formed from 冂 and 口. Its formative principle is the same as that of 倉 and 舍. All characters in the 高 class are formed with 高.

亭.e: 民所安定也。亭有樓，从高省，丁聲。
亭.eEn: A place where people settle and rest. A pavilion has an upper story. Formed from an abbreviated form of 高, with 丁 indicating the pronunciation.

亳.e: 京兆杜陵亭也。从高省，乇聲。
亳.eEn: A pavilion district in Duling, in the Jingzhao region. Formed from an abbreviated 高, with 乇 indicating the pronunciation.

冂.e: 邑外謂之郊，郊外謂之野，野外謂之林，林外謂之冂。象遠界也。凡冂之屬皆从冂。
冂.eEn: Outside a settlement is called the suburban zone; beyond the suburban zone is called the open country; beyond the open country is called the forest; beyond the forest is called 冂. It depicts a distant boundary. All characters in the 冂 class are formed with 冂.

市.e: 買賣所之也。市有垣，从冂从绁，绁，古文及，象物相及也。之省聲。
市.eEn: A place to which people go to buy and sell. A market has enclosing walls. Formed from 冂 and 绁. 绁 is the ancient form of 及, depicting things reaching one another. An abbreviated 之 indicates the pronunciation.

冘.eEn: Moving along in a continuous, flowing manner. Formed from 人 emerging from 冂.

蒢.eEn: Huangchu, the plant called 職. Formed from 艸, with 除 indicating the pronunciation.

央.e: 中央也。从大在冂之内。大，人也。央㫄同意。一曰久也。
央.eEn: The center. Formed from 大 inside 冂. 大 represents a person. 央 and 㫄 embody the same idea. Another explanation is: long-lasting.

隺.e: 高至也。从隹上欲出冂。《易》曰：“夫乾隺然。”
隺.eEn: Reaching high. Formed from 隹 above, about to emerge from 冂. The Book of Changes says: “Indeed, Qian rises loftily.”

京.e: 人所爲絕高丘也。从高省，| 象高形。凡京之屬皆从京。
京.eEn: An exceptionally high mound made by people. Formed from an abbreviated 高; the vertical stroke depicts height. All characters in the 京 class are formed with 京.

就.e: 就，高也。从京从尤。尤，異於凡也。
就.eEn: To reach a high position. Formed from 京 and 尤. 尤 means different from the ordinary.

亯.e: 獻也。从高省，曰象進孰物形。《孝經》曰：“祭則鬼亯之。”凡亯之屬皆从亯。
亯.eEn: To offer. Formed from an abbreviated 高; 曰 depicts the presentation of cooked offerings. The Classic of Filial Piety says: “When sacrifices are made, the spirits partake of them.” All characters in the 亯 class are formed with 亯.

蒲.e: 水艸也。可以作席。从艸浦聲。
蒲.eEn: An aquatic plant that can be used to make mats. Formed from 艸, with 浦 indicating the pronunciation.

厚.eEn: The thickness of mountains and hills. Formed from 𣆪 and 厂.

畗.e: 滿也。从高省，象高厚之形。凡畗之屬皆从畗。讀若伏。
畗.eEn: Full. Formed from an abbreviated 高, depicting height and thickness. All characters in the 畗 class are formed with 畗. Pronounced like 伏.

良.eEn: Good. Formed from an abbreviated 畗, with 亡 indicating the pronunciation.

稟.eEn: To bestow grain. Formed from 㐭 and 禾.

亶.eEn: Having abundant grain. Formed from 㐭, with 旦 indicating the pronunciation.

啚.eEn: To be sparing. Formed from 口 and 㐭. 㐭 means to receive.

嗇.e: 愛瀒也。从來从㐭。來者，㐭而藏之。故田夫謂之嗇夫。凡嗇之屬皆从嗇。
嗇.eEn: To cherish and be sparing with things. Formed from 來 and 㐭. What comes in is put into a granary and stored. Thus a farmer is called a “husband of thrift.” All characters in the 嗇 class are formed with 嗇.

蒻.e: 蒲子。可以爲平席。从艸弱聲。
蒻.eEn: Young cattail growth, which can be used to make flat mats. Formed from 艸, with 弱 indicating the pronunciation.

牆.eEn: An enclosing wall or screen. Formed from 嗇, with 爿 indicating the pronunciation.

來.e: 周所受瑞麥來麰。一來二縫，象芒朿之形。天所來也，故爲行來之來。《詩》曰：“詒我來麰。”凡來之屬皆从來。
來.eEn: The auspicious grain, laimou, received by the Zhou. One central stalk and two rows depict its awns and pointed shoots. It was something Heaven caused to come, and therefore the character was used for “come” in the sense of coming and going. The Book of Odes says: “He bestowed on us wheat and barley.” All characters in the 來 class are formed with 來.

麥.e: 芒穀，秋穜厚薶，故謂之麥。麥，金也。金王而生，火王而死。从來，有穗者；从夊。凡麥之屬皆从麥。
麥.eEn: An awned grain. It is sown in autumn and buried deeply; hence it is called 麥. 麥 belongs to Metal: it grows when Metal holds sway and dies when Fire holds sway. Formed from 來, representing a plant with ears of grain, and from 夊. All characters in the 麥 class are formed with 麥.

麰.eEn: Laimou, a kind of wheat or barley. Formed from 麥, with 牟 indicating the pronunciation.

麧.eEn: Hard wheat. Formed from 麥, with 气 indicating the pronunciation.

麩.eEn: The fragmented outer husk of wheat; bran. Formed from 麥, with 夫 indicating the pronunciation.

麪.eEn: Ground wheat; flour. Formed from 麥, with 丏 indicating the pronunciation.

麷.e: 煑麥也。从麥豐聲。讀若馮。
麷.eEn: Boiled wheat. Formed from 麥, with 豐 indicating the pronunciation. Pronounced like 馮.

麮.eEn: Sweet wheat gruel. Formed from 麥, with 去 indicating the pronunciation.

夊.e: 行遲曳夊夊，象人兩脛有所躧也。凡夊之屬皆从夊。
夊.eEn: Walking slowly, dragging the feet. It depicts a person whose two lower legs have something being trodden beneath them. All characters in the 夊 class are formed with 夊.

夋.e: 行夋夋也。一曰倨也。从夊允聲。
夋.eEn: To walk in a slow, deliberate manner. Another explanation is: haughty. Formed from 夊, with 允 indicating the pronunciation.

夌.e: 越也。从夊从𡴆。𡴆，高也。一曰夌约也。
夌.eEn: To pass beyond. Formed from 夊 and 𡴆. 𡴆 means high. Another explanation is: to encroach upon or constrain.

蓷.e: 萑也。从艸推聲。《詩》曰：“中谷有蓷。”
蓷.eEn: The plant called 萑. Formed from 艸, with 推 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Odes says: “In the valley there is motherwort.”

致.eEn: To convey to a destination. Formed from 夊 and 至.

憂.e: 和之行也。从夊𢚧聲。《詩》曰：“布政憂憂。”
憂.eEn: A harmonious manner of walking. Formed from 夊, with 𢚧 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Odes says: “He spreads his government gently and harmoniously.”

愛.eEn: A manner of walking. Formed from 夊, with 㤅 indicating the pronunciation.

竷.e: 繇也舞也。樂有章。从章从夅从夊。《詩》曰：“竷竷舞我。”
