頢.eEn: A short face. Formed from 頁, with 𠯑 indicating the pronunciation.

頲.eEn: A narrow head. Formed from 頁, with 廷 indicating the pronunciation.

頠.eEn: A composed and practiced bearing of the head. Formed from 頁, with 危 indicating the pronunciation.

頷.eEn: A yellow complexion. Formed from 頁, with 含 indicating the pronunciation.

薄.e: 林薄也。一曰蠶薄。从艸溥聲。
薄.eEn: A thicket. Another meaning is a tray for silkworms. Formed from 艸, with 溥 indicating the pronunciation.

頍.e: 舉頭也。从頁支聲。《詩》曰：“有頍者弁。”
頍.eEn: To raise the head. Formed from 頁, with 支 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Odes says: “That raised ceremonial cap.”

顧.eEn: To turn and look back. Formed from 頁, with 雇 indicating the pronunciation.

順.eEn: Order; proper arrangement. Formed from 頁 and 巛.

顓.eEn: The cautious appearance of the head. Formed from 頁, with 耑 indicating the pronunciation.

頊.eEn: The cautious appearance of the head. Formed from 頁, with 玉 indicating the pronunciation.

顉.e: 低頭也。从頁金聲。《春秋傳》曰：“迎于門，顉之而巳。”
顉.eEn: To lower the head. Formed from 頁, with 金 indicating the pronunciation. The Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals says: “He met him at the gate and merely nodded his head to him.”

苑.e: 所以養禽獸也。从艸夗聲。
苑.eEn: An enclosure for keeping birds and beasts. Formed from 艸, with 夗 indicating the pronunciation.

頓.eEn: To lower the head. Formed from 頁, with 屯 indicating the pronunciation.

頫.e: 低頭也。从頁，逃省。太史卜書，頫仰字如此。楊雄曰：人面頫。
頫.eEn: To lower the head. Formed from 頁 and an abbreviated form of 逃. In the Grand Scribe’s divination writings, the characters for looking down and looking up are written in this way. Yang Xiong says: “A person’s face looks downward.”

頣.eEn: The appearance of raising the eyes to look at someone. Formed from 頁, with 臣 indicating the pronunciation.

頡.eEn: To hold the neck straight. Formed from 頁, with 吉 indicating the pronunciation.

顥.e: 白皃。从頁从景。《楚詞》曰：“天白顥顥。”南山四顥，白首人也。
顥.eEn: A white appearance. Formed from 頁 and 景. The Songs of Chu says: “The sky is white, brilliantly white.” The Four Hao of the Southern Mountain were white-haired men.

頨.e: 頭妍也。从頁，翩省聲。讀若翩。
頨.eEn: A beautiful head. Formed from 頁, with an abbreviated form of 翩 indicating the pronunciation. Read like 翩.

藪.e: 大澤也。从艸𢿙聲。九州之藪：楊州具區，荆州雲夢，豫州甫田，青州孟諸，沇州大野，雝州弦圃，幽州奚養，冀州楊紆，并州昭餘祁是也。
藪.eEn: A great marsh. Formed from 艸, with 𢿙 indicating the pronunciation. The marshes of the Nine Provinces are: Juqu in Yangzhou, Yunmeng in Jingzhou, Futian in Yuzhou, Mengzhu in Qingzhou, Daye in Yanzhou, Xianpu in Yongzhou, Xiyang in Youzhou, Yangyu in Jizhou, and Zhaoyuqi in Bingzhou.

顗.eEn: A cautious and dignified appearance. Formed from 頁, with 豈 indicating the pronunciation.

顅.e: 頭鬢少髮也。从頁肩聲。《周禮》：“數目顅脰。”
顅.eEn: Having little hair at the temples. Formed from 頁, with 肩 indicating the pronunciation. The Rites of Zhou says: “Closely set eyes and a sparsely haired neck.”

頛.e: 頭不正也。从頁从耒。耒，頭傾也。讀又若《春秋》陳夏齧之齧。
頛.eEn: A head that is not upright. Formed from 頁 and 耒. 耒 signifies the head leaning. It is also read like 齧 in the name of Chen’s Xia Nie in the Spring and Autumn Annals.

頗.eEn: A head tilted to one side. Formed from 頁, with 皮 indicating the pronunciation.

菑.e: 不耕田也。从艸、甾。《易》曰：“不菑畬。”
菑.eEn: An untilled field. Formed from 艸 and 甾. The Book of Changes says: “Without breaking new ground or cultivating older fields.”

顫.eEn: A head that is not upright. Formed from 頁, with 亶 indicating the pronunciation.

顑.e: 飯不飽，面黃起行也。从頁咸聲。讀若戇。
顑.eEn: To have insufficient food, so that the face turns yellow and develops lines. Formed from 頁, with 咸 indicating the pronunciation. Read like 戇.

顲.eEn: A sallow, gaunt appearance of the face. Formed from 頁, with 𤎭 indicating the pronunciation.

煩.e: 熱頭痛也。从頁从火。一曰焚省聲。
煩.eEn: A headache caused by heat. Formed from 頁 and 火. Another explanation is that an abbreviated form of 焚 indicates the pronunciation.

頪.e: 難曉也。从頁、米。一曰鮮白皃。从粉省。
頪.eEn: Difficult to understand. Formed from 頁 and 米. Another meaning is a bright white appearance; on this explanation, it is formed with an abbreviated form of 粉.

顦.eEn: To be haggard and worn. Formed from 頁, with 焦 indicating the pronunciation.

顇.eEn: To be haggard and worn. Formed from 頁, with 卒 indicating the pronunciation.

頦.eEn: Ugly. Formed from 頁, with 亥 indicating the pronunciation.

顯.eEn: Bright ornamentation of the head. Formed from 頁, with 㬎 indicating the pronunciation.

預.e: 安也。案：經典通用豫。从頁，未詳。
預.eEn: At ease. Note: the classical texts generally use 豫 for this meaning. Formed from 頁; the formation is not fully understood.

脜.eEn: A gentle expression on the face. Formed from 𦣻 and 肉. Read like 柔.

面.e: 顔前也。从𦣻，象人面形。凡面之屬皆从面。
面.eEn: The front of the head. Formed from 𦣻 and depicting the shape of a human face. All characters in the 面 class are formed with 面.

靦.e: 面見也。从面、見，見亦聲。《詩》曰：“有靦面目。”
靦.eEn: The face being visible. Formed from 面 and 見, with 見 also indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Odes says: “With an unabashed face and eyes.”

薙.e: 除艸也。《明堂月令》曰：“季夏燒薙。”从艸雉聲。
薙.eEn: To remove grass. The Bright Hall’s Monthly Ordinances says: “In the last month of summer, burn the cut vegetation.” Formed from 艸, with 雉 indicating the pronunciation.

靨.eEn: A pleasing appearance. Formed from 面, with 厭 indicating the pronunciation.

丏.e: 不見也。象壅蔽之形。凡丏之屬皆从丏。
丏.eEn: Not visible. It depicts the shape of something blocked and concealed. All characters in the 丏 class are formed with 丏.

首.e: 𦣻同。古文𦣻也。巛象髪，謂之鬊，鬊卽巛也。凡𩠐之屬皆从𩠐。
首.eEn: The same as 𦣻. It is an ancient-script form of 𦣻. 巛 depicts hair, which is called 鬊; 鬊 is precisely what 巛 represents. All characters in the 𩠐 class are formed with 𩠐.

縣.eEn: To suspend or tie up. Formed from 系 holding 𥄉.

須.e: 面毛也。从頁从彡。凡須之屬皆从須。
須.eEn: Facial hair. Formed from 頁 and 彡. All characters in the 須 class are formed with 須.

頿.eEn: The hair above the mouth; a moustache. Formed from 須, with 此 indicating the pronunciation.

彡.e: 毛飾畫文也。象形。凡彡之屬皆从彡。
彡.eEn: Hair ornamentation and painted patterns. A pictograph. All characters in the 彡 class are formed with 彡.

形.eEn: The outward shape of a thing. Formed from 彡, with 幵 indicating the pronunciation.

修.eEn: To adorn. Formed from 彡, with 攸 indicating the pronunciation.

彰.e: 文彰也。从彡从章，章亦聲。
彰.eEn: A pattern being clearly displayed. Formed from 彡 and 章, with 章 also indicating the pronunciation.

彫.eEn: To carve patterns. Formed from 彡, with 周 indicating the pronunciation.

弱.e: 橈也。上象橈曲，彡象毛氂橈弱也。弱物并，故从二𢎥。
弱.eEn: To bend. The upper part depicts bending and curvature; 彡 depicts fine hairs bending softly. Weak things are paired, so it is formed from two instances of 𢎥.

彩.eEn: Decorative patterns. Formed from 彡, with 采 indicating the pronunciation.

彣.e: 㦽也。从彡从文。凡彣之屬皆从彣。
彣.eEn: Richly patterned. Formed from 彡 and 文. All characters in the 彣 class are formed with 彣.

彥.e: 美士有文，人所言也。从彣厂聲。
彥.eEn: An excellent man of refinement, spoken of by others. Formed from 彣, with 厂 indicating the pronunciation.

文.e: 錯畫也。象交文。凡文之屬皆从文。
文.eEn: Intersecting strokes. It depicts intersecting patterns. All characters in the 文 class are formed with 文.

斐.e: 分別文也。从文非聲。《易》曰：“君子豹變，其文斐也。”
斐.eEn: Distinctly differentiated patterns. Formed from 文, with 非 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Changes says: “The noble person changes like a leopard; his markings are distinct.”

辬.eEn: A mottled pattern. Formed from 文, with 辡 indicating the pronunciation.

髟.e: 長髮猋猋也。从長从彡。凡髟之屬皆从髟。
髟.eEn: Long hair streaming out. Formed from 長 and 彡. All characters in the 髟 class are formed with 髟.

蔪.e: 艸相蔪苞也。从艸斬聲。《書》曰：“艸木蔪苞。”
蔪.eEn: Plants growing together in luxuriant clusters. Formed from 艸, with 斬 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Documents says: “Grasses and trees grow in luxuriant clusters.”

髮.eEn: Roots. Formed from 髟, with 犮 indicating the pronunciation.

鬢.eEn: Hair along the cheeks. Formed from 髟, with 賓 indicating the pronunciation.

鬗.e: 髮長也。从髟㒼聲。讀若蔓。
鬗.eEn: Long hair. Formed from 髟, with 㒼 indicating the pronunciation. Read like 蔓.

鬈.e: 髮好也。从髟卷聲。《詩》曰：“其人美且鬈。”
鬈.eEn: Beautiful hair. Formed from 髟, with 卷 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Odes says: “That man is handsome and has beautiful hair.”

髦.eEn: Hair. Formed from 髟 and 毛.

茀.e: 道多艸，不可行。从艸弗聲。
茀.eEn: A road so overgrown with grass that it cannot be traveled. Formed from 艸, with 弗 indicating the pronunciation.

鬋.eEn: The appearance of a woman’s hair hanging down at the temples. Formed from 髟, with 前 indicating the pronunciation.

鬑.e: 鬋也。一曰長皃。从髟兼聲。讀若慊。
鬑.eEn: Hair hanging down at the temples. Another meaning is a long appearance. Formed from 髟, with 兼 indicating the pronunciation. Read like 慊.

鬄.eEn: Added hair; a hairpiece. Formed from 髟, with 易 indicating the pronunciation.

髲.eEn: Added hair; a hairpiece. Formed from 髟, with 皮 indicating the pronunciation.

髺.eEn: To bind up the hair neatly. Formed from 髟, with 𠯑 indicating the pronunciation.

苾.eEn: Fragrant. Formed from 艸, with 必 indicating the pronunciation.

鬕.eEn: An ornament made by tying a band. Formed from 髟, with 莫 indicating the pronunciation.

鬣.eEn: Hair standing out like a mane. Formed from 髟, with 巤 indicating the pronunciation.

髴.eEn: To resemble; to seem like. Formed from 髟, with 弗 indicating the pronunciation.

髶.eEn: Disordered hair. Formed from 髟, with an abbreviated form of 茸 indicating the pronunciation.

鬌.eEn: Hair falling away. Formed from 髟 and an abbreviated form of 隋.

鬊.eEn: Hair at the temples and on the head. Formed from 髟, with 春 indicating the pronunciation.

蔎.eEn: A fragrant plant. Formed from 艸, with 設 indicating the pronunciation.

鬝.eEn: Bald at the temples. Formed from 髟, with 閒 indicating the pronunciation.

髡.eEn: To shave off the hair. Formed from 髟, with 兀 indicating the pronunciation.

鬀.e: 𩮜髮也。从髟弟聲。大人曰髡，小人曰鬀，盡及身毛曰𩮜。
鬀.eEn: To shave off the hair. Formed from 髟, with 弟 indicating the pronunciation. For adults this is called 髡; for children it is called 鬀. Removing all hair, including body hair, is called 𩮜.

髽.e: 喪結。《禮》：女子髽衰，弔則不髽。魯臧武仲與齊戰于狐鮐，魯人迎喪者，始髽。从髟坐聲。
髽.eEn: A mourning hair-knot. The Rites states: “Women wear the mourning hair-knot and mourning garments; when merely offering condolences, they do not wear the mourning hair-knot.” When Zang Wuzhong of Lu fought against Qi at Hutai, the people of Lu who went out to receive the dead first adopted this hairstyle. Formed from 髟, with 坐 indicating the pronunciation.

鬐.eEn: A horse’s mane. Formed from 髟, with 耆 indicating the pronunciation.

髫.eEn: A young child’s hanging hair-knot. Formed from 髟, with 召 indicating the pronunciation.

髻.e: 緫髮也。从髟吉聲。古通用結。
髻.eEn: To gather up the hair. Formed from 髟, with 吉 indicating the pronunciation. In ancient usage, 結 was commonly used interchangeably with it.

芳.eEn: A fragrant plant. Formed from 艸, with 方 indicating the pronunciation.

鬟.e: 緫髮也。从髟睘聲。案：古婦人首飾，琢玉爲兩環。此二字皆後人所加。
鬟.eEn: To gather up the hair. Formed from 髟, with 睘 indicating the pronunciation. Note: an ancient women’s head ornament consisted of jade carved into two rings. These two characters were both added by later hands.

后.e: 繼體君也。象人之形。施令以告四方，故厂之。从一、口。發號者，君后也。凡后之屬皆从后。
后.eEn: A ruler who succeeds to the sovereign position. It depicts a human figure. The ruler issues commands to inform the four quarters, hence the 厂 form. Formed from 一 and 口. The one who proclaims commands is the sovereign. All characters in the 后 class are formed with 后.

司.e: 臣司事於外者。从反后。凡司之屬皆从司。
司.eEn: A minister who administers affairs outside. Formed from a reversed 后. All characters in the 司 class are formed with 司.

詞.e: 意内而言外也。从司从言。
詞.eEn: Meaning within, expressed outwardly in words. Formed from 司 and 言.

卮.e: 圜器也。一名觛。所以節飲食。象人，卪在其下也。《易》曰：“君子節飲食。”凡巵之屬皆从巵。
卮.eEn: A round vessel, also called 觛, used to regulate eating and drinking. It depicts a person, with 卪 below. The Book of Changes says: “The noble person regulates eating and drinking.” All characters in the 巵 class are formed with 巵.

卩.e: 瑞信也。守國者用玉卪，守都鄙者用角卪，使山邦者用虎卪，士邦者用人卪，澤邦者用龍卪，門關者用符卪，貨賄用璽卪，道路用旌卪。象相合之形。凡卪之屬皆从卪。
卩.eEn: A credential serving as a token of trust. Those guarding states use jade tallies; those guarding cities and outlying districts use horn tallies; envoys to mountain states use tiger tallies; those to open-country states use human-figure tallies; those to marsh states use dragon tallies. Gates and passes use matching tallies; trade in goods uses seal tallies; roads use banner tallies. It depicts shapes fitting together. All characters in the 卪 class are formed with 卪.

令.eEn: To issue commands. Formed from 亼 and 卪.

蕡.eEn: A mixture of fragrant plants. Formed from 艸, with 賁 indicating the pronunciation.

卶.e: 有大度也。从卪多聲。讀若侈。
卶.eEn: To have great magnanimity. Formed from 卪, with 多 indicating the pronunciation. Read like 侈.

卲.eEn: High. Formed from 卪, with 召 indicating the pronunciation.

厄.e: 科厄，木節也。从卪厂聲。賈侍中說，以爲厄，裹也。一曰厄，蓋也。
厄.eEn: A knot in wood, as in the expression 科厄. Formed from 卪, with 厂 indicating the pronunciation. Palace Attendant Jia explains 厄 as “to wrap.” Another meaning is “to cover.”

厀.eEn: The joint at the upper end of the shin; the knee. Formed from 卪, with 桼 indicating the pronunciation.

卷.eEn: The bending of the knee. Formed from 卪, with 𢍏 indicating the pronunciation.

卻.eEn: To restrain desires. Formed from 卪, with 谷 indicating the pronunciation.

卸.e: 舍車解馬也。从卪、止、午。讀若汝南人寫書之寫。
卸.eEn: To put away the carriage and unharness the horses. Formed from 卪, 止, and 午. Read like 寫 in the Runan people’s expression 寫書, “to write a document.”

藥.eEn: Plants used to treat illness. Formed from 艸, with 樂 indicating the pronunciation.

印.e: 執政所持信也。从爪从卪。凡印之屬皆从印。
印.eEn: A token of authority held by one who governs. Formed from 爪 and 卪. All characters in the 印 class are formed with 印.

色.e: 顔气也。从人从卪。凡色之屬皆从色。
色.eEn: The expression of the face. Formed from 人 and 卪. All characters in the 色 class are formed with 色.

艴.e: 色艴如也。从色弗聲。《論語》曰：“色艴如也。”
艴.eEn: An agitated expression. Formed from 色, with 弗 indicating the pronunciation. The Analects says: “His expression became agitated.”

艵.eEn: A pale blue color. Formed from 色, with 并 indicating the pronunciation.

辟.e: 法也。从卩从辛，節制其辠也；从口，用法者也。凡辟之屬皆从辟。
辟.eEn: Law. Formed from 卩 and 辛, representing the regulation of offenses; also from 口, representing one who administers the law. All characters in the 辟 class are formed with 辟.

勹.e: 裹也。象人曲形，有所包裹。凡勹之屬皆从勹。
勹.eEn: To wrap. It depicts a person bending, with something enclosed and wrapped. All characters in the 勹 class are formed with 勹.

匍.eEn: To move on the hands. Formed from 勹, with 甫 indicating the pronunciation.

匐.eEn: To lie prostrate on the ground. Formed from 勹, with 畐 indicating the pronunciation.

匊.eEn: What is held in the hands is called 匊. Formed from 勹 and 米.

勻.eEn: Few; little. Formed from 勹 and 二.

勼.eEn: To gather. Formed from 勹, with 九 indicating the pronunciation. Read like 鳩.

旬.eEn: To go all the way around. Ten days make a 旬. Formed from 勹 and 日.

勽.eEn: To cover. Formed from 勹 covering 人.

蓆.eEn: Broad and abundant. Formed from 艸, with 席 indicating the pronunciation.

匈.eEn: A sound. Formed from 勹, with 凶 indicating the pronunciation.

匌.eEn: To surround. Formed from 勹 and 合, with 合 also indicating the pronunciation.

冢.eEn: A high burial mound. Formed from 勹, with 豖 indicating the pronunciation.

包.e: 象人褢妊，巳在中，象子未成形也。元气起於子。子，人所生也。男左行三十，女右行二十，俱立於巳，爲夫婦。褢妊於巳，巳爲子，十月而生。男起巳至寅，女起巳至申。故男秊始寅，女秊始申也。凡包之屬皆从包。
包.eEn: It depicts a pregnant person, with 巳 inside representing a child whose form is not yet complete. Primal vital energy arises at 子. A child, 子, is what a human being gives birth to. The male proceeds leftward through thirty, and the female rightward through twenty; both stand at 巳 and become husband and wife. Pregnancy begins at 巳; 巳 represents the child, which is born after ten months. The male starts from 巳 and reaches 寅; the female starts from 巳 and reaches 申. Thus the male's years begin at 寅, and the female's years begin at 申. All characters in the 包 class are formed with 包.

胞.eEn: The wrapping in which a child is born. Formed from 肉 and 包.

匏.e: 瓠也。从包，从夸聲。包，取其可包藏物也。
匏.eEn: A gourd. Formed from 包, with 夸 indicating the pronunciation. 包 is used because a gourd can enclose and store things.

茍.e: 自急敕也。从羊省，从包省。从口，口猶愼言也。从羊，羊與義、善、美同意。凡茍之屬皆从茍。
茍.eEn: To urge and admonish oneself. Formed from abbreviated forms of 羊 and 包, and from 口. 口 conveys being cautious in speech. 羊 has the same significance here as in 義, 善, and 美. All characters in the 茍 class are formed with 茍.

芟.eEn: To cut grass. Formed from 艸 and 殳.

敬.eEn: To be solemn and respectful. Formed from 攴 and 茍.

鬼.e: 人所歸爲鬼。从人，象鬼頭。鬼陰气賊害，从厶。凡鬼之屬皆从鬼。
鬼.eEn: What a person returns to becomes a ghost. Formed from 人, with a depiction of a ghost's head. A ghost's yin energy injures and harms, so the character includes 厶. All characters in the 鬼 class are formed with 鬼.

魂.eEn: Yang vital energy. Formed from 鬼, with 云 indicating the pronunciation.

魄.eEn: The yin spirit. Formed from 鬼, with 白 indicating the pronunciation.

魖.eEn: A spirit that causes depletion. Formed from 鬼, with 虚 indicating the pronunciation.

魃.e: 旱鬼也。从鬼犮聲。《周禮》有赤魃氏，除牆屋之物也。《詩》曰：“旱魃爲虐。”
魃.eEn: A drought ghost. Formed from 鬼, with 犮 indicating the pronunciation. The Rites of Zhou has an official called 赤魃氏, who removes creatures from walls and roofs. The Book of Odes says: “The drought ghost wreaks havoc.”

鬽.e: 老精物也。从鬼、彡。彡，鬼毛。
鬽.eEn: An aged supernatural being. Formed from 鬼 and 彡. 彡 represents the ghost's hair.

鬾.e: 鬼服也。一曰小兒鬼。从鬼支聲。《韓詩傳》曰：“鄭交甫逢二女，鬾服。”
鬾.eEn: A ghost's clothing. Another explanation is a child ghost. Formed from 鬼, with 支 indicating the pronunciation. The Commentary on the Han Tradition of the Odes says: “Zheng Jiaofu encountered two women wearing ghostly garments.”

禖.eEn: A sacrifice. Formed from 示, with 某 indicating the pronunciation.

荐.eEn: A mat laid underneath. Formed from 艸, with 存 indicating the pronunciation.

醜.eEn: Loathsome. Formed from 鬼, with 酉 indicating the pronunciation.

魋.eEn: A supernatural beast. Formed from 鬼, with 隹 indicating the pronunciation.

魑.eEn: A kind of ghost. Formed from 鬼 and 离, with 离 also indicating the pronunciation.

魔.eEn: A ghost. Formed from 鬼, with 麻 indicating the pronunciation.

藉.e: 祭藉也。一曰艸不編，狼藉。从艸耤聲。
藉.eEn: A mat used in sacrifices. Another explanation is grass that has not been woven together, lying scattered in disorder. Formed from 艸, with 耤 indicating the pronunciation.

魘.eEn: To be frightened in a dream. Formed from 鬼, with 厭 indicating the pronunciation.

甶.e: 鬼頭也。象形。凡甶之屬皆从甶。
甶.eEn: A ghost's head. A pictograph. All characters in the 甶 class are formed with 甶.

畏.e: 惡也。从甶，虎省。鬼頭而虎爪，可畏也。
畏.eEn: To dislike. Formed from 甶 and an abbreviated form of 虎. With a ghost's head and a tiger's claws, it is fearsome.

禺.e: 母猴屬。頭似鬼。从甶从禸。
禺.eEn: A kind of macaque. Its head resembles a ghost's. Formed from 甶 and 禸.

厶.e: 姦衺也。韓非曰：“蒼頡作字，自營爲厶。”凡厶之屬皆从厶。
厶.eEn: Wicked and perverse. Han Fei says: “When Cangjie created characters, acting for one's own interests was represented by 厶.” All characters in the 厶 class are formed with 厶.

篡.e: 屰而奪取曰篡。从厶算聲。
篡.eEn: To seize something in defiance of rightful order is called 篡. Formed from 厶, with 算 indicating the pronunciation.

嵬.e: 高不平也。从山鬼聲。凡嵬之屬皆从嵬。
嵬.eEn: High and uneven. Formed from 山, with 鬼 indicating the pronunciation. All characters in the 嵬 class are formed with 嵬.

巍.eEn: High. Formed from 嵬, with 委 indicating the pronunciation.

山.e: 宣也。宣气𢿱，生萬物，有石而高。象形。凡山之屬皆从山。
山.eEn: To spread forth: it spreads and disperses vital energy, bringing forth the myriad things. It has rocks and rises high. A pictograph. All characters in the 山 class are formed with 山.

蒩.e: 茅藉也。从艸租聲。《禮》曰：“封諸侯以土，蒩以白茅。”
蒩.eEn: A mat of cogon grass. Formed from 艸, with 租 indicating the pronunciation. The Rites says: “In enfeoffing the feudal lords, earth is bestowed, with white cogon grass laid beneath it.”

嶽.e: 東，岱；南，靃；西，華；北，恆；中，泰室。王者之所以巡狩所至。从山獄聲。
嶽.eEn: In the east, 岱; in the south, 靃; in the west, 華; in the north, 恆; in the center, 泰室. These are the places reached by the king on his inspection tours. Formed from 山, with 獄 indicating the pronunciation.

岱.eEn: Mount Tai. Formed from 山, with 代 indicating the pronunciation.

峱.e: 山，在齊地。从山狃聲。《詩》曰：“遭我于峱之間兮。”
峱.eEn: A mountain in the territory of Qi. Formed from 山, with 狃 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Odes says: “You met me among the slopes of Nao.”

嶧.e: 葛嶧山，在東海下邳。从山睪聲。《夏書》曰：“嶧陽孤桐。”
嶧.eEn: Mount 葛嶧, in Xiapi in Donghai. Formed from 山, with 睪 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Xia says: “The solitary tong tree on the sunny side of Yi.”

嵎.e: 封嵎之山，在吳楚之閒，汪芒之國。从山禺聲。
嵎.eEn: Mount 封嵎, between Wu and Chu, in the state of Wangmang. Formed from 山, with 禺 indicating the pronunciation.

嶷.e: 九嶷山，舜所葬，在零陵營道。从山疑聲。
嶷.eEn: Mount 九嶷, where Shun was buried, in Yingdao in Lingling. Formed from 山, with 疑 indicating the pronunciation.

巀.e: 巀𡾦山，在馮翊池陽。从山𢧵聲。
巀.eEn: Mount 巀𡾦, in Chiyang in Fengyi. Formed from 山, with 𢧵 indicating the pronunciation.

蕝.e: 朝會束茅表位曰蕝。从艸絕聲。《春秋國語》曰：“致茅蕝，表坐。”
蕝.eEn: Bundles of cogon grass used to mark positions at court assemblies are called 蕝. Formed from 艸, with 絕 indicating the pronunciation. The Discourses of the States of the Spring and Autumn period says: “They set out bundles of cogon grass to mark the seating positions.”

崞.eEn: A mountain in Yanmen. Formed from 山, with 𩫖 indicating the pronunciation.

崵.e: 崵山，在遼西。从山昜聲。一曰嵎鐵崵谷也。
崵.eEn: Mount 崵, in Liaoxi. Formed from 山, with 昜 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation identifies it as 嵎鐵崵 Valley.

岵.e: 山有草木也。从山古聲。《詩》曰：“陟彼岵兮。”
岵.eEn: A mountain with grass and trees. Formed from 山, with 古 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Odes says: “I climb that wooded mountain.”

屺.e: 山無草木也。从山己聲。《詩》曰：“陟彼屺兮。”
屺.eEn: A mountain without grass or trees. Formed from 山, with 己 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Odes says: “I climb that bare mountain.”

嶨.e: 山多大石也。从山，學省聲。
嶨.eEn: A mountain with many large rocks. Formed from 山, with an abbreviated form of 學 indicating the pronunciation.

嶅.eEn: A mountain with many small rocks. Formed from 山, with 敖 indicating the pronunciation.

岨.e: 石戴土也。从山且聲。《詩》曰：“陟彼岨矣。”
岨.eEn: Rock bearing earth on top. Formed from 山, with 且 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Odes says: “I climb that rocky height.”

岡.eEn: The backbone of a mountain. Formed from 山, with 网 indicating the pronunciation.

茨.eEn: To roof a house with cogon grass or reeds. Formed from 艸, with 次 indicating the pronunciation.

岑.eEn: A mountain that is small but high. Formed from 山, with 今 indicating the pronunciation.

崟.eEn: The towering height of a mountain. Formed from 山, with 金 indicating the pronunciation.

崒.eEn: Precipitously high. Formed from 山, with 卒 indicating the pronunciation.

巒.eEn: A mountain that is small and pointed. Formed from 山, with 䜌 indicating the pronunciation.

密.eEn: A mountain shaped like a hall. Formed from 山, with 宓 indicating the pronunciation.

岫.eEn: A cave in a mountain. Formed from 山, with 由 indicating the pronunciation.

嶞.e: 山之墮墮者。从山，从憜省聲。讀若相推落之憜。
嶞.eEn: A mountain that slopes downward. Formed from 山, with an abbreviated form of 憜 indicating the pronunciation. Read like 憜 in the sense of pushing one another down.

嶘.eEn: Especially high. Formed from 山, with 棧 indicating the pronunciation.

崛.eEn: A mountain that is short but rises high. Formed from 山, with 屈 indicating the pronunciation.

葺.eEn: To thatch. Formed from 艸, with 咠 indicating the pronunciation.

峯.eEn: The summit of a mountain. Formed from 山, with 夆 indicating the pronunciation.

巖.eEn: A steep bank or cliff. Formed from 山, with 嚴 indicating the pronunciation.

峼.e: 山皃。一曰山名。从山告聲。
峼.eEn: The appearance of a mountain. Another explanation is the name of a mountain. Formed from 山, with 告 indicating the pronunciation.

嵯.eEn: The appearance of a mountain. Formed from 山, with 𢀩 indicating the pronunciation.

峨.eEn: The towering appearance expressed by 嵯峨. Formed from 山, with 我 indicating the pronunciation.

葢.eEn: A thatch covering. Formed from 艸, with 盇 indicating the pronunciation.

崝.eEn: Lofty, as expressed by 嶸. Formed from 山, with 青 indicating the pronunciation.

嶸.eEn: The lofty appearance expressed by 崝嶸. Formed from 山, with 榮 indicating the pronunciation.

岪.eEn: A path along the flank of a mountain. Formed from 山, with 弗 indicating the pronunciation.

嵍.eEn: The name of a mountain. Formed from 山, with 敄 indicating the pronunciation.

嶢.eEn: 焦嶢 describes the lofty appearance of a mountain. Formed from 山, with 堯 indicating the pronunciation.

嵏.e: 九嵏山，在馮翊谷口。从山㚇聲。
嵏.eEn: Mount 九嵏, in Gukou in Fengyi. Formed from 山, with 㚇 indicating the pronunciation.

苫.eEn: A covering. Formed from 艸, with 占 indicating the pronunciation.

崇.eEn: Lofty and high. Formed from 山, with 宗 indicating the pronunciation.

崔.eEn: Great and high. Formed from 山, with 隹 indicating the pronunciation.

嶙.eEn: 嶙峋 describes the appearance of deep cliffs. Formed from 山, with 粦 indicating the pronunciation.

峋.eEn: The appearance expressed by 嶙峋. Formed from 山, with 旬 indicating the pronunciation.

岌.eEn: The lofty appearance of a mountain. Formed from 山, with 及 indicating the pronunciation.

嶠.e: 山銳而高也。从山喬聲。古通用喬。
嶠.eEn: A mountain that is pointed and high. Formed from 山, with 喬 indicating the pronunciation. In ancient usage, 喬 was used interchangeably with it.

嵌.eEn: The deeply recessed appearance of a mountain. Formed from 山, with an abbreviated form of 歁 indicating the pronunciation.

嶼.eEn: An island. Formed from 山, with 與 indicating the pronunciation.

嶺.eEn: A mountain path. Formed from 山, with 領 indicating the pronunciation.

嵐.eEn: The name of a mountain. Formed from 山, with an abbreviated form of 葻 indicating the pronunciation.

嵩.e: 中岳，嵩高山也。从山从高，亦从松。韋昭《國語》注云：“古通用崇字。”
嵩.eEn: The Central Sacred Peak, Mount Songgao. Formed from 山 and 高; it is also formed with 松. Wei Zhao's commentary on the Discourses of the States says: “In ancient usage, the character 崇 was used interchangeably with it.”

崑.e: 崑崙，山名。从山昆聲。《漢書》楊雄文通用昆侖。
崑.eEn: 崑崙, the name of a mountain. Formed from 山, with 昆 indicating the pronunciation. In the Book of Han, Yang Xiong's writings use 昆侖 interchangeably with 崑崙.

崙.eEn: As in 崑崙. Formed from 山, with 侖 indicating the pronunciation.

嵇.e: 山名。从山，稽省聲。奚氏避難特造此字，非古。
嵇.eEn: The name of a mountain. Formed from 山, with an abbreviated form of 稽 indicating the pronunciation. The Xi clan specially created this character while fleeing calamity; it is not ancient.

屾.e: 二山也。凡屾之屬皆从屾。
屾.eEn: Two mountains. All characters in the 屾 class are formed with 屾.

嵞.e: 會稽山。一曰九江當嵞也。民以辛壬癸甲之日嫁娶。从屾余聲。《虞書》曰：“予娶嵞山。”
嵞.eEn: Mount Kuaiji. Another account identifies it as Dangtu in Jiujiang. The people marry on days designated 辛, 壬, 癸, and 甲. Formed from 屾, with 余 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Yu says: “I married at Mount Tu.”

屵.e: 岸高也。从山、厂，厂亦聲。凡屵之屬皆从屵。
屵.eEn: A high bank. Formed from 山 and 厂, with 厂 also indicating the pronunciation. All characters in the 屵 class are formed with 屵.

岸.eEn: A high bank beside water. Formed from 屵, with 干 indicating the pronunciation.

崖.eEn: A high edge. Formed from 屵, with 圭 indicating the pronunciation.

嵟.eEn: High. Formed from 屵, with 隹 indicating the pronunciation.

嶏.eEn: The sound of a collapse. Formed from 屵, with 配 indicating the pronunciation. Read like 費.

广.e: 因广爲屋，象對剌高屋之形。凡广之屬皆从广。讀若儼然之儼。
广.eEn: Making a dwelling by relying on a sheltering overhang. It depicts the form of a tall building with opposing sloping sides. All characters in the 广 class are formed with 广. Read like 儼 in 儼然, “solemn.”

府.eEn: A repository for documents. Formed from 广, with 付 indicating the pronunciation.

廱.e: 天子饗飲辟廱。从广雝聲。
廱.eEn: The Biyong, where the Son of Heaven holds ceremonial feasts and drinking gatherings. Formed from 广, with 雝 indicating the pronunciation.

庠.e: 禮官養老。夏曰校，殷曰庠，周曰序。从广羊聲。
庠.eEn: A place where ritual officials care for the elderly. Under the Xia it was called 校, under the Yin 庠, and under the Zhou 序. Formed from 广, with 羊 indicating the pronunciation.

廬.e: 寄也。秋冬去，春夏居。从广盧聲。
廬.eEn: A temporary lodging. People leave it in autumn and winter and occupy it in spring and summer. Formed from 广, with 盧 indicating the pronunciation.

庭.eEn: The courtyard within a palace. Formed from 广, with 廷 indicating the pronunciation.

庉.eEn: The wall of a multistory building. Formed from 广, with 屯 indicating the pronunciation.

藩.eEn: A screen or barrier. Formed from 艸, with 潘 indicating the pronunciation.

庌.e: 廡也。从广牙聲。《周禮》曰：“夏庌馬。”
庌.eEn: A covered gallery. Formed from 广, with 牙 indicating the pronunciation. The Rites of Zhou says: “In summer, shelter the horses under a covered gallery.”

廡.eEn: The buildings surrounding the space below the main hall. Formed from 广, with 無 indicating the pronunciation.

庖.eEn: A kitchen. Formed from 广, with 包 indicating the pronunciation.

廚.eEn: A building used as a kitchen. Formed from 广, with 尌 indicating the pronunciation.

庫.eEn: A storehouse for war chariots. Formed from 車 beneath 广.

廏.e: 馬舍也。从广㲃聲。《周禮》曰：“馬有二百十四匹爲廏，廏有僕夫。”
廏.eEn: A stable for horses. Formed from 广, with 㲃 indicating the pronunciation. The Rites of Zhou says: “Two hundred and fourteen horses constitute a stable; each stable has a groom.”

序.eEn: The eastern and western walls. Formed from 广, with 予 indicating the pronunciation.

廦.eEn: A wall. Formed from 广, with 辟 indicating the pronunciation.

廣.eEn: A large building serving as a palace hall. Formed from 广, with 黃 indicating the pronunciation.

菹.eEn: Vegetables preserved in vinegar. Formed from 艸, with 沮 indicating the pronunciation.

廥.eEn: A storehouse for fodder and straw. Formed from 广, with 會 indicating the pronunciation.

庾.e: 水槽倉也。从广臾聲。一曰倉無屋者。
庾.eEn: A granary by a water channel. Formed from 广, with 臾 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation is a granary without a roof.

庰.eEn: To screen or conceal. Formed from 广, with 幷 indicating the pronunciation.

廁.eEn: A privy. Formed from 广, with 則 indicating the pronunciation.

廛.e: 一畝半，一家之居。从广、里、八、土。
廛.eEn: One and a half mu of land, the dwelling place of one household. Formed from 广, 里, 八, and 土.

廉.eEn: A side or edge. Formed from 广, with 兼 indicating the pronunciation.

荃.eEn: Crisp mustard greens. Formed from 艸, with 全 indicating the pronunciation.

龐.eEn: A tall building. Formed from 广, with 龍 indicating the pronunciation.

底.e: 山居也。一曰下也。从广氐聲。
底.eEn: A mountain dwelling. Another explanation is “below.” Formed from 广, with 氐 indicating the pronunciation.

庢.eEn: To obstruct and stop. Formed from 广, with 至 indicating the pronunciation.

廮.e: 安止也。从广嬰聲。鉅鹿有廮陶縣。
廮.eEn: To settle peacefully. Formed from 广, with 嬰 indicating the pronunciation. There is a Yingtao County in Julu.

庳.e: 中伏舍。从广卑聲。一曰屋庳。或讀若逋。
庳.eEn: A dwelling whose middle is low. Formed from 广, with 卑 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation is a low building. Sometimes read like 逋.

庇.eEn: To shelter. Formed from 广, with 比 indicating the pronunciation.

庶.e: 屋下眾也。从广、炗。炗，古文光字。
庶.eEn: A multitude beneath a roof. Formed from 广 and 炗. 炗 is the ancient-script form of 光.

庤.eEn: To store things beneath a roof. Formed from 广, with 寺 indicating the pronunciation.

廙.eEn: A movable dwelling. Formed from 广, with 異 indicating the pronunciation.

廔.e: 屋麗廔也。从广婁聲。一曰穜也。
廔.eEn: The latticework of a house. Formed from 广, with 婁 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation is “late-ripening grain.”

廢.eEn: A building collapsing. Formed from 广, with 發 indicating the pronunciation.

庮.e: 久屋朽木。从广酉聲。《周禮》曰：“牛夜鳴則𢉷。”臭如朽木。
庮.eEn: Rotten timber in an old building. Formed from 广, with 酉 indicating the pronunciation. The Rites of Zhou says: “If an ox lows at night, its flesh is foul-smelling.” Its odor is like rotten wood.

廑.eEn: A small, inferior dwelling. Formed from 广, with 堇 indicating the pronunciation.

廟.eEn: The expression of reverence for one's ancestors. Formed from 广, with 朝 indicating the pronunciation.

廞.e: 陳輿服於庭也。从广欽聲。讀若歆。
廞.eEn: To display carriages and ceremonial garments in the courtyard. Formed from 广, with 欽 indicating the pronunciation. Read like 歆.

蘫.eEn: Pickled melon. Formed from 艸, with 監 indicating the pronunciation.

廫.eEn: Empty and vacant. Formed from 广, with 膠 indicating the pronunciation.

廈.eEn: A building. Formed from 广, with 夏 indicating the pronunciation.

廊.e: 東西序也。从广郎聲。《漢書》通用郎。
廊.eEn: The eastern and western side galleries. Formed from 广, with 郎 indicating the pronunciation. In the Book of Han, 郎 is used interchangeably with this character.

廂.eEn: A gallery. Formed from 广, with 相 indicating the pronunciation.

庪.eEn: Sacrificing to a mountain is called 庪縣. Formed from 广, with 技 indicating the pronunciation.

庱.eEn: A place name. Formed from 广; the remaining formation is unclear.

廖.e: 人姓。从广，未詳。當是省廫字尔。
廖.eEn: A surname. Formed from 广; the remaining formation is unclear. It is presumably simply an abbreviated form of 廫.

厂.e: 山石之厓巖，人可居。象形。凡厂之屬皆从厂。
厂.eEn: A rocky mountain cliff or recess where people can dwell. A pictograph. All characters in the 厂 class are formed with 厂.

厓.eEn: The edge of a mountain. Formed from 厂, with 圭 indicating the pronunciation.

厜.eEn: 厜㕒 means a mountain summit. Formed from 厂, with 垂 indicating the pronunciation.

厬.e: 仄出泉也。从厂晷聲。讀若軌。
厬.eEn: A spring issuing sideways. Formed from 厂, with 晷 indicating the pronunciation. Read like 軌.

厎.eEn: A soft stone. Formed from 厂, with 氐 indicating the pronunciation.

厥.eEn: To launch stones. Formed from 厂, with 欮 indicating the pronunciation.

厲.eEn: A dry stone. Formed from 厂, with an abbreviated form of 蠆 indicating the pronunciation.

厱.e: 厱諸，治玉石也。从厂僉聲。讀若藍。
厱.eEn: 厱諸 is a stone used to work jade. Formed from 厂, with 僉 indicating the pronunciation. Read like 藍.

厤.eEn: To put in order. Formed from 厂, with 秝 indicating the pronunciation.

厗.eEn: 唐厗 is a kind of stone. Formed from 厂, with an abbreviated form of 屖 indicating the pronunciation.

厝.e: 厲石也。从厂㫺聲。《詩》曰：“他山之石，可以爲𠪞。”
厝.eEn: A whetstone. Formed from 厂, with 㫺 indicating the pronunciation. The Odes says: “Stones from another mountain can serve as whetstones.”

厖.eEn: A large stone. Formed from 厂, with 尨 indicating the pronunciation.

仄.eEn: To lean or tilt to one side. Formed from 人 beneath 厂.

厞.eEn: Hidden. Formed from 厂, with 非 indicating the pronunciation.

厭.e: 笮也。从厂猒聲。一曰合也。
厭.eEn: To press down. Formed from 厂, with 猒 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation is “to join together.”

厃.e: 仰也。从人在厂上。一曰屋梠也，秦謂之桷，齊謂之厃。
厃.eEn: To look upward. Formed from 人 above 厂. Another explanation is the timber along a roof's edge: in Qin it is called 桷, and in Qi it is called 厃.

丸.e: 圜，傾側而轉者。从反仄。凡丸之屬皆从丸。
丸.eEn: Something round that rolls as it tips to one side. Formed from a reversed 仄. All characters in the 丸 class are formed with 丸.

危.e: 在高而懼也。从厃，自卪止之。凡危之屬皆从危。
危.eEn: To be afraid while in a high place. Formed from 厃, with 卪 holding oneself back. All characters in the 危 class are formed with 危.

石.e: 山石也。在厂之下；囗，象形。凡石之屬皆从石。
石.eEn: Mountain rock. It is beneath 厂; 囗 represents the rock. A pictograph. All characters in the 石 class are formed with 石.

磺.e: 銅鐵樸石也。从石黃聲。讀若穬。
磺.eEn: Unworked stone containing copper or iron. Formed from 石, with 黃 indicating the pronunciation. Read like 穬.

碭.eEn: Patterned stone. Formed from 石, with 昜 indicating the pronunciation.

碝.eEn: A stone ranking next to jade. Formed from 石, with 耎 indicating the pronunciation.

砮.e: 石，可以爲矢鏃。从石奴聲。《夏書》曰：“梁州貢砮丹。”《春秋國語》曰：“肅愼氏貢楛矢石砮。”
砮.eEn: A stone that can be made into arrowheads. Formed from 石, with 奴 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Xia says: “Liangzhou presents arrowhead stone and cinnabar as tribute.” The Discourses of the States of the Spring and Autumn period says: “The Sushen people presented arrows of hu wood with stone arrowheads as tribute.”

礜.e: 毒石也。出漢中。从石與聲。
礜.eEn: A poisonous stone, found in Hanzhong. Formed from 石, with 與 indicating the pronunciation.

碣.e: 特立之石。東海有碣石山。从石曷聲。
碣.eEn: A stone standing alone. There is a Mount Jieshi in Donghai. Formed from 石, with 曷 indicating the pronunciation.

磏.e: 厲石也。一曰赤色。从石兼聲。讀若鎌。
磏.eEn: A whetstone. Another explanation specifies a red color. Formed from 石, with 兼 indicating the pronunciation. Read like 鎌.

碬.e: 厲石也。从石叚聲。《春秋傳》曰：“鄭公孫碬字子石。”
碬.eEn: A whetstone. Formed from 石, with 叚 indicating the pronunciation. The Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals says: “Gongsun Xia of Zheng had the courtesy name Zishi.”

礫.eEn: A small stone. Formed from 石, with 樂 indicating the pronunciation.

若.e: 擇菜也。从艸、右。右，手也。一曰杜若，香艸。
若.eEn: To select vegetables. Formed from 艸 and 右. 右 means a hand. Another explanation is 杜若, an aromatic herb.

磧.eEn: A stony islet or shoal in water. Formed from 石, with 責 indicating the pronunciation.

碑.eEn: An upright stone. Formed from 石, with 卑 indicating the pronunciation.

磒.e: 落也。从石員聲。《春秋傳》曰：“磒石于宋五。”
磒.eEn: To fall. Formed from 石, with 員 indicating the pronunciation. The Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals says: “Stones fell in Song—five of them.”

硞.eEn: The sound of stones. Formed from 石, with 告 indicating the pronunciation.

硠.eEn: The sound of stones. Formed from 石, with 良 indicating the pronunciation.

礐.eEn: The sound of stones. Formed from 石, with an abbreviated form of 學 indicating the pronunciation.

硈.e: 石堅也。从石吉聲。一曰突也。
硈.eEn: A stone being hard. Formed from 石, with 吉 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation is “to jut out.”

丄.e: 高也。此古文上，指事也。凡丄之屬皆从丄。
丄.eEn: High. This is the ancient-script form of 上. An indicative character. All characters in the 丄 class are formed with 丄.

祳.e: 社肉，盛以蜃，故謂之祳。天子所以親遺同姓。从示辰聲。《春秋傳》曰：“石尚來歸祳。”
祳.eEn: Meat from a sacrifice to the soil altar. It is placed in a large shell, 蜃, and is therefore called 祳. It is what the Son of Heaven personally sends as a gift to those sharing his surname. Formed from 示, with 辰 indicating the pronunciation. The Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals says: “Shi Shang came to deliver sacrificial meat.”

蓴.eEn: A clump of cattails. Formed from 艸, with 專 indicating the pronunciation.

磕.eEn: The sound of stones. Formed from 石, with 盍 indicating the pronunciation.

硻.eEn: That which remains hard. Formed from 石 and an abbreviated form of 堅.

磿.eEn: The sound of stones. Formed from 石, with 厤 indicating the pronunciation.

磛.eEn: 磛礹 is rock. Formed from 石, with 斬 indicating the pronunciation.

礹.eEn: A rocky mountain. Formed from 石, with 嚴 indicating the pronunciation.

礊.eEn: Hard. Formed from 石, with 毄 indicating the pronunciation.

确.eEn: Hard stone. Formed from 石, with 角 indicating the pronunciation.

磽.eEn: Hard stone. Formed from 石, with 堯 indicating the pronunciation.

硪.eEn: A rocky cliff. Formed from 石, with 我 indicating the pronunciation.

碞.e: 磛嵒也。从石、品。《周書》曰：“畏于民碞。”讀與巖同。
碞.eEn: Precipitous and craggy. Formed from 石 and 品. The Book of Zhou says: “Be wary of the people's dangerous heights.” Pronounced the same as 巖.

磬.e: 樂石也。从石、殸。象縣虡之形。殳，擊之也。古者母句氏作磬。
磬.eEn: A musical stone. Formed from 石 and 殸, depicting the shape of its suspension and supporting frame. 殳 represents striking it. In antiquity, Mother Gou made the musical stone.

礙.eEn: To stop or obstruct. Formed from 石, with 疑 indicating the pronunciation.

硩.e: 上摘巖空青、珊瑚墮之。从石折聲。《周禮》有硩蔟氏。
硩.eEn: To climb up and dislodge the mineral kongqing and coral from cliffs, making them fall. Formed from 石, with 折 indicating the pronunciation. The Rites of Zhou includes an official called the 硩蔟氏.

硟.eEn: To press silk fabric with a stone. Formed from 石, with 延 indicating the pronunciation.

碎.eEn: To grind or crush. Formed from 石, with 卒 indicating the pronunciation.

破.eEn: Stone breaking into pieces. Formed from 石, with 皮 indicating the pronunciation.

礱.e: 䃺也。从石龍聲。天子之桷，椓而礱之。
礱.eEn: To grind or polish. Formed from 石, with 龍 indicating the pronunciation. The Son of Heaven's square rafters are hewn and then polished.

研.eEn: To grind. Formed from 石, with 幵 indicating the pronunciation.

磑.e: 䃺也。从石豈聲。古者公輸班作磑。
磑.eEn: To grind. Formed from 石, with 豈 indicating the pronunciation. In antiquity, Gongshu Ban made the mill.

碓.eEn: To pound grain. Formed from 石, with 隹 indicating the pronunciation.

磻.eEn: A stone attached to a corded shooting arrow. Formed from 石, with 番 indicating the pronunciation.

硯.eEn: A smooth stone. Formed from 石, with 見 indicating the pronunciation.

砭.eEn: To pierce with a stone to treat illness. Formed from 石, with 乏 indicating the pronunciation.

砢.eEn: A mass or heap of stones, as in 磊砢. Formed from 石, with 可 indicating the pronunciation.

磊.eEn: Many stones. Formed from three instances of 石.

礪.e: 䃺也。从石厲聲。經典通用厲。
礪.eEn: To grind or sharpen. Formed from 石, with 厲 indicating the pronunciation. The canonical texts commonly use 厲 interchangeably for it.

莜.e: 艸田器。从艸，條省聲。《論語》曰：“以杖荷莜。”今作蓧。
莜.eEn: An implement for weeding fields. Formed from 艸, with an abbreviated form of 條 indicating the pronunciation. The Analects says: “He carried the weeding implement on his staff.” It is now written 蓧.

碏.e: 《左氏傳》：“衞大夫石碏。”《唐韻》云：敬也。从石，未詳。昔聲。
碏.eEn: The Zuo Commentary mentions “Shi Que, a grand officer of Wei.” The Tang Rhymes says it means “respectful.” Formed from 石, though the reason is not fully understood, with 昔 indicating the pronunciation.

磯.eEn: A large rock against which water dashes. Formed from 石, with 幾 indicating the pronunciation.

碌.eEn: The appearance of stone. Formed from 石, with 彔 indicating the pronunciation.

砧.eEn: A stone pounding block. Formed from 石, with 占 indicating the pronunciation.

砌.eEn: The masonry of steps. Formed from 石, with 切 indicating the pronunciation.

礩.eEn: A stone beneath a pillar. Formed from 石, with 質 indicating the pronunciation.

礎.eEn: A foundation stone beneath a pillar. Formed from 石, with 楚 indicating the pronunciation.

硾.eEn: To pound. Formed from 石, with 垂 indicating the pronunciation.

長.e: 久遠也。从兀从匕。兀者，高遠意也。久則變化。亾聲。纼者，倒亾也。凡長之屬皆从長。
長.eEn: Long-lasting or far-reaching. Formed from 兀 and 匕. 兀 conveys height and distance. With the passage of time, things change. 亾 indicates the pronunciation. 纼 is an inverted 亾. All characters in the 長 class are formed with 長.

萆.e: 雨衣。一曰衰衣。从艸卑聲。一曰萆藨，似烏韭。
萆.eEn: A rain garment. Another explanation: a straw raincoat. Formed from 艸, with 卑 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation: the plant called 萆藨, resembling crow's chives.

镾.eEn: Lasting a long time. Formed from 長, with 爾 indicating the pronunciation.

镻.eEn: A long, fiercely venomous snake. Formed from 長, with 失 indicating the pronunciation.

勿.e: 州里所建旗。象其柄，有三游。雜帛，幅半異。所以趣民，故遽，稱勿勿。凡勿之屬皆从勿。
勿.eEn: A flag erected in a district or village. It depicts its pole and has three streamers. It is made of mixed silks, with the two halves of each breadth differing. It is used to urge the people onward; hence haste is called 勿勿. All characters in the 勿 class are formed with 勿.

昜.e: 開也。从日、一、勿。一曰飛揚。一曰長也。一曰彊者眾皃。
昜.eEn: To open. Formed from 日, 一, and 勿. Another explanation: to fly upward. Another explanation: to grow or be long. Another explanation: the appearance of the strong being numerous.

冄.e: 毛冄冄也。象形。凡冄之屬皆从冄。
冄.eEn: The soft, drooping appearance of hair. A pictograph. All characters in the 冄 class are formed with 冄.

而.e: 頰毛也。象毛之形。《周禮》曰：“作其鱗之而。”凡而之屬皆从而。
而.eEn: Hair on the cheeks. It depicts the shape of hair. The Rites of Zhou says: “Make its scales and cheek hair.” All characters in the 而 class are formed with 而.

耏.eEn: A punishment for an offense not severe enough to warrant shaving the head. Formed from 而 and 彡.

豕.e: 彘也。竭其尾，故謂之豕。象毛足而後有尾。讀與豨同。(桉：今丗字，誤以豕爲彘，以彘爲豕。何以明之？爲啄琢从豕，蟸从彘。皆取其聲，以是明之。)凡豕之屬皆从豕。
豕.eEn: A pig. Because its tail is raised to its utmost, it is called 豕. It depicts the hair and feet, with a tail behind. Pronounced the same as 豨. (Note: in present-day writing, 豕 is mistakenly used for 彘, and 彘 for 豕. How can this be shown? 啄 and 琢 are formed with 豕, while 蟸 is formed with 彘. All take these components for their sound; this makes it clear.) All characters in the 豕 class are formed with 豕.

豬.e: 豕而三毛叢居者。从豕者聲。
豬.eEn: A pig whose bristles grow together in groups of three. Formed from 豕, with 者 indicating the pronunciation.

豰.eEn: A small piglet. Formed from 豕, with 𣪎 indicating the pronunciation.

豯.e: 生三月豚，腹豯豯皃也。从豕奚聲。
豯.eEn: A three-month-old piglet, with a plump-looking belly. Formed from 豕, with 奚 indicating the pronunciation.

豵.e: 生六月豚。从豕從聲。一曰一歲豵，尚叢聚也。
豵.eEn: A six-month-old piglet. Formed from 豕, with 從 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation: a one-year-old pig, still gathering in a group.

豝.e: 牝豕也。从豕巴聲。一曰一歲，能相把拏也。《詩》曰：“一發五豝。”
豝.eEn: A female pig. Formed from 豕, with 巴 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation: a one-year-old pig, able to grapple with others. The Odes says: “One shot at five sows.”

豣.e: 三歲豕，肩相及者。从豕幵聲。《詩》曰：“並驅从兩豣兮。”
豣.eEn: Three-year-old pigs whose shoulders reach the same height. Formed from 豕, with 幵 indicating the pronunciation. The Odes says: “Driving abreast, we pursue two three-year-old pigs.”

豶.eEn: A castrated pig. Formed from 豕, with 賁 indicating the pronunciation.

豭.eEn: A male pig. Formed from 豕, with 叚 indicating the pronunciation.

豛.e: 上谷名豬豭。从豕，役省聲。
豛.eEn: The name for a boar in Shanggu. Formed from 豕, with an abbreviated form of 役 indicating the pronunciation.

豤.eEn: To bite or gnaw. Formed from 豕, with 𥃩 indicating the pronunciation.

豷.e: 豕息也。从豕壹聲。《春秋傳》曰：“生敖及豷。”
豷.eEn: A pig's breathing. Formed from 豕, with 壹 indicating the pronunciation. The Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals says: “She bore Ao and Yi.”

苴.eEn: Grass placed inside footwear. Formed from 艸, with 且 indicating the pronunciation.

豧.eEn: A pig's breathing. Formed from 豕, with 甫 indicating the pronunciation.

豢.eEn: To raise pigs in a pen on grain. Formed from 豕, with 𢍏 indicating the pronunciation.

豠.eEn: A kind of pig. Formed from 豕, with 且 indicating the pronunciation.

豲.e: 逸也。从豕原聲。《周書》曰：“豲有爪而不敢以撅。”讀若桓。
豲.eEn: To escape. Formed from 豕, with 原 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Zhou says: “The 豲 has claws, yet dares not strike with them.” Pronounced like 桓.

豨.e: 豕走豨豨。从豕希聲。古有封豨脩虵之害。
豨.eEn: The running movement of a pig. Formed from 豕, with 希 indicating the pronunciation. In antiquity, there was the scourge of the great boar and the long serpent.

豖.e: 豕絆足行豖豖。从豕繫二足。
豖.eEn: The hobbling gait of a pig with its feet tethered. Formed from 豕 with two feet bound.

豦.e: 鬬相丮不解也。从豕、虍。豕、虍之鬬，不解也。讀若蘮蒘草之蘮。司馬相如說：豦，封豕之屬。一曰虎兩足舉。
豦.eEn: To grapple in a fight without breaking apart. Formed from 豕 and 虍: a pig and a tiger fighting without breaking apart. Pronounced like 蘮 in the plant name 蘮蒘. Sima Xiangru says: “豦 is a kind of great boar.” Another explanation: a tiger raising two feet.

豩.eEn: Two pigs. 豳 is formed with this component. Explanation missing in the source.

彑.e: 豕之頭。象其銳，而上見也。凡彑之屬皆从彑。讀若罽。
彑.eEn: A pig's head. It depicts its pointed shape as seen from above. All characters in the 彑 class are formed with 彑. Pronounced like 罽.

彘.e: 豕也。後蹏廢謂之彘。从彑矢聲；从二匕，彘足與鹿足同。
彘.eEn: A pig. One whose hind hooves are disabled is called 彘. Formed from 彑, with 矢 indicating the pronunciation; it also contains two instances of 匕, since a pig's feet are the same as a deer's.

豚.e: 小豕也。从彖省，象形。从又持肉，以給祠祀。凡豚之屬皆从豚。
豚.eEn: A small pig. Formed from an abbreviated 彖. A pictograph. It also contains 又 holding meat, to supply sacrificial rites. All characters in the 豚 class are formed with 豚.

蕢.eEn: A container made of grass. Formed from 艸, with 䝿 indicating the pronunciation.

豸.e: 獸長𦟝，行豸豸然，欲有所司殺形。凡豸之屬皆从豸。(司殺讀若伺候之伺。)
豸.eEn: A beast with a long spine, moving slowly as though watching for something to kill; the graph depicts this form. All characters in the 豸 class are formed with 豸. (司 in 司殺 is pronounced like 伺 in 伺候, “to watch or attend.”)

豹.eEn: An animal resembling a tiger, with circular markings. Formed from 豸, with 勺 indicating the pronunciation.

貙.eEn: The animal called 貙獌, resembling a wildcat. Formed from 豸, with 區 indicating the pronunciation.

貚.eEn: A kind of 貙. Formed from 豸, with 單 indicating the pronunciation.

貔.e: 豹屬，出貉國。从豸𣬉聲。《詩》曰：“獻其貔皮。”《周書》曰：“如虎如貔。”貔，猛獸。
貔.eEn: A kind of leopard, found in the country of Mo. Formed from 豸, with 𣬉 indicating the pronunciation. The Odes says: “Present their 貔 skins.” The Book of Zhou says: “Like tigers, like 貔.” The 貔 is a fierce beast.

豺.eEn: An animal of the wolf kind, with a dog's voice. Formed from 豸, with 才 indicating the pronunciation.

貐.e: 猰貐，似貙，虎爪，食人，迅走。从豸俞聲。
貐.eEn: The animal called 猰貐, resembling a 貙, with tiger's claws; it eats people and runs swiftly. Formed from 豸, with 俞 indicating the pronunciation.

貘.e: 似熊而黃黑色，出蜀中。从豸莫聲。
貘.eEn: An animal resembling a bear, yellow and black in color, found in Shu. Formed from 豸, with 莫 indicating the pronunciation.

貜.eEn: The animal called 纱玃. Formed from 豸, with 矍 indicating the pronunciation.

貀.e: 獸，無前足。从豸出聲。《漢律》：“能捕豺貀，購百錢。”
貀.eEn: A beast with no front feet. Formed from 豸, with 出 indicating the pronunciation. The Laws of Han states: “For anyone able to catch a jackal or a 貀, the reward is one hundred coins.”

貈.e: 似狐，善睡獸。从豸舟聲。《論語》曰：“狐貈之厚以居。”
貈.eEn: A beast resembling a fox, fond of sleeping. Formed from 豸, with 舟 indicating the pronunciation. The Analects says: “Thick fox and 貈 furs for sitting upon.”

豻.eEn: A wild dog of the northern Hu lands. Formed from 豸, with 干 indicating the pronunciation.

貂.e: 鼠屬。大而黃黑，出胡丁零國。从豸召聲。
貂.eEn: An animal of the rat kind, large and yellow-black, found in the Hu country of Dingling. Formed from 豸, with 召 indicating the pronunciation.

貉.e: 北方豸穜。从豸各聲。孔子曰：“貉之爲言惡也。”
貉.eEn: A northern kind of beast. Formed from 豸, with 各 indicating the pronunciation. Confucius said: “The word 貉 conveys the meaning ‘evil.’”

貆.eEn: An animal of the 貉 kind. Formed from 豸, with 亘 indicating the pronunciation.

貍.eEn: A beast that lies in wait, resembling a 貙. Formed from 豸, with 里 indicating the pronunciation.

貒.eEn: A beast. Formed from 豸, with 耑 indicating the pronunciation. Pronounced like 湍.

貛.eEn: A wild pig. Formed from 豸, with 雚 indicating the pronunciation.

祴.eEn: To perform the music called 祴 in the ancestral temple. Formed from 示, with 戒 indicating the pronunciation.

茵.eEn: A double mat for a carriage. Formed from 艸, with 因 indicating the pronunciation.

貁.eEn: An animal of the rat kind, adept at turning around. Formed from 豸, with 穴 indicating the pronunciation.

貓.eEn: An animal of the wildcat kind. Formed from 豸, with 苗 indicating the pronunciation.

易.e: 蜥易，蝘蜓，守宮也。象形。《祕書》說：日月爲易，象陰陽也。一曰从勿。凡易之屬皆从易。
易.eEn: The lizard, also called 蝘蜓 or 守宮. A pictograph. The Secret Writings explains: “日 and 月 make 易, depicting yin and yang.” Another explanation: it is formed from 勿. All characters in the 易 class are formed with 易.

象.e: 長鼻牙，南越大獸，三秊一乳，象耳牙四足之形。凡象之屬皆从象。
象.eEn: A large beast of the southern Yue region, with a long trunk and tusks, giving birth once every three years. Its form depicts the ears, tusks, and four legs. All characters in the 象 class are formed with 象.

豫.e: 象之大者。賈侍中說：不害於物。从象予聲。
豫.eEn: A large elephant. Palace Attendant Jia explains: “It does no harm to other creatures.” Formed from 象, with 予 indicating the pronunciation.

馬.e: 怒也。武也。象馬頭髦尾四足之形。凡馬之屬皆从馬。
馬.eEn: Fierce; martial. Its form depicts a horse's head, mane, tail, and four legs. All characters in the 馬 class are formed with 馬.

駒.e: 馬二歲曰駒，三歲曰駣。从馬句聲。
駒.eEn: A horse at two years old is called 駒; at three years old, 駣. Formed from 馬, with 句 indicating the pronunciation.

芻.eEn: To cut grass. It depicts the shape of grass wrapped into bundles.

騏.e: 馬青驪，文如博棊也。从馬其聲。
騏.eEn: A blue-black horse with markings like those of a gaming board. Formed from 馬, with 其 indicating the pronunciation.

驪.eEn: A horse of a deep black color. Formed from 馬, with 麗 indicating the pronunciation.

駽.e: 青驪馬。从馬肙聲。《詩》曰：“駜彼乘駽。”
駽.eEn: A blue-black horse. Formed from 馬, with 肙 indicating the pronunciation. The Odes says: “Sturdy are those four blue-black horses.”

騩.eEn: A horse of a light black color. Formed from 馬, with 鬼 indicating the pronunciation.

驑.e: 赤馬黑毛尾也。从馬畱聲。
驑.eEn: A red horse with a black mane and tail. Formed from 馬, with 畱 indicating the pronunciation.

騢.e: 馬赤白雜毛。从馬叚聲。謂色似鰕魚也。
騢.eEn: A horse with mixed red and white hair. Formed from 馬, with 叚 indicating the pronunciation. This means its coloring resembles that of a shrimp.

騅.eEn: A horse with mixed blue-gray and black hair. Formed from 馬, with 隹 indicating the pronunciation.

駱.e: 馬白色黑鬣尾也。从馬各聲。
駱.eEn: A white horse with a black mane and tail. Formed from 馬, with 各 indicating the pronunciation.

茭.e: 乾芻。从艸交聲。一曰牛蘄艸。
茭.eEn: Dried fodder. Formed from 艸, with 交 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation: the plant called 牛蘄.

駰.e: 馬陰白雜毛。黑。从馬因聲。《詩》曰：“有駰有騢。”
駰.eEn: A horse with a mixture of dusky-white hairs; dark in color. Formed from 馬, with 因 indicating the pronunciation. The 《詩》 says: “There are 駰 horses and 騢 horses.”

驄.e: 馬青白雜毛也。从馬悤聲。
驄.eEn: A horse with mixed blue-gray and white hairs. Formed from 馬, with 悤 indicating the pronunciation.

驈.e: 驪馬白胯也。从馬矞聲。《詩》曰：“有驈有騜。”
驈.eEn: A black horse with white flanks. Formed from 馬, with 矞 indicating the pronunciation. The 《詩》 says: “There are 驈 horses and 騜 horses.”

駹.e: 馬面顙皆白也。从馬尨聲。
駹.eEn: A horse whose face and forehead are both white. Formed from 馬, with 尨 indicating the pronunciation.

騧.eEn: A yellow horse with a black muzzle. Formed from 馬, with 咼 indicating the pronunciation.

驃.e: 黃馬發白色。一曰白髦尾也。从馬𤐫聲。
驃.eEn: A yellow horse showing white coloration. Another explanation: a horse with a white mane and tail. Formed from 馬, with 𤐫 indicating the pronunciation.

駓.eEn: A yellow horse with white hairs. Formed from 馬, with 丕 indicating the pronunciation.

馰.e: 馬白頟也。从馬，的省聲。一曰駿也。《易》曰：“爲的顙。”
馰.eEn: A horse with a white forehead. Formed from 馬, with an abbreviated form of 的 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation: an excellent horse. The 《易》 says: “It represents a horse with a white forehead.”

荹.eEn: Tangled grass. Formed from 艸, with 步 indicating the pronunciation.

駁.eEn: A horse whose coloring is not uniform. Formed from 馬, with 爻 indicating the pronunciation.

馵.e: 馬後左足白也。从馬，二其足。讀若注。
馵.eEn: A horse with a white left hind foot. Formed from 馬, with a mark on its foot. Pronounced like 注.

驔.e: 驪馬黃𦟝。从馬覃聲。讀若簟。
驔.eEn: A black horse with yellow hair along its back. Formed from 馬, with 覃 indicating the pronunciation. Pronounced like 簟.

驠.eEn: A horse with a white rump. Formed from 馬, with 燕 indicating the pronunciation.

騽.eEn: A horse with hairy shanks. Formed from 馬, with 習 indicating the pronunciation.

騛.e: 馬逸足也。从馬从飛。《司馬法》曰：“飛衞斯輿。”
騛.eEn: A fleet-footed horse. Formed from 馬 and 飛. The 《司馬法》 says: “Swiftly guard this chariot.”

驁.e: 駿馬。以壬申日死，乘馬忌之。从馬敖聲。
驁.eEn: An excellent horse. Such horses die on a 壬申 day; those who ride horses regard this as a taboo. Formed from 馬, with 敖 indicating the pronunciation.

驥.e: 千里馬也，孫陽所相者。从馬冀聲。天水有驥縣。
驥.eEn: A horse capable of traveling a thousand li, of the kind that Sun Yang identified by examining horses. Formed from 馬, with 冀 indicating the pronunciation. There is a Ji County in Tianshui.

駿.eEn: A horse of excellent natural quality. Formed from 馬, with 夋 indicating the pronunciation.

茹.eEn: To feed a horse. Formed from 艸, with 如 indicating the pronunciation.

驍.eEn: A fine horse. Formed from 馬, with 堯 indicating the pronunciation.

驕.e: 馬高六尺爲驕。从馬喬聲。《詩》曰：“我馬唯驕。”一曰野馬。
驕.eEn: A horse six chi tall is called 驕. Formed from 馬, with 喬 indicating the pronunciation. The 《詩》 says: “My horses are tall.” Another explanation: a wild horse.

騋.e: 馬七尺爲騋，八尺爲龍。从馬來聲。《詩》曰：“騋牝驪牡。”
騋.eEn: A horse seven chi tall is called 騋; one eight chi tall is called 龍. Formed from 馬, with 來 indicating the pronunciation. The 《詩》 says: “Tall mares and black stallions.”

驩.eEn: A name for a horse. Formed from 馬, with 雚 indicating the pronunciation.

驗.eEn: A name for a horse. Formed from 馬, with 僉 indicating the pronunciation.

馼.e: 馬赤鬣縞身，目若黃金，名曰𩢌。吉皇之乘，周文王時，犬戎獻之。从馬从文，文亦聲。《春秋傳》曰：“𩢌馬百駟。”畫馬也。西伯獻紂，以全其身。
馼.eEn: A horse with a red mane, a white body, and eyes like gold is called 𩢌. It was the mount of Ji Huang. In the time of King Wen of Zhou, the Quanrong presented one as tribute. Formed from 馬 and 文, with 文 also indicating the pronunciation. The 《春秋傳》 says: “One hundred teams of four 𩢌 horses.” These are patterned horses. The Earl of the West presented them to King Zhou to preserve his own life.

馶.eEn: A strong horse. Formed from 馬, with 支 indicating the pronunciation.

莝.eEn: Chopped fodder. Formed from 艸, with 坐 indicating the pronunciation.

駜.e: 馬飽也。从馬必聲。《詩》云：“有駜有駜。”
駜.eEn: A well-fed horse. Formed from 馬, with 必 indicating the pronunciation. The 《詩》 says: “Well-fed, well-fed are the horses.”

駫.e: 馬盛肥也。从馬光聲。《詩》曰：“四牡駫駫。”
駫.eEn: A robust, fat horse. Formed from 馬, with 光 indicating the pronunciation. The 《詩》 says: “The four stallions are robust and fat.”

騯.e: 馬盛也。从馬㫄聲。《詩》曰：“四牡𩤐𩤐。”
騯.eEn: A vigorous horse. Formed from 馬, with 㫄 indicating the pronunciation. The 《詩》 says: “The four stallions are vigorous.”

驤.eEn: A horse lowering and raising its head. Formed from 馬, with 襄 indicating the pronunciation.

驀.eEn: To mount a horse. Formed from 馬, with 莫 indicating the pronunciation.

騎.eEn: To sit astride a horse. Formed from 馬, with 奇 indicating the pronunciation.

駕.eEn: A horse placed in a yoke. Formed from 馬, with 加 indicating the pronunciation.

騑.eEn: An outside horse in a chariot team, also called 驂. Formed from 馬, with 非 indicating the pronunciation.

駢.eEn: To harness two horses together. Formed from 馬, with 并 indicating the pronunciation.

萎.eEn: To feed cattle. Formed from 艸, with 委 indicating the pronunciation.

驂.eEn: To harness three horses together. Formed from 馬, with 參 indicating the pronunciation.

駟.eEn: One chariot team of four horses. Formed from 馬, with 四 indicating the pronunciation.

駙.e: 副馬也。从馬付聲。一曰近也。一曰疾也。
駙.eEn: A spare horse. Formed from 馬, with 付 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation: near. Another explanation: swift.

騀.eEn: A horse shaking its head. Formed from 馬, with 我 indicating the pronunciation.

駊.eEn: Used in 駊騀, describing a horse shaking its head. Formed from 馬, with 皮 indicating the pronunciation.

篤.eEn: A horse moving slowly and haltingly. Formed from 馬, with 竹 indicating the pronunciation.

騤.e: 馬行威儀也。从馬癸聲。《詩》曰：“四牡騤騤。”
騤.eEn: A horse moving with dignified bearing. Formed from 馬, with 癸 indicating the pronunciation. The 《詩》 says: “The four stallions move with dignified bearing.”

蓛.e: 以榖萎馬，置莝中。从艸敇聲。
蓛.eEn: To feed a horse grain placed among chopped fodder. Formed from 艸, with 敇 indicating the pronunciation.

駸.e: 馬行疾也。从馬，㑴省聲。《詩》曰：“載驟𩤿𩤿。”
駸.eEn: A horse moving swiftly. Formed from 馬, with an abbreviated form of 㑴 indicating the pronunciation. The 《詩》 says: “Then they gallop, moving swiftly.”

馺.e: 馬行相及也。从馬从及。讀若《爾雅》“小山馺，大山峘”。
馺.eEn: Horses moving along and catching up with one another. Formed from 馬 and 及. Pronounced like 馺 in the 《爾雅》 passage: “A small hill is called 馺; a large hill is called 峘.”

馮.eEn: A horse moving swiftly. Formed from 馬, with 冫 indicating the pronunciation.

騃.eEn: A horse moving with a forceful bearing. Formed from 馬, with 矣 indicating the pronunciation.

驟.eEn: A horse moving at a rapid pace. Formed from 馬, with 聚 indicating the pronunciation.

颿.eEn: A horse moving at a rapid pace. Formed from 馬, with 風 indicating the pronunciation.

驅.eEn: A horse running swiftly. Formed from 馬, with 區 indicating the pronunciation.

馳.eEn: To drive a horse at full speed. Formed from 馬, with 也 indicating the pronunciation.

騖.eEn: To gallop about in disorder. Formed from 馬, with 敄 indicating the pronunciation.

騁.eEn: To gallop straight ahead. Formed from 馬, with 甹 indicating the pronunciation.

駾.e: 馬行疾來皃。从馬兌聲。《詩》曰：“昆夷駾矣。”
駾.eEn: The appearance of a horse coming swiftly. Formed from 馬, with 兌 indicating the pronunciation. The 《詩》 says: “The Kunyi fled at a gallop.”

駻.eEn: A horse charging forward. Formed from 馬, with 旱 indicating the pronunciation.

駧.eEn: To ride a horse swiftly straight away. Formed from 馬, with 同 indicating the pronunciation.

驚.eEn: A horse taking fright. Formed from 馬, with 敬 indicating the pronunciation.

駭.eEn: To be startled. Formed from 馬, with 亥 indicating the pronunciation.

蔟.eEn: A bedding of straw on which silkworms are arranged. Formed from 艸, with 族 indicating the pronunciation.

騫.eEn: A horse with its abdomen drawn tight. Formed from 馬, with an abbreviated form of 寒 indicating the pronunciation.

駐.eEn: A horse standing still. Formed from 馬, with 主 indicating the pronunciation.

馴.eEn: An obedient horse. Formed from 馬, with 川 indicating the pronunciation.

駗.eEn: A horse struggling under a heavy load. Formed from 馬, with 㐱 indicating the pronunciation.

驙.e: 駗驙也。从馬亶聲。《易》曰：“乘馬驙如。”
驙.eEn: Used in 駗驙, describing a horse struggling under a heavy load. Formed from 馬, with 亶 indicating the pronunciation. The 《易》 says: “The horses of the team strain under their burden.”

騺.eEn: The appearance of a horse weighed down. Formed from 馬, with 執 indicating the pronunciation.

驧.eEn: A horse arching its back. Formed from 馬, with 鞠 indicating the pronunciation.

騬.eEn: A castrated horse. Formed from 馬, with 乘 indicating the pronunciation.

騷.e: 擾也。一曰摩馬。从馬蚤聲。
騷.eEn: To disturb. Another explanation: to rub a horse. Formed from 馬, with 蚤 indicating the pronunciation.

禡.e: 師行所止，恐有慢其神，下而祀之曰禡。从示馬聲。《周禮》曰：“禡於所征之地。”
禡.eEn: When an army on the march halts, fearing that it may have slighted the local spirits, its members dismount and offer sacrifices to them; this is called 禡. Formed from 示, with 馬 indicating the pronunciation. The 《周禮》 says: “Perform the 禡 sacrifice in the territory being campaigned against.”

苣.eEn: Reeds bundled together for burning. Formed from 艸, with 巨 indicating the pronunciation.

馽.e: 絆馬也。从馬，囗其足。《春秋傳》曰：“韓厥執馽前。”讀若輒。
馽.eEn: To hobble a horse. Formed from 馬, with 囗 enclosing its feet. The 《春秋傳》 says: “Han Jue held the horse's hobble at the front.” Pronounced like 輒.

駘.eEn: A horse's bit coming loose. Formed from 馬, with 台 indicating the pronunciation.

駔.e: 牡馬也。从馬且聲。一曰馬蹲駔也。
駔.eEn: A stallion. Formed from 馬, with 且 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation: used in 蹲駔 to describe a horse.

騶.eEn: A stable attendant who handles horses. Formed from 馬, with 芻 indicating the pronunciation.

驛.eEn: Mounted couriers stationed along a route. Formed from 馬, with 睪 indicating the pronunciation.

馹.eEn: A relay courier service. Formed from 馬, with 日 indicating the pronunciation.

騰.e: 傳也。从馬朕聲。一曰騰，犗馬也。
騰.eEn: To convey by relay. Formed from 馬, with 朕 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation: 騰 means a castrated horse.

駉.e: 牧馬苑也。从馬冋聲。《詩》曰：“在駉之野。”
駉.eEn: An enclosure for pasturing horses. Formed from 馬, with 冋 indicating the pronunciation. The 《詩》 says: “In the fields where horses are pastured.”

駪.eEn: The appearance of a great many horses. Formed from 馬, with 先 indicating the pronunciation.

蕘.eEn: Firewood. Formed from 艸, with 堯 indicating the pronunciation.

駮.e: 獸，如馬，倨牙，食虎豹。从馬交聲。
駮.eEn: A beast resembling a horse, with projecting teeth, that eats tigers and leopards. Formed from 馬, with 交 indicating the pronunciation.

駃.e: 駃騠，馬父驘子也。从馬夬聲。
駃.eEn: A 駃騠: a mule offspring sired by a horse. Formed from 馬, with 夬 indicating the pronunciation.

騠.eEn: Used in 駃騠, a mule offspring sired by a horse. Formed from 馬, with 是 indicating the pronunciation.

驘.eEn: An animal with a donkey as its sire and a horse as its dam. Formed from 馬, with 𦝠 indicating the pronunciation.

驢.eEn: An animal resembling a horse, with long ears. Formed from 馬, with 盧 indicating the pronunciation.

驒.e: 驒騱，野馬也。从馬單聲。一曰青驪白鱗，文如鼉魚。
驒.eEn: A 驒騱, a wild horse. Formed from 馬, with 單 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation: a blue-black horse with white, scale-like markings, patterned like an alligator.

騱.eEn: The horse called 驒騱. Formed from 馬, with 奚 indicating the pronunciation.

騊.e: 騊駼，北野之良馬。从馬匋聲。
騊.eEn: The 騊駼, a fine horse of the northern wilds. Formed from 馬, with 匋 indicating the pronunciation.

駼.eEn: Used in 騊駼, a fine horse of the northern wilds. Formed from 馬, with 余 indicating the pronunciation.

薪.eEn: Firewood. Formed from 艸, with 新 indicating the pronunciation.

驫.eEn: A multitude of horses. Formed from three instances of 馬.

駥.eEn: A horse eight chi tall. Formed from 馬, with 戎 indicating the pronunciation.

騣.eEn: A horse's mane. Formed from 馬, with 㚇 indicating the pronunciation.

馱.e: 負物也。从馬大聲。此俗語也。
馱.eEn: To carry a load on the back. Formed from 馬, with 大 indicating the pronunciation. This is a colloquial expression.

薦.e: 獸之所食艸。从𢊁从艸。古者神人以𢊁遺黃帝。帝曰：“何食？何處？”曰：“食薦；夏處水澤，冬處松柏。”
薦.eEn: Grass eaten by beasts. Formed from 𢊁 and 艸. In ancient times, a divine being presented a 𢊁 beast to the Yellow Emperor. The emperor asked: “What does it eat? Where does it live?” The reply was: “It eats grass; in summer it lives in waters and marshes, and in winter among pines and cypresses.”

灋.e: 刑也。平之如水，从水；𢊁，所以觸不直者；去之，从去。
灋.eEn: Punishment. It makes things level, like water, and is therefore formed with 水. The 𢊁 beast is what butts those who are not upright; they are removed, and so the character is formed with 去.

蒸.eEn: The central stalk of hemp after it has been broken. Formed from 艸, with 烝 indicating the pronunciation.

鹿.e: 獸也。象頭角四足之形。鳥鹿足相似，从匕。凡鹿之屬皆从鹿。
鹿.eEn: A beast: the deer. It depicts the head, antlers, and four feet. Birds and deer have similar feet, so it incorporates 匕. All characters in the 鹿 class are formed with 鹿.

麚.e: 牡鹿。从鹿叚聲。以夏至解角。
麚.eEn: A male deer. Formed from 鹿, with 叚 indicating the pronunciation. It sheds its antlers at the summer solstice.

麟.eEn: A large female deer. Formed from 鹿, with 粦 indicating the pronunciation.

麛.eEn: A young deer. Formed from 鹿, with 弭 indicating the pronunciation.

麉.e: 鹿之絕有力者。从鹿幵聲。
麉.eEn: An exceptionally powerful deer. Formed from 鹿, with 幵 indicating the pronunciation.

麒.e: 仁獸也。麋身牛尾，一角。从鹿其聲。
麒.eEn: A benevolent beast. It has the body of a milu deer, the tail of an ox, and one horn. Formed from 鹿, with 其 indicating the pronunciation.

麐.eEn: A female 麒. Formed from 鹿, with 吝 indicating the pronunciation.

麋.e: 鹿屬。从鹿米聲。麋冬至解其角。
麋.eEn: A kind of deer. Formed from 鹿, with 米 indicating the pronunciation. The milu deer sheds its antlers at the winter solstice.

蕉.eEn: Raw hemp. Formed from 艸, with 焦 indicating the pronunciation.

麎.eEn: A female milu deer. Formed from 鹿, with 辰 indicating the pronunciation.

麇.eEn: A 麞 deer. Formed from 鹿, with an abbreviated 囷 indicating the pronunciation.

麞.eEn: A kind of milu deer. Formed from 鹿, with 章 indicating the pronunciation.

麔.eEn: A female milu deer. Formed from 鹿, with 咎 indicating the pronunciation.

麠.e: 大鹿也。牛尾一角。从鹿畺聲。
麠.eEn: A large deer. It has an ox's tail and one horn. Formed from 鹿, with 畺 indicating the pronunciation.

麃.eEn: A kind of 麠 deer. Formed from 鹿, with an abbreviated 㶾 indicating the pronunciation.

麈.eEn: A kind of milu deer. Formed from 鹿, with 主 indicating the pronunciation.

麑.eEn: The suanni, a beast. Formed from 鹿, with 兒 indicating the pronunciation.

麙.e: 山羊而大者，細角。从鹿咸聲。
麙.eEn: A large mountain goat with slender horns. Formed from 鹿, with 咸 indicating the pronunciation.

麢.eEn: A large sheep with slender horns. Formed from 鹿, with 霝 indicating the pronunciation.

麗.e: 旅行也。鹿之性，見食急則必旅行。从鹿丽聲。《禮》：麗皮納聘。蓋鹿皮也。
麗.eEn: To travel in a group. By nature, deer invariably travel in groups when they see food and are eager for it. Formed from 鹿, with 丽 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Rites says: “Paired hides are presented as betrothal gifts.” These were presumably deer hides.

麀.eEn: A female deer. Formed from 鹿 and an abbreviated 牝.

麤.e: 行超遠也。从三鹿。凡麤之屬皆从麤。
麤.eEn: To travel far beyond. Formed from three 鹿 characters. All characters in the 麤 class are formed with 麤.

毚.e: 狡兔也，兔之駿者。从㲋、兔。
毚.eEn: A cunning hare, one of the swiftest hares. Formed from 㲋 and 兔.

薶.eEn: To bury. Formed from 艸, with 貍 indicating the pronunciation.

兔.e: 獸名。象踞，後其尾形。兔頭與㲋頭同。凡兔之屬皆从兔。
兔.eEn: The name of a beast: the hare. It depicts a crouching animal, with its tail behind it. The head of 兔 is the same as the head of 㲋. All characters in the 兔 class are formed with 兔.

逸.e: 失也。从辵、兔。兔謾訑善逃也。
逸.eEn: To escape or be lost. Formed from 辵 and 兔. Hares are deceitful and adept at escaping.

冤.e: 屈也。从兔从冂。兔在冂下，不得走，益屈折也。
冤.eEn: To be bent or constrained. Formed from 兔 and 冂. A hare beneath 冂 cannot run away and becomes all the more bent and cramped.

婏.eEn: A young hare. 婏 also means swift. Formed from 女 and 兔.

萈.e: 山羊細角者。从兔足，𥄕聲。凡萈之屬皆从萈。讀若丸。寬字从此。
萈.eEn: A mountain goat with slender horns. Formed from the feet of 兔, with 𥄕 indicating the pronunciation. All characters in the 萈 class are formed with 萈. Read like 丸. The character 寬 is formed with this component.

犬.e: 狗之有縣蹏者也。象形。孔子曰：“視犬之字如畫狗也。”凡犬之屬皆从犬。
犬.eEn: A dog with hanging dewclaws. A pictograph. Confucius says: "Looking at the character 犬 is like looking at a drawing of a dog." All characters in the 犬 class are formed with 犬.

葠.eEn: Matting used in funerary rites. Formed from 艸, with 㑴 indicating the pronunciation.

狗.e: 孔子曰：“狗，叩也。叩气吠以守。”从犬句聲。
狗.eEn: Confucius said: “狗 means to knock or strike: it expels its breath in barking to keep guard.” Formed from 犬, with 句 indicating the pronunciation.

獀.e: 南趙名犬獿獀。从犬叜聲。
獀.eEn: In southern Zhao, dogs are called naosou (獿獀). Formed from 犬, with 叜 indicating the pronunciation.

尨.e: 犬之多毛者。从犬从彡。《詩》曰：“無使尨也吠。”
尨.eEn: A shaggy dog. Formed from 犬 and 彡. The Book of Odes says: “Do not let the shaggy dog bark.”

狡.e: 少狗也。从犬交聲。匃奴地有狡犬，巨口而黑身。
狡.eEn: A young dog. Formed from 犬, with 交 indicating the pronunciation. In the land of the Xiongnu there are jiao dogs, with enormous mouths and black bodies.

獪.eEn: Cunning and crafty. Formed from 犬, with 會 indicating the pronunciation.

猲.e: 短喙犬也。从犬曷聲。《詩》曰：“載獫猲獢。”《爾雅》曰：“短喙犬謂之猲獢。”
猲.eEn: A short-muzzled dog. Formed from 犬, with 曷 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Odes says: “With both long-muzzled and short-muzzled hounds.” The Erya says: “A short-muzzled dog is called a xie-xiao.”

獢.eEn: The xie-xiao, a short-muzzled dog. Formed from 犬, with 喬 indicating the pronunciation.

獫.e: 長喙犬。一曰黑犬黃頭。从犬僉聲。
獫.eEn: A long-muzzled dog. Another explanation: a black dog with a yellow head. Formed from 犬, with 僉 indicating the pronunciation.

猈.eEn: A short-legged dog. Formed from 犬, with 卑 indicating the pronunciation.

猗.eEn: A castrated dog. Formed from 犬, with 奇 indicating the pronunciation.

狊.eEn: The appearance of a dog looking. Formed from 犬 and 目.

默.e: 犬暫逐人也。从犬黑聲。讀若墨。
默.eEn: A dog suddenly chasing a person. Formed from 犬, with 黑 indicating the pronunciation. Read like 墨.

猝.e: 犬从艸暴出逐人也。从犬卒聲。
猝.eEn: A dog suddenly bursting out of the grass to chase a person. Formed from 犬, with 卒 indicating the pronunciation.

猩.eEn: Xing-xing: the sound of a dog barking. Formed from 犬, with 星 indicating the pronunciation.

猥.eEn: The sound of a dog barking. Formed from 犬, with 畏 indicating the pronunciation.

卉.eEn: A collective term for grasses and plants. Formed from 艸 and 屮.

獿.eEn: Unruly or troublesome, as in naonao (獿㺒). Formed from 犬 and 夒.

狦.eEn: A fierce, strong dog. Formed from 犬, with an abbreviated 𠛹 indicating the pronunciation.

狠.eEn: The sound of barking and fighting. Formed from 犬, with 艮 indicating the pronunciation.

狋.e: 犬怒皃。从犬示聲。一曰犬難得。代郡有狋氏縣。讀又若銀。
狋.eEn: The appearance of an angry dog. Formed from 犬, with 示 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation: a dog that is difficult to obtain. There is a Yishi County in Dai Commandery. It is also read like 銀.

禂.e: 禱牲馬祭也。从示周聲。《詩》曰：“旣禡旣禂。”
禂.eEn: A sacrifice in which prayers are offered for livestock and horses. Formed from 示, with 周 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Odes says: “The military sacrifice and the sacrifice for livestock have both been performed.”

艽.e: 逺荒也。从艸九聲。《詩》曰：“至于艽野。”
艽.eEn: Remote wilderness. Formed from 艸, with 九 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Odes says: “Reaching the distant wilds.”

獡.e: 犬獡獡不附人也。从犬舄聲。南楚謂相驚曰獡。讀若愬。
獡.eEn: A dog that is timid and will not approach people. Formed from 犬, with 舄 indicating the pronunciation. In southern Chu, frightening one another is called 獡. Read like 愬.

獷.e: 犬獷獷不可附也。从犬廣聲。漁陽有獷平縣。
獷.eEn: A dog that is fierce and cannot be approached. Formed from 犬, with 廣 indicating the pronunciation. There is a Guangping County in Yuyang.

狀.eEn: The form of a dog. Formed from 犬, with 爿 indicating the pronunciation.

獒.e: 犬如人心可使者。从犬敖聲。《春秋傳》曰：“公嗾夫獒。”
獒.eEn: A dog that understands a person's intentions and can be directed. Formed from 犬, with 敖 indicating the pronunciation. The Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals says: “The duke set that mastiff on him.”

獳.e: 怒犬皃。从犬需聲。讀若槈。
獳.eEn: The appearance of an angry dog. Formed from 犬, with 需 indicating the pronunciation. Read like 槈.

狧.e: 犬食也。从犬从舌。讀若比目魚鲽之鲽。
狧.eEn: A dog eating. Formed from 犬 and 舌. Read like the character 鲽 in the name of the flatfish.

狎.eEn: A dog that can be tamed. Formed from 犬, with 甲 indicating the pronunciation.

狃.eEn: A dog's nature being proud or unruly. Formed from 犬, with 丑 indicating the pronunciation.

犯.e: 侵也。从犬巳（段註改為㔾）聲。
犯.eEn: To encroach upon. Formed from 犬, with 巳 indicating the pronunciation; Duan's commentary changes 巳 to 㔾.

蒜.eEn: A pungent vegetable: garlic. Formed from 艸, with 祘 indicating the pronunciation.

猜.eEn: To resent and harm. Formed from 犬, with 青 indicating the pronunciation.

猛.eEn: A strong dog. Formed from 犬, with 孟 indicating the pronunciation.

犺.eEn: A strong dog. Formed from 犬, with 亢 indicating the pronunciation.

獜.e: 健也。从犬粦聲。《詩》曰：“盧獜獜。”
獜.eEn: Strong. Formed from 犬, with 粦 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Odes says: “The black hound is strong and vigorous.”

獧.e: 疾跳也。一曰急也。从犬瞏聲。
獧.eEn: To leap swiftly. Another explanation: urgent or hasty. Formed from 犬, with 瞏 indicating the pronunciation.

倏.eEn: To run. Formed from 犬, with 攸 indicating the pronunciation. Read like 叔.

狟.e: 犬行也。从犬亘聲。《周禮》曰：“尚狟狟。”
狟.eEn: A dog walking. Formed from 犬, with 亘 indicating the pronunciation. The Rites of Zhou says: “Esteem a steady, measured gait.”

犻.e: 過弗取也。从犬巿聲。讀若孛。
犻.eEn: To pass by without taking. Formed from 犬, with 巿 indicating the pronunciation. Read like 孛.

芥.eEn: A vegetable: mustard. Formed from 艸, with 介 indicating the pronunciation.

猌.e: 犬張齗怒也。从犬來聲。讀又若銀。
猌.eEn: A dog baring its gums in anger. Formed from 犬, with 來 indicating the pronunciation. It is also read like 銀.

犮.e: 走犬皃。从犬而丿之。曳其足，則剌犮也。
犮.eEn: The appearance of a running dog. Formed from 犬 with a 丿 stroke added. When its feet are dragged, it sprawls awkwardly.

戾.e: 曲也。从犬出戶下。戾者，身曲戾也。
戾.eEn: Bent or twisted. Formed from a 犬 emerging beneath a 戶. 戾 describes its body being bent and twisted.

獨.e: 犬相得而鬬也。从犬蜀聲。羊爲羣，犬爲獨也。一曰北嚻山有獨𤞞獸，如虎，白身，豕鬣，尾如馬。
獨.eEn: Dogs encountering one another and fighting. Formed from 犬, with 蜀 indicating the pronunciation. Sheep form flocks, whereas dogs remain solitary. Another explanation: on Mount Beixiao there is a beast called the duyu, resembling a tiger, with a white body, a pig's mane, and a tail like a horse's.

獵.eEn: To range out hunting and pursue game. Formed from 犬, with 巤 indicating the pronunciation.

獠.eEn: To hunt. Formed from 犬, with 尞 indicating the pronunciation.

狩.e: 犬田也。从犬守聲。《易》曰：“明夷于南狩。”
狩.eEn: To hunt with dogs. Formed from 犬, with 守 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Changes says: “Mingyi, on the southern hunt.”

臭.e: 禽走，臭而知其迹者，犬也。从犬从自。
臭.eEn: When game runs away, it is the dog that recognizes its tracks by smelling them. Formed from 犬 and 自.

蔥.eEn: A vegetable: the scallion. Formed from 艸, with 悤 indicating the pronunciation.

獲.eEn: What is caught in hunting. Formed from 犬, with 蒦 indicating the pronunciation.

獘.e: 頓仆也。从犬敝聲。《春秋傳》曰：“與犬，犬獘。”
獘.eEn: To collapse and fall down. Formed from 犬, with 敝 indicating the pronunciation. The Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals says: “He gave it to a dog, and the dog collapsed.”

獻.e: 宗廟犬名羹獻。犬肥者以獻之。从犬鬳聲。
獻.eEn: The ritual name for a dog offered in the ancestral temple is gengxian, “broth offering.” A fat dog is used for the offering. Formed from 犬, with 鬳 indicating the pronunciation.

獟.eEn: A fierce dog. Formed from 犬, with 堯 indicating the pronunciation.

狾.e: 狂犬也。从犬折聲。《春秋傳》曰：“狾犬入華臣氏之門。”
狾.eEn: A mad dog. Formed from 犬, with 折 indicating the pronunciation. The Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals says: “A mad dog entered the gate of Hua Chen's household.”

狂.eEn: A mad dog. Formed from 犬, with 㞷 indicating the pronunciation.

類.e: 種類相似，唯犬爲甚。从犬頪聲。
類.eEn: Members of the same kind resemble one another; this is especially true of dogs. Formed from 犬, with 頪 indicating the pronunciation.

狄.e: 赤狄，本犬種。狄之爲言淫辟也。从犬，亦省聲。
狄.eEn: The Red Di, originally of dog stock. The word 狄 conveys licentiousness and perversity. Formed from 犬, with an abbreviated 亦 indicating the pronunciation.

狻.e: 狻麑，如虦貓，食虎豹者。从犬夋聲。見《爾雅》。
狻.eEn: The suanni, resembling a striped cat and eating tigers and leopards. Formed from 犬, with 夋 indicating the pronunciation. It appears in the Erya.

蒮.e: 艸也。从艸隺聲。《詩》曰：“食鬱及蒮。”
蒮.eEn: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 隺 indicating the pronunciation. The Book of Odes says: “Eat the yu herb and the yu plant.”

玃.e: 母猴也。从犬矍聲。《爾雅》云：“玃父善顧。”攫持人也。
玃.eEn: A monkey. Formed from 犬, with 矍 indicating the pronunciation. The Erya says: “The juefu is adept at looking around.” It seizes and holds people.

猶.e: 玃屬。从犬酋聲。一曰隴西謂犬子爲猷。
猶.eEn: A kind of monkey. Formed from 犬, with 酋 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation: in Longxi, a puppy is called 猷.

狙.e: 玃屬。从犬且聲。一曰狙，犬也，暫齧人者。一曰犬不齧人也。
狙.eEn: A kind of monkey. Formed from 犬, with 且 indicating the pronunciation. Another explanation: 狙 is a dog that suddenly bites people. Yet another explanation: a dog that does not bite people.

猴.eEn: A monkey. Formed from 犬, with 矦 indicating the pronunciation.

狼.e: 似犬，銳頭，白頰，高前，廣後。从犬良聲。
狼.eEn: An animal resembling a dog, with a pointed head, white cheeks, high forequarters, and broad hindquarters. Formed from 犬, with 良 indicating the pronunciation.

狛.e: 如狼，善驅羊。从犬白聲。讀若蘗。甯嚴讀之若淺泊。
狛.eEn: An animal resembling a wolf, adept at driving sheep. Formed from 犬, with 白 indicating the pronunciation. Read like 蘗. Ning Yan reads it like 泊 in 淺泊.

獌.e: 狼屬。从犬曼聲。《爾雅》曰：“貙獌，似貍。”
獌.eEn: A kind of wolf. Formed from 犬, with 曼 indicating the pronunciation. The Erya says: “The chuman resembles a wildcat.”

狐.e: 䄏獸也。鬼所乘之。有三徳：其色中和，小前大後，死則丘首。从犬瓜聲。
狐.eEn: A supernatural beast: the fox. Ghosts ride upon it. It has three virtues: its coloration is balanced and harmonious; it is small in front and large behind; and when it dies, it turns its head toward its home mound. Formed from 犬, with 瓜 indicating the pronunciation.

獺.e: 如小狗也。水居食魚。从犬賴聲。
獺.eEn: An animal resembling a small dog. It lives in water and eats fish. Formed from 犬, with 賴 indicating the pronunciation.

蕇.eEn: The plant ting-li. Formed from 艸, with 單 indicating the pronunciation.

猵.eEn: A kind of otter. Formed from 犬, with 扁 indicating the pronunciation.

猋.eEn: The appearance of dogs running. Formed from three 犬 components.

狘.eEn: The appearance of a beast running. Formed from 犬, with 戉 indicating the pronunciation.

狷.eEn: Narrow-minded and impatient. Formed from 犬, with 肙 indicating the pronunciation.

猰.eEn: Ya-yu, the name of a beast. Formed from 犬, with 契 indicating the pronunciation.

獄.e: 确也。从㹜从言。二犬，所以守也。
獄.eEn: Firmness. Formed from 㹜 and 言. The two dogs are there to keep guard.

鼠.e: 穴蟲之緫名也。象形。凡鼠之屬皆从鼠。
鼠.eEn: A general name for burrowing creatures. A pictograph. All characters in the 鼠 class are formed with 鼠.

苟.eEn: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 句 indicating the pronunciation.

鼢.e: 地行鼠，伯勞所作也。一曰偃鼠。从鼠分聲。
鼢.eEn: A rat that moves underground, produced by the transformation of a shrike. Another explanation identifies it as the yan-rat. Formed from 鼠, with 分 indicating the pronunciation.

鼶.eEn: A rat. Formed from 鼠, with 虒 indicating the pronunciation.

鼫.e: 五技鼠也。能飛，不能過屋；能緣，不能窮木；能游，不能渡谷；能穴，不能掩身；能走，不能先人。从鼠石聲。
鼫.eEn: The rat of five skills. It can fly, but cannot get over a house; it can climb, but cannot reach the top of a tree; it can swim, but cannot cross a valley stream; it can burrow, but cannot conceal its body; it can run, but cannot outpace a person. Formed from 鼠, with 石 indicating the pronunciation.

鼨.eEn: A rat with leopard-like markings. Formed from 鼠, with 冬 indicating the pronunciation.
